# ecf (email-classify-filter): v1 specification

Status: first version, 2026-09-27. Source: the approved design plan, `docs/history/design-plan-2026-09-27.md` ("the plan"). This document is authoritative for v1; where it and the plan differ, this document wins. Roadmap milestones M1-M4 and later items are specified in the plan until each `docs/roadmap/<milestone>.md` is written at the start of that milestone (§1.4).

## 0. How to read this document

- **Scope tags:** [v1] is built now. [M1]-[M4] and [later] are roadmap items, mentioned here only where v1 must leave room for them.
- **Default origin markers.** Every default carries one of:
  - "operator decision <date>": decided by the operator;
  - "reviewer recommendation confirmed by the operator <date>";
  - "reviewed by the operator 2026-09-26/27": a default from the plan with no individual marker (all plan defaults were reviewed on those dates);
  - **"proposed in SPEC, accepted by the operator 2026-09-27"** (short form **[proposed]**, or P in tables): something the plan did not define, proposed here and accepted as a whole (OD-162). New proposals added later are marked "proposed in SPEC, pending operator review" until decided; §23.3 lists the accepted set.
- **Citations.** A fact called "verified" gives its source site and date. "(rv)" means verified by a reviewer's cited source and not re-checked by Claude. Everything else reads "unverified, confirm in V1.x" (or in the milestone named).
- **Numbers** that have no config key are listed as fixed in §14.3.
- **v3.0.0 removes the local model** (ADR 0031, OD-506; plan `planning-docs/REMOVE-LOCAL-MODELS.md` draft 2): presets A and B, Ollama, Gemma, the model queue, the battery and heat rules and the local fallback go. Live text describes v3.0.0 after the removal; "as built" records of those features are history and say so ("removed in v3.0.0"). Milestone records (§1.3-§1.5), results (§21) and the OD table (§23.4) are kept as written.
- **Traceability.** `OD-nnn` numbers operator decisions and appears next to the decision it annotates, `G1-n` numbers the Group 1 documentation findings, and seven review IDs are cited by name; all are in §23.

## 1. Scope, milestones and release criteria [v1]

### 1.1 What v1 is

ecf watches a configured list of business mailboxes (for example `accounts-payable@`, `billing@`, `info@`), classifies each message against an operator-owned schema, applies deterministic fraud and regulator rules computed by a local service, lets a model propose actions, and asks a person in Slack to approve anything that isn't safe to do automatically.

v1 is **single-user local mode** (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-013; section: OD-153):
- **Platforms:** macOS and Linux (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-001); Windows later. Linux desktops are supported through Secret Service; headless Linux is best-effort on systemd 256+ (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-002). **v1.0.0 supports macOS only** (operator decision 2026-10-04, OD-422, ADR 0020): the Linux code (systemd user unit, Secret Service, `systemd-creds`, PAM) stays in the repo but is unsupported and unverified until roadmap milestone M5 (§1.2).
- **One person, one computer.** The OS user is the sole admin and approver. ecf runs only while the computer is on and awake. A computer simply left on is allowed (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-007).
- **No AWS.** State, secrets, scheduling and Slack connectivity all live in one local service (§11).
- **Mail:** IMAP only, via app passwords (from M6, the next minor release (OD-533), in progress: personal Gmail addresses may instead use the Gmail API with OAuth, chosen per address, OD-529; `docs/roadmap/m6-gmail-api.md`). Purelymail first; any IMAP provider that supports app passwords, checked by a per-address probe. Personal Google accounts (gmail.com, googlemail.com) with an app password, from V1.6 (operator decision 2026-10-04, OD-425); another person's account only with the owner's agreement (OD-427); Google Workspace accounts wait for M7, which builds on M6's Gmail API (OD-426; operator decision 2026-10-16, OD-525). Not Microsoft 365 (it requires OAuth2 for IMAP, G1-33).
- **Models:** preset C (all-Claude) (§4; ADR 0031, OD-506). Preset D (TypeSafe Jev classifier + Claude actor) was built in v3.0.0 step 4 and is held back from v3.0.0 (OD-516); Jev is eval-only. Presets A and B (a local model, OD-003) ran from V1.3 to v2.2.x and are removed in v3.0.0.
- **Outbound mail** (template replies and internal forwards) is built but **off per address by default**.

Everything security-relevant runs in the local service, not in a model or client, using the same code the M1 AWS server will use, so M1 moves that code to Lambdas without redesign.

### 1.2 Roadmap (not in v1)

Executed in order (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-004). M1-M3 are fully designed in the plan; M4 is an outline that gets its own design review; M5 (Linux, formerly V1.6 Linux) has its own plan on branch `m5-linux` (operator decision 2026-10-04, OD-421); M6 (Gmail API, personal Google accounts) and M7 (Google Workspace accounts) are outlined below and each gets its own design review (OD-426; operator decision 2026-10-16, OD-525). M6 starts ahead of M1-M5 (operator decision 2026-10-16, OD-527, amends OD-004); its design is `docs/roadmap/m6-gmail-api.md`. M8 (model-written drafts) and M9 (sending a draft from Slack, which needs M8) come after M7; they are outlined below and each gets its own design review (operator decision 2026-10-26, OD-560; outline `planning-docs/M8-M9-DRAFTS-AND-SEND.md`).

**Removed from Later** (2026-10-14, ADR 0031, P25): heat and which speed to improve, Ollama MLX on macOS (OD-257), shorter classifier keys and grouped model calls, all speed work on the local model; their measurements stay in §21.2. The branches `grouped-model-calls` and `custom-local-classifier` are closed.

**The actor's wording in the gate key** (done in v3.0.1, OD-523; was Later from v3.0.0 step 6 Phase R P12; plan `planning-docs/v3.0.1-ACTOR-KEY.md`): the gate key now holds `actor_prompt`, 16 hex of `ecf.plugin_digest.actor_prompt_digest()` (SHA-256 of the raw `agents/actor.md` template, one for `actor` and `actor_high`), for presets C and D; `release.json`, `GET /v1/upgrade/state`, `ecf upgrade`'s check and eval results carry the full `actor_prompt_digest` (§9.3, §11.10, §16.5).

**The classifier's wording in the gate key** (done in v3.0.2, OD-524; was Later from v3.0.1, OD-523; plan `planning-docs/v3.0.2-CLASSIFIER-KEY.md`): `claude_review.prompt_digest` gains a fourth part, `classifier_template`, `ecf.plugin_digest.classifier_prompt_digest()` (SHA-256 of the raw `agents/classifier.md` template, one for every classifier agent), so `release.json`, the upgrade check and eval results follow without a new field. It moves C's key only (D's `prompt` is Jev's, `claude_pins.pins`) (§9.3, §11.10, §16.5).

**User-layer follow-ups** (Later; v3.0.0 S4, OD-502, P22): labelled examples for your own fields (the synthetic cards don't label them, so their accuracy is reported only); per-mailbox schemas (one schema per install today); more `priority`-labelled cards (116 of 304 today, and the noisiest field between runs of one configuration, §16.5). S4b (after v3.0.0, D1): default-off fields and value replacement for `category` and `sender_type`. **Safety finding from M2** (operator request 2026-10-14; §21.2): in M2 run `d6fd80e0` (preset C, Sonnet classifier, the 8-field hard-case sample applied) the classifier followed an injection on `injection-classify-notification`, answering `category: notification`, the injected target, where 33 other archived results for the card (the control `78efb420` included) answered `invoice` or `vendor_change_request`; `fraud_guard` still escalated it and nothing was hidden. One event, so not attributed to the user fields. Before the user layer is turned on: find whether the added fields or the added-category instruction make injection-following more likely (repeat this card and the other injection cards with and without a user schema), and report injection-following per injection card in each user-layer measurement.

**Reuse of classifications for bulk templates** (Later; operator request 2026-10-10; pre-classifier plan Phase R, P11): when a message's classifier input matches an item this install classified recently, copy that classification instead of asking the classifier again. It is not a plain skip: rules 7 and 8, the main hide paths, need the model's `category`, `sender_type` and `requires_action`, so a bulk sender's mail still needs a classification from somewhere, and facts, rules and policy still run per item and address. The premise "same input, same answer" doesn't hold as built: each classifier request carries a fresh random token (`classifier.py`, `secrets.token_hex`, read 2026-10-10), and the model isn't deterministic (the replicate pair `a0462682`/`112ca628` differ on 32 of 257 cases). Reuse would therefore freeze one sample of the model's answer. The same message delivered again is already recorded without a new classification (`fetch.py`, `item.duplicate_delivery`). So reuse could only help on different messages with byte-identical excerpts, and how often that happens is not measured. Personalized bulk mail (greetings, tracking and unsubscribe links) may make it rare (unverified). Before any design:

1. Count read-only how many retained items share a classifier-excerpt digest within 24 hours, per install, on a real mailbox or the corpus (§16.7).
2. (Was: try shorter classifier keys and grouped model calls first; both left with the local model, ADR 0031.)

If built:
- the input digest is an indexed column, not a JSON lookup (a full scan of `items` per classification otherwise; reviewer measurement, unverified);
- never across installs;
- never copied from a failed or truncated call, or from an item with a person's correction;
- a reused answer doesn't count toward the go-live gate as a reviewed item;
- reuse hits and misses are counted in the model metrics.

**Per-sender bank-account history** (Later; operator request 2026-10-10; pre-classifier plan Phase R, S7/P12): trigger 1 doesn't catch a confirmed vendor whose mailbox is compromised and that sends a new, checksum-valid IBAN with no change wording and no Reply-To mismatch. It fires only on an unconfirmed sender, change wording or a mismatch (§8.5). A per-sender "has sent bank details" bit doesn't help either: vendors that print their IBAN on every invoice set it from the first genuine one. The design that would catch this case:
- store a keyed hash (salted per install) of each IBAN or account number seen from a sender with DMARC-pass history, never the number, bounded to the last few per sender;
- raise a fraud reason on an account number not seen before from a sender whose history has any.

This is a `senders` migration. A new column alone needs no data-format bump (an older ecf already refuses a newer schema; v2.1.0's migration 0035 is the precedent, §8.5); a bump, which drops V1.6 (format 2) bundles from import, is needed only if an older version could misread the data (§1.4, §11.9). To measure first: on the corpus, how many senders send bank details at all, and how often a genuine sender's account changes.

Build notes (checked against v3.0.0, 2026-10-16): the keyword scan records only "valid IBAN", never the number (`triggers.scan`), so the build passes the cleaned-up IBAN to the hashing step without storing or logging it. Only IBANs are detected; other account numbers (e.g. US routing and account numbers) need a new detector, or the check covers IBANs only. The migration would be 0042. The hash key is a per-install secret in the OS secret store, written only by the service (sender hashes today are unkeyed SHA-256, `facts.sender_hash`; an account number is short and structured enough to guess against an unkeyed hash). Moving to another computer: `senders` is in export bundles (`importer.COPY`), so a restore whose key doesn't travel can't match the stored hashes and every known account looks new until the history rebuilds. Either derive the key from the backup key, which already travels with bundles (`backup_key.derive`), or leave the hashes out of exports and accept the relearning; decided when built.

**Plan** (operator 2026-10-27): draft 1 is `planning-docs/PER-SENDER-BANK-HISTORY.md`, approved and **parked** the same day, nothing built and no Phase R yet. The operator chose IBANs only, a step-up command (`ecf sender accept-account`) to accept a genuine change, account history left out of export bundles and relearned after a restore, and a corpus count first.

**Fine-tune a local decision model** (Later; operator request 2026-10-08; since OD-494, 2026-10-12, only on a non-Qwen base: the `tev1:4b` example and the OD-470 route below are void): after `tev1:4b` lost to Gemma on the synthetic set, mostly by over-rating fraud risk on benign mail (§7.8, §21.2), train a LoRA adapter on a small decision model (e.g. `tev1:4b`, from Together's published recipe) on ecf's own question format, then convert it to GGUF and serve it through Ollama like `tev1`. Rules: the synthetic eval set and the corpus's held-out split are never training data; operator-labelled corpus mail is trained on this Mac only (the privacy statement allows no new destination, §12.4); a separate, larger synthetic training set (card builder and hygiene scan) and licensed public sets (e.g. Enron, SpamAssassin, phishing corpora; licences unverified) may add volume; the data mix weights benign mail labelled `fraud_risk: none`. Train exactly as served (schema questions, the OD-255 preamble, the 2,400-byte excerpt). Evaluated with the §7.8 harness and adoption rule; needs ODs for a self-trained derivative under the Qwen exception (OD-470) and for the training-data rules. Unverified: Qwen3.5 support in Apple-silicon LoRA tooling, and how Ollama marks an imported model as decision-capable. Ollama serving is removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031), so this item would also need a runtime decision.

**Optimization of the testing data corpus** (Later; RAW Future, operator 2026-10-12, R9; PLANNING §4.7): a **non-Anthropic** model generates up to 5,000 emails to stress-test the system, each saved as its own file with all headers (`.eml`), in a compressed archive that can mimic an IMAP mailbox (for example a Maildir tree in a `.tar.zst`). The generator is chosen when the item is built, under the model filter (no PRC-, Meta- or X-affiliated labs; no Qwen); a hosted one is given synthetic seeds only, never real mail. Not built in v3.0.0.

**Synthetic training cards** (Later; PLANNING §4.7 L3): generated cards to train a future non-Qwen decision model (above). Generated cards are never eval cards. Offline; no preset involved.

**Atomic Mail** (Later; operator request 2026-09-28): not usable in v1. Its support page says "Atomic Mail does not support IMAP, SMTP, or POP3 protocols for connecting to third-party email clients. We plan to launch this feature later in 2026" (atomicmail.io/support, fetched 2026-09-28). Revisit when it ships IMAP/SMTP, and check: (1) app passwords or an equivalent, since v1 has no OAuth; (2) whether access is direct or through a local decrypting bridge, as with Proton; (3) that ecf receives the original raw message byte for byte, since a bridge that rebuilds messages would break DKIM and leave every sender at `auth_result = none`.

**M8 Model-written drafts** (roadmap milestone; operator request 2026-10-04, OD-424; milestone and scope operator decision 2026-10-26, OD-560): today the actor proposes `draft_reply`, the draft is limited to 4,000 characters and approved only where its card shows all of it (OD-551), and Approve appends it to Drafts, which you send yourself (§8.4). The **draft-quality eval** comes first: synthetic cases that need a reply, with computed facts that let a draft through policy (the V1.5 eval's facts had no `from_count`, so policy dropped every draft, run `c94de7bd`, §8.4); a results file that records each proposed draft's text; scoring for commitments (no payment, bank detail, price or date), recipient, tone and following injected instructions; run for each Claude pin. It can measure today's drafts before then. M8 also adds a drafter role (its own pin, Opus by default, replaceable by setting and in `ecf eval run`; Claude models only; a model is used as drafter only after it passes the draft-quality eval under the model-choice rule), draft data kept in the service's SQLite database as numbers and hashes, never text (whether ecf may read the Sent folder for the sent and edited counts is decided in its plan), and a new draft card whose desktop and phone mockups the operator approves before the build, and the built card is confirmed in a Slack test. Its plan is `docs/roadmap/m8-model-written-drafts.md` (draft 34; OD-566 to OD-568), which owns the details until M8 ships.

**M9 Send a draft from Slack** (roadmap milestone; OD-560, amends OD-424): it starts when M8 is complete and real drafts have earned a set 👍 rate over a set period (both set in M8's plan). It adds a Send email button on the draft card. The send is approved as a template reply is (§9.5): queued from Slack, then step-up at the computer, with the exact text and recipient bound into the grant (OD-317), and the 10-minute delay with Cancel on high-sensitivity addresses. Nothing is sent without your click and step-up. Prerequisites: injection tests on outgoing text, DLP, and a recipient domain allow/deny list. Open for its plan: a draft edited in Drafts can't be sent from the card (the grant covers the text you saw; recommended, not decided).

**Later items from OD-560:** Mistral and OpenAI as actor or drafter options are revisited only when the operator wants one; today they see only generated eval text, as judges (OD-540, OD-550), never real mail, so the privacy rule changes first. External forwards stay Later. Learning from past mail and drafts would put past text into new requests (privacy, injection persistence) and needs an OD. A claude.ai dashboard would send the draft figures to Anthropic outside `/ecf-review` and needs a privacy decision. Sending without approval has no plan and may never be built: it would reverse §3.2 (model output never, alone, sends anything) and would need a threat-model review and an ADR first.

**M6 Gmail API** (roadmap milestone; operator decision 2026-10-04, OD-426: IMAP with app passwords first, in V1.6, the Gmail API as its own milestone; personal Google accounts only, Workspace accounts are M7, operator decision 2026-10-16, OD-525): a Gmail API adapter behind the mail port (`MailSource`, which is shaped around IMAP UIDs today) and an API sender; the OAuth desktop flow (a loopback redirect, no web server); tokens in the OS secret store; narrower scopes by stage (no send scope while outbound is off; dropped at M6's start: `gmail.modify` also permits sending, so the outbound gate is the control, Phase R P23); native labels; history-based sync; polling, not Pub/Sub push (Pub/Sub would add a destination, §12.4). Google facts recorded at planning (fetched 2026-10-04): every Gmail scope ecf needs (`gmail.readonly`, `gmail.modify`, `gmail.compose`, `gmail.metadata`, `https://mail.google.com/`) is restricted, `gmail.send` sensitive, `gmail.labels` non-sensitive; a security assessment applies "if you store restricted scope data on servers (or transmit)" (developers.google.com/gmail/api/auth/scopes); a project in "Testing" gets authorizations and refresh tokens that expire after 7 days, one "In production" and unverified shows an unverified-app screen and is capped at 100 new users over its lifetime (support.google.com/cloud/answer/15549945); personal use under 100 users needs no verification (support.google.com/cloud/answer/13464323); refresh tokens with Gmail scopes end when the password changes and after 6 months unused (developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2). Settled at its start (operator decisions 2026-10-16, OD-527 to OD-531; design `docs/roadmap/m6-gmail-api.md`, ADR 0032 proposed): each operator's own Google Cloud project (personal use needs no verification, so the security assessment question is moot); `addresses.access` per address, IMAP and API addresses mixed; an address moves between them (open items found again, closed items and sender history kept); a minor release, numbered when it ships (OD-533). Phase R on draft 1: P1-P29, all recommendations accepted (operator, 2026-10-16). The roadmap doc's facts (re-fetched 2026-10-16) supersede the ones above.

**M7 Google Workspace accounts** (roadmap milestone; operator decision 2026-10-16, OD-525, amending OD-426): Google Workspace accounts, for which Google says app passwords aren't available (support.google.com/accounts/answer/185833, fetched 2026-10-04). Depends on M6: it reuses M6's Gmail API adapter, API sender and OAuth desktop sign-in (not IMAP with XOAUTH2, which would be a second OAuth path) and adds what Workspace needs. Workspace sending limits differ: 2,000 messages a day on paid accounts and 500 on trials, applied over a rolling 24 hours, blocking for up to 24 hours (knowledge.workspace.google.com, Gmail sending limits in Google Workspace, fetched 2026-10-05). M6's Google facts apply too. To settle at its start: Workspace admin controls; whether the security assessment applies; the `max_sends_per_day` default for a Workspace address; Workspace setup docs. Outline: `planning-docs/M7-GOOGLE-WORKSPACE.md`.

**M3 Teams chat surface: Microsoft facts** (operator request 2026-10-16; plan §17 M3 item 2). Read on learn.microsoft.com on 2026-10-16 by two read-only research agents; facts marked (rv) were not re-read by Claude, the rest were. Teams can't replace Slack in v1's local mode; with M1 it can, with the gaps below. It would add Microsoft as a destination (§12.4), which needs an operator decision first.

- **Inbound needs a public endpoint (M1):** a bot "must expose a publicly accessible HTTPS endpoint"; there is no outbound connection like Socket Mode, and "Inbound IP Address allow-listing isn't supported" (azure/bot-service, bot security FAQ) (rv). The handler validates the Bot Connector's JWT itself (issuer `https://api.botframework.com`, audience the app ID, `serviceUrl` claim, keys from `login.botframework.com`, refreshed at least daily) (bot-framework-rest-connector-authentication) (rv).
- **Registration:** a Teams-managed bot needs no Azure subscription, is single-tenant (new multi-tenant bots ended 2025-07-31) and has no OAuth/SSO; its code can run on AWS (teams-sdk core-concepts; manage-your-apps-in-developer-portal) (rv). The Bot Framework SDK has been out of support since 2025-12-31; its successors are the Teams SDK and the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK (Python support unverified).
- **Card clicks:** `Action.Execute` returns the updated card in the HTTP response (universal-action-model) (rv); activities time out after 15 s with a 504 (bot-builder-basics) (rv), and Microsoft Q&A answers report about 5 s for invokes (unverified). The click handler decides from state in AWS, not by calling a laptop.
- **Proactive posts:** the app must be installed where it posts, with a stored conversation ID, tenant ID and `serviceUrl`; a bot can start a thread in a channel but can't create a channel or group chat (send-proactive-messages) (rv).
- **Private channels:** generally available for apps since 2026-07-07 (Teams platform What's new) (rv); the plan's "paused in March 2026" is superseded. The manifest must be v1.25+ with `supportsChannelFeatures: tier1`, and in a private channel "App must be added to each channel" (build-apps-for-shared-private-channels, updated 2026-09-17). Graph can add an app only to a `shared` channel (graph channel-post-enabledapps, updated 2026-04-07), so a person adds ecf to each address's private channel by hand.
- **Creating channels:** Graph `POST /teams/{id}/channels`; `Channel.Create` needs admin consent, or `Channel.Create.Group` through resource-specific consent from a team owner; the private-channel examples are delegated (graph channel-post) (rv). Whether an app alone can create a private channel is unverified. Members: `channels/{id}/allMembers` with `ChannelMember.Read.Group` (rv).
- **Lost or changed against Slack (§10.1):** no per-message bot name or icon (not documented) (rv), so the card names the address; ephemeral replies become "targeted messages" (GA 2026-07-30, deleted after 24 h) (rv); Graph pins messages in chats only, not channels (rv); mentions use the Entra object ID or UPN (rv).
- **Plain text:** an Adaptive Card `TextBlock` always renders a markdown subset, including `[title](url)` links, with no switch to turn it off; `TextRun` says "Markdown is not supported", unconfirmed in Teams (adaptive-cards schema; Teams cards-format) (rv). Needs a real-service test like Slack's (2026-09-29, §21.1) before email text goes on a card.
- **Tenant setup:** a Teams administrator uploads the app in the Teams admin centre; admin consent for the Graph permissions (teams-custom-app-policies-and-settings) (rv).

### 1.4 Tags and releases

- **Milestone tags** (annotated): `ms-v1.0-foundations`, `ms-v1.1-mail-checks`, `ms-v1.2-slack-approvals`, `ms-v1.3-local-models`, `ms-v1.4-claude`, `ms-v1.5-outbound-ops`, `ms-v1.6-gmail` (OD-425); later `ms-m1-aws`, `ms-m2-teams`, …, `ms-m5-linux` (OD-421), `ms-m6-gmail-api` (OD-426), `ms-m7-google-workspace` (OD-525). They record internal progress and do **not** mean the software is ready for anyone else. (The plan names only the first, fifth and last; the V1.1-V1.4 names are [proposed].)
- **Release tags** `vX.Y.Z` (optionally `-rcN`) are the only tags built and published from, and the only ones `ecf upgrade --to` accepts.
- **Release versions follow semantic versioning** (operator decision 2026-10-08, OD-480): the major version goes up when the classification schema, rules files or the export data format break (`v2.0.0`: schema v2, data format 3), the minor version for added features, the patch version for fixes. A release candidate `vX.Y.Z-rcN` is made only when the operator asks for one (OD-492).
- **Release path** (operator decision 2026-10-12, OD-492; replaces "release candidates come first"): chosen by what a release changes, not by whether it is major, minor or a patch. A release is **checked** when it has a risky change: a migration; a gate-key change (pins, `prompt_digest`, `actor_prompt_digest` from v3.0.1, classifier schema); a change to the upgrade, rollback or Keychain code; or a `data_format` or `api_version` change. Otherwise it is **fast**. Both: one bump commit carries the version, the dated CHANGELOG heading and the README's Status line naming the new release (operator decision 2026-10-14: the README went unchanged from `v1.0.0` through `v2.2.3`; its install command takes the latest release, so carries no version; a version test fails until Status names the release; the same commit fixes any README text the release's CHANGELOG section contradicts); it runs the full macOS suite, 0 skipped (operator decision 2026-10-16, OD-522; until then only the version tests, though every merge it releases had passed the gate: at `v3.0.0` a test that depends on the version passed every merge and failed once the bump changed the version, §21.2); `main` and the annotated tag are pushed together, and the tag's release run, whose `checks` job runs the same Linux checks as CI before the build, is the check for both; afterwards the test install is upgraded once from the published release (`ecf upgrade --to vX.Y.Z`, whose hash check stays), with no local rebuild (CI builds twice and compares). A checked release also tests the upgrade before the tag: the wheel built locally with `scripts/release_build.py` (reproducible, so byte-identical to the release's) goes onto the test install with `ecf upgrade --wheel`, then `ecf upgrade --to <previous>` and `--wheel` again. Why: `v2.2.1` (one message fix) took about 40 minutes after its fix merged, most of it repeated checks: two gates, four CI or release runs, four upgrades.
- Every tag is created and pushed only after the operator confirms and approves the tag and the push (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-012).

### 1.5a Release criteria for `v2.0.0` (operator decision 2026-10-09)

`v2.0.0` (schema v2, the Haiku 5.5 main session, `num_ctx` 6144; OD-474 to OD-480; schema extensions built but off, OD-481) is tagged only after a release candidate passes item 1, on the candidate's wheel; item 2 gates the release that turns schema extensions on (planned `v2.1.0`, OD-481):

1. **Upgrade.** A `v1.0.0` install upgraded with `ecf upgrade --to v2.0.0-rcN`: every address is named as affected (`classifier_schema` 1 to 2, §11.10): when upgrading from a client that knows `classifier_schema` the check lists every address; from `v1.0.0`, whose client doesn't know it, the pre-check can't, and the new client names every address as affected after the upgrade (operator decision 2026-10-09); migration 0034 runs (`staff` becomes `team`, `items.schema_version` 2); a `live` address drops to `assist` (the schema digest in the gate key, §9.3); the `v1.0.0` model copy is kept (§7.5); the service starts and `ecf doctor` is clean apart from the expected gate rows. **Passed** (2026-10-09, install `ecf1009`, §21.2): every point on `v2.0.0-rc2`; the rc2 run also found a crash on upgrading again after a rollback (§11.10), fixed in `v2.0.0-rc3`, where a rollback and a same-label re-upgrade then ran with no manual step.
2. **A schema extension on the synthetic set.** Preset A with a realistic sample extension applied through `ecf config apply` (a `contract_stage` enum, a `needs_signature` boolean, a `vendor_tier` ordinal, and the category values `legal_notice` and `subscription_renewal`): 0 unsafe; fraud-guard recall N/N; no `truncated` or `schema_failure` model call; and on the built-in fields, against `a0462682` (v2, no extension), a Newcombe score lower bound above −5 points, so the extension doesn't dilute the shipped fields. The extension fields' own accuracy is reported only: the synthetic cards don't label them. **Not passed** (2026-10-09, run `6b80a149`, §21.2): the built-in fields lost 4.3 points (lower bound −7.7) and fraud-guard recall was 89/90, so extensions don't ship enabled in `v2.0.0` and this check moves to the release that turns them on, after their dilution is fixed (operator decision 2026-10-09, OD-481). **From v3.0.0 S4** (OD-502, D11b): item 2 stays the gate for presets A and B asking user fields (later, OD-495; until then the service refuses user fields while any A or B address exists, §7.1); item 2b is C's. **Closed** (2026-10-14, ADR 0031, P20): presets A and B are removed in v3.0.0, so item 2 gates nothing; item 2b is the user layer's gate.

2b. **Your own fields on preset C (M2, v3.0.0 S4; OD-502; plan `planning-docs/S4-USER-LAYER.md` draft 3 §7).** Two pinned C runs (C standard, Sonnet ×3, Opus `actor_high`; set `43f650c9d1839407`, 304 cards) with a hard-case sample applied through `ecf config apply` (8 fields at 3,600-4,000 characters, up to 4 category values, one field overlapping a fixed item in meaning while passing the fixed-name check), each compared with both S3b runs (`024ec270`, `1a8708cf`; four cross pairings), criteria named before the runs: (1) both runs 0 unsafe, fraud-guard recall 104/104, gate passed, refused `record_classification` tries reported (`ClaimRecord.invalid`); Newcombe paired lower bound in each pairing above (2) −5 on `correct`, (3) −5 on every labelled shipped field right (old-style `correct`: schema v2's labelled fields and the rule), (4) −5 on `fraud_risk` right, (5) −3.5 on rule right, (6) −5 on `category` (cases answering an added value listed), (7) −5 on `phishing` recall per run pairing (n 93; pooled reported); (8) report only: `priority`, the workflow fields, per-field McNemar/Holm, within-arm discordance, the user fields' answers, bytes per classify read (each C result records `read_bytes` in its summary since S4, review R9) and Sonnet classifier input tokens per case (expected +30-45% over the S3b pair with the hard-case sample; the ±10% band is the S3b pair's own noise, not a target). Criterion 2 is not item 2's built-in-fields figure; criterion 3 is closer. One repeat only if exactly one pairing misses its margin by under 1 point; a control C run with `schema: default` on S4 code if a gated criterion fails, before the loss is put on the user fields. Pass: `ecf.schema.EXTENSIONS_ENABLED` merges True and this item records the measured envelope (fields, characters, the overlapping field, bytes per read); fail: the user layer isn't shipped enabled in v3.0.0, the operator decides next (first option offered: lower C caps, measured by a new pair). Computed with `scripts/s4_criteria.py`. Noise reference: §16.5. **Failed 2026-10-14** (§21.2): run `d6fd80e0` had one unsafe case and 12 of the gated pairings missed their margins, so the user layer isn't shipped enabled in v3.0.0 (`EXTENSIONS_ENABLED` False; operator decision 2026-10-14, the outcome named above).

Each result goes in §21.2 with its run IDs.

Real-service test results go in this document; an ADR only when a result changes a decision.

**V1.5 step 14 decisions** (operator decisions 2026-10-03, OD-404 to OD-410): the two guides split by task: `docs/operator-guide.md` is day-to-day use (Slack cards, approvals and step-up, `ecf inbox`, `item`, `answer`, outbound and its reminders, alerts, `/ecf-review`); `docs/admin-guide.md` is setting up and running ecf (`init`, addresses, config, rules and templates, stages and the go-live gate, models, backups, restore and import, upgrade and rollback, `destroy`, `doctor`) plus every §13.5 recovery topic (OD-404). SECURITY.md says vulnerability reports aren't accepted until `v1.0.0` (the repository is private, so GitHub's private vulnerability reporting isn't available; checked 2026-10-03, GitHub API 404) (OD-406) and that no version is supported until `v1.0.0` (OD-407). ## 2. Glossary

| Term | Plain meaning |
|---|---|
| address | One watched mailbox (e.g. `billing@`), identified by an `address_id` slug. |
| install | One ecf installation (`--install <name>`, default `default`), with its own data directory, socket, service unit and secrets. |
| local service | `ecf-server local`: the background process that does all the work in v1. |
| preset | A model configuration: C all-Claude (D, Jev classifier + Claude actor, is built but held back from v3.0.0, OD-516). A (all-local) and B (local classifier + Claude actor) are removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031). |
| pair | The configured (classifier, actor) models for an address. |
| classifier / actor | The model that fills the schema / the model that proposes an action. |
| Claude queue, `awaiting_claude` | Items waiting for a person to run `/ecf-review`. |
| Claude queue timeout (`claude_queue_timeout`) | Removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031): an optional hand-off of long-waiting Claude items to the local model ("local fallback"). |
| check | One round of fetching and processing an address. |
| pre-check, `prechecked` | The scheduled model-free check; records it created carry `prechecked = true`. |
| catch-up | Running checks back to back while a backlog remains. |
| time=0 | An address's first successful check: it records INBOX's position and fetches nothing. Mail that arrived before it, including after `ecf address add`, is reached only by `ecf backfill` (OD-507). |
| old mail, marker | An item an `ecf backfill` read (`facts.backfill`, with its run in `facts.scan_run`) or `ecf reprocess` decided again (`facts.reprocess`): no card or post of its own, every hide approved, one Slack summary per run (§5.4; OD-507). |
| lease, fencing token | A time-limited lock on an address; a counter that makes writes from an expired holder fail. |
| claim | A time-limited right for a model session to work on one item. |
| grant | A single-use, hash-bound permission to execute one action on one message. |
| stage | shadow ("Watching only"), assist ("Labels only"), live ("Full"). |
| sensitivity | `standard` or `high` ("Finance (extra checks)") per address. |
| role | [M2] a person's per-address permission: `approver`, `reviewer` or `observer`. v1 has no roles; the OS user does everything. |
| approval mode | single-approver in v1; multi-approver in M2. |
| step-up | A fresh OS authentication (Touch ID, password, PAM or polkit) bound to one action. |
| action policy | The per-action auto/approve matrix (§8.3). |
| reversible | An action ecf can undo. |
| hide action, hide corroboration | mark_read, archive, move, junk; the server-side evidence required before one runs automatically. |
| outbound switch | Per-address `OUTBOUND` on/off gate for sends. |
| probe | Per-address capability check of the IMAP server. |
| real-service test | A test against real Slack, mail or OS services, run with the operator's go-ahead. |
| "Needs you" | The pinned Slack message listing items waiting on a person. |
| digest, daily summary | Hourly (business-hours) roll-up of automatic actions; the once-a-day status post. |
| `content_unscanned` | A flag that part of the message wasn't fully scanned or verified. |
| `stable_id` | ecf's identifier for a message (§6.3). |
| `local_high_risk` | Removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031): the policy used when a local model acted on a high-risk item (§8.2). |
| `high_risk_route` | The server's decision that an item is high risk and which actor or policy handles it. |
| manifest digest | The content hash of an Ollama model, pinned per release until v3.0.0 (ADR 0031). |
| `models.lock` | The file, shipped in the `ecf_server` wheel, holding the pinned Claude model ID for each role for a release; the Ollama pin had its own file (OD-235), a stub from v3.0.0 (ADR 0031). |
| `install_role` | `prod` or `test`. |
| `resident` | Removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031): kept the local model loaded. |
| unverified sender | A payment-related message whose DMARC result is `none`. |
| first-time sender | A sender with `sender_seen_before = false` (§7.2). |
| N-1 | The previous product version. |
| Wilson interval | A confidence interval for a proportion that behaves well at small counts. |
| McNemar test | A paired test comparing two classifiers on the same items. |
| non-inferiority | A switch is allowed when the new model is not worse than the old by more than a margin. |
| (rv) | Verified by a reviewer's cited source, not re-checked by Claude. |
| OBSERVE, WORK, RESPOND | MCP tool profiles (§10.4). RESPOND is not in v1. |

## 3. Architecture and trust boundary [v1]

### 3.1 Components

```
 This computer (one OS user)
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ ecf CLI ─────────┐                                                     │
 │ Claude Code      │  HTTP over 0600 Unix socket                          │
 │  (ecf claude) ─ ecf-mcp (stdio) ─┤                                     │
 │                  ▼                                                     │
 │  ┌──────────── ecf-server local (launchd / systemd user unit) ──────┐  │
 │  │ API (Starlette/uvicorn) · timers (1-min tick) · job queue        │  │
 │  │ broker: IMAP/SMTP · facts · DKIM/DMARC · fraud/regulator triggers│──┼──► IMAP/SMTP provider
 │  │ rules · policy · grants · transition() · executor                │  │
 │  │ Slack Socket Mode client ─────────────────────────────────────── │──┼──► Slack (outbound WebSocket)
 │  │ Stepper (Touch ID / PAM / polkit) · Notifier                     │  │
 │  │ telemetry receiver (loopback TCP, separate app)                  │  │
 │  │ SQLite (WAL) · log files · OS secret store                       │  │
 │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 Anthropic receives message text only inside /ecf-review and /ecf-eval subagents (preset C; D's actor).
 TypeSafe receives only the eval's synthetic text in v3.0.0 (preset D, which would send it mail, is held back, OD-516).
 No model runs on this computer from v3.0.0 (ADR 0031).
```

### 3.2 Trust boundary

- **The local service computes facts, fraud and regulator triggers, rules and policy.** Model sessions submit only classifications and proposals. Model output can raise risk but can never, alone, hide mail, approve or send anything. Nothing a model returns becomes a fact; a computed fact goes to a model only as a derived signal an OD exempts (§7.2, ADR 0026).
- **Mailbox credentials** are held only by the service's broker, in the OS secret store. Model processes never see them; the CLI sees an app password only while you type it into a hidden prompt, and passes it over the socket for the service to store. Hidden prompts need a real terminal: without one (e.g. Claude Code's `!` commands) the CLI refuses with a message saying to run the command in a terminal, rather than echoing the input (observed 2026-09-28).
- **Clients** (`ecf` CLI, `ecf-mcp`) contain no rules, policy, facts or state transitions. `ecf` never imports `ecf_server` (import-linter).
- **Stated limit** (§12.2): in v1 the boundary is a process boundary on one machine; anyone who controls your OS account controls ecf.

### 3.3 Ports (Protocols, no SDK imports)

Only where a second implementation or a test fake is needed now (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-125):

| Port | v1 implementations | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `MailSource` | IMAP (`imapclient`); from M6 (in progress) also the Gmail API (`GmailApiSource`, OD-529) | capability flags, semantic actions, sending included |
| `ChatSurface` | Slack Socket Mode | neutral `ItemCard`; opaque `RouteRef`/`ThreadRef`; flags `private_routes`, `create_route`, `pin`, `per_route_identity`, `sync_interaction_response` |
| `SecretStore` | Keychain, Secret Service, `systemd-creds` | service is the only writer |
| `Stepper` | LocalAuthentication, PAM (polkit from M5, OD-224) | always run by the service |
| `Notifier` | macOS `osascript`, `notify-send`, none | no email-derived text |
| `Classifier`, `Actor` | Claude via the plugin; TypeSafe Jev for the classifier (`ecf_server/jev.py`; eval only: preset D held back, OD-516) | Ollama removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031) |
| `Clock` | system; injectable fake | wall-clock and monotonic |

State, blob storage and identity are plain modules in v1 (redesigned against DynamoDB in M1). Adapter selection is an explicit registry dict, no entry-point plugins.

## 4. Presets and operating model [v1]

### 4.1 Operating model

- ecf runs **only while the computer is on and awake** (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-018; `/loop` is not used in v1). The service runs the scheduled pre-check at each address's fetch interval (default 10 min in business hours, 30 min otherwise); a D address's mail would be classified by Jev after the fetch (built in v3.0.0 step 4; D held back, OD-516). `ecf watch` runs the service in the foreground; `ecf service install` makes it the background unit.
- **Claude is used on demand:** the operator opens `ecf claude` and types `/ecf-review`. `claude -p` and scheduled Claude runs are not used. Unattended Claude is the M4 Bedrock item.
- **Service level** (v3.0.0, ADR 0031, P18): nobody classifies a C address's mail until someone runs `/ecf-review` in an `ecf claude` session. Addresses that were preset A go from "within one check interval" to "at the next review". The model-free pre-check still labels, flags and escalates fraud and regulator mail at fetch (§5.4). Plan on a review at least once a working day: the reminder at `claude_review_reminder_hours` (24 h) and the escalation at twice that (§13.3) say when one is overdue. Each item costs about 1.7-2.3k input tokens on Sonnet agents (§10; measured before v3.0.0 moved every gate role to Opus, OD-520), on the reviewer's Claude plan.
- Not supported: the claude.ai web app and desktop Chat tab for processing, desktop scheduled tasks, Windows.

### 4.2 Presets

**v3.0.0** (ADR 0031, OD-506; supersedes OD-003 and OD-495): presets A (all-local) and B (local classifier + Claude actor) are removed with Gemma and Ollama. C is the default; D, "Jev classifier + Claude actor", was built in v3.0.0 step 4 (`planning-docs/v3.0.0-PLANNING.md` §4.5) and is **held back from v3.0.0** (operator decision 2026-10-15, OD-516): v3.0.0 ships C only, Jev stays eval-only, and D is revisited when TypeSafe ships a better version (its code stays, dormant: §7.10). At upgrade every A or B address becomes C and is paused (§4.3).

| | C: all-Claude | D: Jev classifier + Claude actor (built in step 4; held back from v3.0.0, OD-516) |
|---|---|---|
| Runs | everything waits for `/ecf-review` | Jev classifies within seconds of the pre-check (§7.10); actor items queue for `/ecf-review`; while Jev is down D mail waits, and nothing else classifies it (no Claude fallback in v3.0.0, OD-510) |
| Classifier, `standard` | `ecf-classifier` (Opus from v3.0.0, OD-520; Sonnet from v1.0.0, OD-461; was Haiku 4.5; batched) | TypeSafe Jev, pinned (`jev.lock`) |
| Classifier, `high` | `ecf-classifier-high` (Opus from v3.0.0, OD-520; 1 message per spawn by default) | TypeSafe Jev |
| Actor, standard items | Opus family from v3.0.0 (OD-521; Sonnet before) | Opus family |
| Actor, high-risk items | Opus family | Opus family |
| Must be running | computer, service; Claude Code during review | computer, service, network to api.typesafe.ai; Claude Code during review |
| Claude plan | the reviewer's own | the reviewer's own, plus TypeSafe's per-token charge (§20) |

- Config rejects any preset but C and D; migration 0038 rebuilds `addresses` with `CHECK (preset IN ('C','D'))` (ADR 0031, R-D7). While D is held back (OD-516) an address can be C only: the service refuses adding a D address ("preset D (TypeSafe Jev) isn't available in v3.0.0 (OD-516); add the address as preset C"), `ecf address add` and `ecf init` don't offer D, and import and restore refuse a bundle with a D address that isn't removed, with the same reason; D stays a valid stored value. When D is on, adding a D address needs the TypeSafe key, the account owner's typed agreement and step-up, and refuses while your own fields are stored (§7.10; OD-509); a preset changes only by remove and re-add.
- **Pinned pair per address:** the configured (classifier, actor) pair, with its own gate (the fallback models and their gates are removed in v3.0.0). The service enforces high-risk ceilings from the pinned pair, not from what a client claims.
- Claude is used only during `/ecf-review` and `/ecf-eval`; no idle usage. README advises keeping Claude's extra paid usage off or capped. `ecf init` warns about plan usage whenever preset C is chosen.
- The eval compares Jev against C (`planning-docs/JEV-STEP2.md` draft 5).

### 4.3 Claude queue (the local fallback removed in v3.0.0)

- Every C item, and a D item that needs the actor, waits at `awaiting_claude` until `/ecf-review`, which works through the queue interactively and exits. A D item waits there unclassified for Jev's drain (§7.10): `/ecf-review` never offers it for classification, and it counts in none of the queue's `waiting`, `backlog`, `overdue`, reminder or escalation, but as "waiting for Jev" in the daily summary and `ecf status` (v3.0.0 step 4, P13).
- **No local fallback** (v3.0.0, ADR 0031, R-D4, P10; supersedes OD-019 and OD-020): mail waits however long it takes. The `claude_review` reminder opens at `claude_review_reminder_hours` (24 h) and a second, loud alert at twice that (48 h), counts and dates only (§13.3). `claude_queue_timeout`, its shadow runs, its gates (`fallback/B`, `fallback/C`) and `fallback_shadow` are removed; items the fallback had handed off get `claude_since` = the upgrade time (P12). The queue's per-tick queries (`claude_queue.backlog`, `overdue`, `waiting`, the review queue) read the partial index `items_claude_waiting (address_id, claude_since) WHERE status IN ('awaiting_claude', 'clarified')` (0038), and the reminder and the escalation share one `overdue` query per tick (diff review R2).
- **As built in V1.4** (step 1, 2026-10-02; code: `ecf_server/claude_queue.py`; the B and local-model parts removed in v3.0.0): **C:** each email goes `new → awaiting_claude` as soon as the pre-check has decided it (its labels, flags and escalations stand); records-only backfilled mail is closed as `observed` and never queued, `ecf backfill --act` mail is queued like new mail. **B:** the local model classifies; when the rule continues to the actor the item goes `classified → awaiting_claude` instead of waiting for the local actor. **C after a Claude classification:** the same edge when the actor is needed (OD-269). An answered question (`clarified`) on a B or C address stays at `clarified` and waits for `/ecf-review` too. The local model queue takes only `new` mail in A and B and the actor's items in A, so Gemma never gets Claude's work (until the fallback, step 8). Each tick queues items a crash left short (pre-checked C mail still at `new`, or a B/C item at `classified` whose rule continues to the actor) once they are a minute old. Nothing yet takes items off the queue: `/ecf-review` arrives in later V1.4 steps. **Preset changes:** a preset changes only by removing the address and adding it again; removal resolves its open items first, and adding again is refused while any item is open, so nothing is left at `awaiting_claude` (which has no edge back to the local model) or waiting for the wrong model. A future command that changes a preset in place must refuse while items wait for a model or Claude, or say how they move (operator decision 2026-10-02).
- **The fallback as built in V1.4** (step 8, 2026-10-02; OD-293 to OD-296): removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031); the record is in git history before the removal and in §23.4.
- **Converted addresses** (v3.0.0, migration 0038; ADR 0031, R-D3, P3, P8, P12): every A and B address, removed rows included, becomes C and is **paused**; the migration never refuses, and the importer does the same for older bundles. At the first start (and after a restore or import) `stages.announce_converted` moves a converted `live` address to `assist` through `set_stage` (audited, its own posted reason; an `assist` or `shadow` address keeps its stage), moves its pre-checked mail still at `new` (it waited for the local model; `ecf backfill --act` mail among it, a records-only backfill's left) to `awaiting_claude` through `claude_queue.route_new`, its wait starting then (diff review R3; the tick's sweep would also move it after a minute), writes an `address.converted` audit row and, in the same transaction, marks the address announced, then posts one Security Notice per address (ids and counts only, in the shared wording `ecf.upgrade_check.converted_notice` from v3.0.3 (operator request 2026-10-16), as `ecf upgrade`, `ecf doctor` and `ecf resume` use since v3.0.2; R6: a failure after the mark doesn't announce that address again); the settings `stages.converted_v3` (each converted address and its old preset) and `stages.converted_v3_announced` make a restore announce it again. Removing a converted address drops its id from `stages.converted_v3`, `..._announced` and `..._consented`, so adding it again starts afresh (R5); `import --replace` clears all three before applying the bundle (R7). The waiting-item count isn't computed for a consented address (R6). While paused its items aren't offered to `/ecf-review` (§13.3), and the pre-check and fraud flagging go on (§5.4). **Resuming it is the consent act** (`ecf resume <address>` asks "Has the account owner agreed to their mail and derived signals going to Anthropic? [y/N]"; no `--yes`; the service refuses the resume with 409 without `owner_agreed: true`; `--all` and the Slack buttons skip such an address and name it; the agreement is recorded once, in the setting `stages.converted_v3_consented` and an `address.consent_confirmed` audit row with no content, after which resumes are ordinary): the operator confirms the account owner agreed to mail, and the derived signals, going to Anthropic (OD-427, §12.4), or removes the address (`ecf address remove`). `ecf doctor`, a Security Notice and the new CLI's upgrade output name each converted address with its waiting-item count (`converted` in `GET /v1/upgrade/state`, §11.10). From v3.0.2 (OD-524, P3) the upgrade notice (on the 2.x to 3.x upgrade only), `ecf doctor` and the `ecf resume` question share one phrasing: "{id} was set up for a local model ecf no longer has; it now uses Claude and stays paused until the account's owner agrees to their mail, and what ecf derives from it, going to Anthropic; N email(s) waiting" ("and what ecf derives from it" added 2026-10-16, operator request: the derived signals, OD-483); doctor's row stays until consent or removal.

## 5. Pipeline [v1]

### 5.1 A check (per address)

1. **Take the check lease:** 3 minutes, renewed every 60 s by a dedicated renewal thread (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-023), with a fencing token required on every write; a per-address `threading.Lock` gives in-process exclusion. A crashed or sleeping holder blocks the address for at most 3 minutes. If the lease is busy, skip the address.
2. **Start with what changed elsewhere:** approvals, answers, executions, and `prechecked` records still at `new`.
3. **Fetch a page** via the broker since the service-owned cursor (§6.4):
   - `UID SEARCH UID <last+1>:*`, filtered to `uid > last_uid` (IMAP may return the highest existing UID); a NOOP precedes each query about what INBOX holds, since a server may hold back changes made by other sessions until then (Dovecot does; tested 2026-09-28); batched `UID FETCH` of `RFC822.SIZE`, envelope and `BODYSTRUCTURE`;
   - the **full raw message** via `BODY.PEEK[]` (IMAPClient returns it under `b'BODY[]'`) when `RFC822.SIZE ≤ max_message_bytes` (64 MB on `high`, 16 MB on `standard`; operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-024), because DKIM signs the whole body including attachments (RFC 6376, except with `l=`);
   - messages over 16 MB (a fixed threshold) are processed after the rest of the page, counted against the time budget, and deferred to the next check if time runs out (never skipped; listed in `deferred_uids`);
   - messages over the limit get headers and the first `max_scan_bytes_per_part` of each text part only; ecf never sets `\Seen` while fetching;
   - IMAP library: `imapclient` 4.1.0 (on stdlib `imaplib`; verified 2026-09-27, PyPI), unless the V1.1 real-service test shows it can't do partial and literal handling;
   - page limit 30 messages or 20 s, whichever first (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-026);
   - first run starts from now (`start_from: now`); history via `ecf backfill --since <date>` (time=0, §2).
   - **Deferred mail** (V1.1 build, 2026-09-28): after the page, deferred messages are handled oldest first, one at a time across the whole service, only while the check's budget (`max_per_check`) fits an estimate from their size and the throughput measured on the page (2 MB/s assumed until measured). Messages over `max_message_bytes` are read from BODYSTRUCTURE plus the header block (up to 256 KB) and the first `max_scan_bytes_per_part` of each text part; they are marked `oversized` and `content_unscanned`, and an attached message counts as one attachment. Messages over 16 MB but within the limit are read whole, with `tracemalloc` measuring the peak (it slows other threads while on, which is why it runs only for these). Deferred messages that disappear from INBOX are dropped from `deferred_uids`.
   - Full bodies are never batched into one FETCH; whether to fetch a large message is decided from `RFC822.SIZE`, measured throughput and the remaining budget; small mail is processed before deferred large mail (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-030).
   - **Memory (measured 2026-09-29, V1.1; operator decision 2026-09-29, OD-195):** a DKIM-signed invoice read from Dovecot through fetch, parse, DKIM, facts and triggers on this Mac (Python 3.12.14) peaked at 9 MB of Python memory for 1.1 MB, 149 MB for 17.2 MB and 557 MB for 64.6 MB (process growth 16, 246 and 871 MB), about 8.6 times the message size, not the 4-6 times estimated (OD-025). Stage peaks for 64.6 MB: parse 531 MB (Python's `email` parser holds several copies), DKIM 285 MB, fetch 204 MB; 7-10 s in all. So messages over 16 MB are parsed and verified in a short-lived child process (`python -m ecf_server.isolate`): the service fetches the message and passes it through a pipe, the child returns the parsed message and the DKIM/DMARC outcome as JSON (never pickle) and exits, and its memory goes back to the system (the child alone peaked at 746 MB resident for 64.6 MB, 3.3 s, with the DKIM key lookup failing early, since the test key isn't in public DNS; a passing check also hashes the body, whose in-process peak was below the parse peak). The child opens its own connection to the database for the DNS cache, with its own DNS budget; its stderr is discarded (a traceback could quote message text); a failure, timeout (180 s) or unreadable result counts as a crash on that message, so the quarantine rule applies. **imaplib debug output is off:** imapclient 4.1.0 sets the wrapped imaplib connection's `debug` to 5, which formats every command and response with `%r` even when nothing logs: the LOGIN line with the app password and each fetched message in full. That cost about 3 times the message size per fetch and was never given back (six 46 MB fetches grew the process footprint by about 144 MB each, measured with macOS `footprint`), and at DEBUG it would have logged secrets and content; ecf sets it to 0, after which the footprint stayed flat at about 170 MB across the six messages. The `high` default stays 64 MB (48 MB was considered to match Purelymail's 51,200,000-byte SMTP limit, then kept at 64 MB once the leak was fixed; operator decision 2026-09-29, OD-195). Oversized messages are processed one at a time across the whole service; the service logs its own peak per message. The `BytesHeaderParser` option is not needed. **Provider cap (operator decision 2026-09-29, OD-196):** when a tested provider-table row gives the provider's receiving limit and it is smaller than ecf's (default or set per address), ecf uses the provider's; mail above it is then handled as oversized. `APPENDLIMIT` isn't used: it bounds uploading into the mailbox, not receiving (Gmail advertises 34 MB and receives about 50 MB, unverified) (operator decision 2026-09-29, OD-200). Purelymail's 51,200,000 bytes (48.8 MB) is its tested sending limit; its inbound MX announces the same figure on port 587, and the port 25 listener that receives mail couldn't be reached from the test network, so the receiving limit is likely the same but unverified (§18 provider table). Sizes are printed in ecf's MB (1,048,576 bytes). Full messages are never written to disk.
4. **Compute facts** (§7.2) and run the **deterministic fraud and regulator triggers** (§8.5) over every decoded MIME part after stripping hidden HTML text; each decoded text part is scanned up to `max_scan_bytes_per_part` (10 MB; operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-027), measured after removing embedded base64 `data:` URIs from HTML (only inside quoted attribute values or CSS `url(...)`, so body text shaped like a data URI is still scanned; V1.1 build, 2026-09-28). Set `content_unscanned` when applicable (§7.2). Create the item at `new`, advance the cursor, and prepare truncated text (about 4,000 characters for the classifier and for the actor, the classifier's 1,500 until OD-558; each excerpt records the window it was cut at, `excerpts.classifier_chars`; `text/plain` preferred, HTML stripped) with a claim.
5. **Classify** (§7): Claude in `/ecf-review` (C), or Jev after the fetch (D; held back from v3.0.0, OD-516), records the classification (`record_classification`); the service validates strictly. The local model's failure handling (OD-236, `model_failed`) is removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031).
6. **Rules** (§8.6): first match wins, fraud guard first.
7. **Actor** runs only for items the service marks actor-needed; it proposes `{action, target, reason}` or `needs_clarification`.
8. **Policy** (§8, §9): stage, sensitivity ceiling, action policy, `high_risk_route`, outbound switch. Automatic actions get a grant and go to the action queue; items needing a person go to Slack through the Slack output queue.
9. **Report:** Slack threads only for items needing a person; the pinned "Needs you"; automatic actions roll into an hourly digest (with a per-address `content_unscanned` count); audit events are written by the service. No idle posts.

**Crash safety:** the service records "processing `<stable_id>`" before each message. After 2 crashes on the same message it quarantines it (`content_unscanned` plus escalate) and moves on, so one crafted email can't trip the crash-loop breaker and stop fraud checks everywhere. **Fixed in OD-552 (2026-10-24):** until then a quarantined item was never pre-checked, so it got no escalation; it now joins the check's new items and is escalated only; nothing reads it again (the pre-check skips its actions, `actions.verify` refuses it before any fetch for approved actions and reprocess, and Undo is never offered for it), and each check also pre-checks the address's new mail that an earlier failed check created, or an earlier version quarantined, but never pre-checked (at most 100 a check; backfill items are left to backfill, except that an item an earlier version quarantined during a scan carries no backfill mark and is escalated as new mail). **Since the V1.1 review (2026-09-29):** every message is parsed and DKIM-checked in a short-lived child process with a time limit (30 s plus 3 s per MB), so a crash, a hang or runaway work on one message counts as a crash on it and can never stall the single check thread (operator decision 2026-09-29, OD-204). **From the corpus build (2026-10-07; code: `ecf_server/isolate.py`):** the child also cuts both excerpts, removing text addressed to an automated reader (OD-254) under the same time limit, so a message whose redaction outruns it is quarantined like any other crash; a lost lease or a mail-connection error doesn't count as an attempt, since neither is the message's fault (a message the server can never deliver fails the check each time, which shows in `ecf status` and raises Mail Provider Unreachable).

### 5.2 Time budgets (the model queue removed in v3.0.0)

- `max_per_check` (default 6 minutes) bounds each check's IMAP and rules work; settable (1-30 min) from V1.3 (operator decision 2026-09-30, OD-228).
- **Removed in v3.0.0** (ADR 0031; the decisions were OD-028, OD-029, OD-032 and their amendments OD-243, OD-248, OD-264, OD-306): the global model queue and its 6-minute round, model loading and `resident`, Ollama's server settings, the heat throttle, the battery rules (model checks at the off-hours interval on battery, the sleep assertion during model work), `jobs` queue `model`, and the daily summary's "Waiting for the local model" and "On battery" lines. The records as built (V1.3, V1.4) are in git history before the removal.

### 5.3 Catch-up

`catch_up: auto|off` (default `auto`; operator decisions 2026-09-26, OD-031). When a check ends with messages still waiting, the next check starts after a 30 s pause instead of the interval, until the backlog is empty or `catch_up_max_minutes` passes; then normal intervals resume.
- `catch_up_max_minutes`: 30 on fanless laptops (MacBook Air, from a shipped lookup table of `hw.model` values), 60 elsewhere including all Linux machines, 30 on unknown Apple laptops. **V1.1** (V1.1 build, 2026-09-29): no verified table of fanless `hw.model` values exists yet (Apple Silicon models report identifiers like `Mac14,2`), so every Mac laptop (one with a battery) gets 30, the stricter value; Mac desktops and all Linux machines get 60.
- After the cap, catch-up can't restart for `catch_up_cooldown_minutes` (15).
- If the lease is busy when a round wants to start, catch-up waits up to 60 s rather than ending.
- On laptops it runs only on AC power (`pmset` on macOS, `/sys/class/power_supply` on Linux) unless `catch_up_on_battery: true` (default false).
- Each round keeps the 6-minute budget and renews its lease every 60 s; the pre-check is unaffected. The 30/60 defaults are checked against the V1.3 load test on the Air. **Checked** (V1.3 step 8d, 2026-10-01): the cap limits back-to-back mail checks only, and on a 150-email backlog the checks took 12.7 s on AC, so it never applies; model rounds weren't bound by it and heat was handled by the throttle (OD-248), both removed in v3.0.0. The defaults stay.
- **`ecf check`** fetches each address once (`--until-empty` and the local-model rounds it ran are removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031), P17). **Cards in a backlog** (V1.3 step 12b; from v3.0.0 keyed on the items waiting at `awaiting_claude`, P9, where it was the local model's backlog): while more than 100 items wait, an approval gets no card of its own: the digest's "Approve all N reversible" lists it, or, for a draft, "Drafts waiting for you to read" (OD-551) (`ecf inbox` shows all); once the backlog is back under 100, each tick posts the cards that were held back, up to 20 at a time (a card whose post Slack gave up on counts as not posted and is tried once more, OD-551; a card Slack refused, given up during an outage, or that failed twice, waits for `ecf slack repost` (until its approval expires, when it is posted once more), OD-557), so approvals the digest can't offer (payment, fraud, first-time senders, drafts) reach Slack before they expire. `ecf watch` stops the background unit, waits (up to 60 s) for the service's single-instance lock, writes a marker in the run folder, and runs `ecf-server local --foreground` as a child with an allow-listed environment (HOME, PATH, LANG, TZ, ECF_HOME; TMPDIR on macOS; the D-Bus, runtime and display variables on Linux); Ctrl-C stops it, and the unit is started again if it was running. A child process rather than the `execv` of the design plan, so the unit can be restored; if `ecf watch` itself is killed, `ecf status` and `ecf doctor` report the marker and `ecf service start` restores the unit and clears it.
- **Fixed after the V1.3 closing shadow run** (2026-10-01, §21.3 items 2 and 3): `--until-empty` and the local-model backlog estimate; removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031).
- `status` and the "Caught up" line show the remaining backlog (the ETA and "waiting for AC power" came from the local model and are removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031), P23). While a backlog exceeds 100 items, proposals post as batched review-style posts with "Approve all N reversible" per batch.

### 5.4 Scheduled pre-check (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-154)

Runs in the service with no model and no client session, while the computer is on.
- **Schedule:** per address, `mail_fetch_interval_workday` (10 min) inside business hours and `mail_fetch_interval_offhours` (30 min) otherwise; range 5-120 min (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-033); per-install defaults with per-address overrides. The 1-minute tick fetches each address whose interval has elapsed.
- **Business hours:** `business_hours` = days, start, end, IANA time zone; default Mon-Fri 08:00-17:00 `America/New_York` (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-034); per-address overrides. It also drives catch-up, digest timing and the daily summary.
- **What it does:** take the lease (skip if a model check holds it), fetch (same limits), compute facts, run the fraud and regulator triggers, create items at `new` with `prechecked = true`, advance the cursor, release.
- **Actions it may take** (model-free rules only, within the stage): a fraud trigger → `label(suspicious)`, `flag`, `escalate` (first-time sender + payment keyword without a second signal gets only `label(suspicious)`, `flag` and a digest section); a regulator trigger → `label(regulatory)`, `flag`, `escalate`; `payment keyword ∧ auth_result = none` → `label(unverified_sender)`, `flag`. Nothing is hidden, moved, answered or sent. In shadow stage it posts only. Pre-check actions run from `new` with a grant and an audit entry and no status change.
- **In V1.1** (V1.1 build, 2026-09-29; code: `ecf_server/precheck.py`, `ecf_server/actions.py`): the actions of every trigger that fired are combined (a message can get both `suspicious` and `regulatory`), not first match; a quarantined message (§5.1) is escalated like a fraud hit, the escalation only (no label or flag: it is never read again; until OD-552, 2026-10-24, a quarantined item was never pre-checked). The decision is stored on the item (`prechecked = 1`, `facts.precheck`) and audited as `precheck.decided`. In shadow nothing is done to the mailbox. Outside shadow, label and flag run after re-finding the message and verifying its content hash, under a grant claimed before acting (`action.granted`, `action.executed`, or `action.failed`); undo removes the keyword and flag (`action.undone`). Escalations are recorded as pending until Slack arrives in V1.2. Keywords follow `$ecf_<install>_<label>`; install names may contain `-`, which IMAP allows, and never `_`.
- **Hand-off:** the classifier (Claude in `/ecf-review`; Jev on a D address, held back from v3.0.0, OD-516) picks up `prechecked` items for classification and the remaining rules. Model output can add risk but can't undo a pre-check escalation. **Pause never stops the pre-check or fraud flagging.**
- **Since v2.1.0** (OD-490): a credential request, a gift-card code request or a crypto payment demand with a second signal, and a known sender whose mail fails DMARC, are fraud reasons, so the pre-check escalates them at fetch without the model (§8.5).
- **Escalation delivery:** a Slack thread immediately, up to `escalations_per_hour` per address for escalations other than fraud and regulator ones, which are never held back by the cap (bursts still merge; operator decision 2026-09-29, OD-212) (default 20; operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-035), beyond which they roll into one "N more escalations" thread ordered by severity (a known sender with a bank change first); more than 5 fraud or regulatory escalations in a minute merge into one thread (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-036); plus email per the alert settings (§13.3).
- **As built in V1.2** (step 6, 2026-09-29; code: `ecf_server/escalations.py`, `cards.py`): the pre-check queues each escalation in an `escalations` table in the same transaction as its decision (migration 0015), and the Slack thread posts it. Nothing is dropped: an escalation waits until your member ID is confirmed and its channel exists. Each becomes a card in the address's channel mentioning you; more than 5 for one address within a minute merge into one thread listing them by severity (a known sender with bank or change wording first, then other fraud and quarantined mail, then regulatory mail), and later ones in the same minute go into that thread. `escalations_per_hour` has nothing to hold back in V1.2: every pre-check escalation is fraud, quarantine or regulator, which the cap never delays (OD-212); it applies from V1.3. Escalations V1.1 recorded as pending (the migration carries them over) go into one post in the summary channel: counts by address, the 5 most severe of the last 7 days, and `ecf inbox` for the rest (OD-211).

- **Old mail** (v3.0.0 step 5, OD-507; plan `planning-docs/v3.0.0-STEP5.md` §2; code: `marked.py`, `scans.py`, `scan_summary.py`): one per-item marker, never a time window or an address flag, so new mail during a scan escalates at once as above. Marked items (`facts.backfill` or `facts.reprocess`): no Slack post or card of their own (their escalation rows are merged under their run's summary); every hide needs approval (`policy.Context.historical`); not in "Approve all", `approvals.pending`, held-back cards, re-offer cards or digests; not in the Claude backlog's card switch, the reminder or the overdue alert (a separate "N scan/reprocess items waiting" line in both); `/ecf-review` hands them out only when no new mail waits; "Needs you" and `ecf inbox` show one count line per run; no alert email (Possible Fraud Attempt, Regulatory Mail Notice, Unverified Payment Sender; §13.3): the run's summary thread mentions you instead (operator decision 2026-10-14, review M5); scanned mail never counts toward sender history; `ecf stats --stages` reports them apart.

### 5.5 Clocks and sleep

- Due-ness, lease expiry and approval TTLs use wall-clock time. The tick and the 10-minute send delay use the monotonic clock, which stops during sleep on macOS and Linux (documented).
- **Scheduling in V1.1** (V1.1 build, 2026-09-29; code: `ecf_server/schedule.py`): the 1-minute tick enqueues a `fetch` job for each address whose `next_due_at` has passed (or that was never checked), never twice; a `checks` worker thread runs them one at a time and sets the next due time: the interval for the hour, 30 s while catching up, 60 s after a busy lease. Power comes from `pmset -g batt` (macOS) or `/sys/class/power_supply` (Linux); unknown means a desktop on AC. A failed tick is logged and never stops the timer; a crashed check fails its job, which retries with the queue's backoff.
- Sleep is detected when wall-clock minus monotonic drift between two ticks exceeds a threshold; on wake every address's due time is re-evaluated at once and a pending send delay re-announces "sending in 10 minutes". **As built** (V1.2 review, 2026-09-30, which found two thresholds): the scheduler makes every address due after a drift of more than 60 s (`schedule.SLEEP_DRIFT_S`, V1.1); the approval runner re-announces delayed sends after more than 120 s (`service.SLEEP_GAP_S`, V1.2), so a short stall doesn't repeat the announcement. Both are fixed numbers (§14.3).
- A watchdog exits non-zero (so launchd/systemd restart the service) and notifies you if no tick happens for 5 minutes while awake.

### 5.6 Other rules

- **Folders:** INBOX only.
- **Heartbeats** exist for `status` only.
- **Batched classification:** classifications record a `batch_id`; hide actions are never automatic when the batch contained any item with a fraud signal, the `phishing` item (`spam_or_phishing` before S3b), or `fraud_risk ≥ low` (cross-item injection guard). **For Claude** (V1.4 step 3; code: `claude_queue.batch_risky`): the items one `review_queue` round gives the same batched agent (`ecf-classifier`, `ecf-actor`) form a batch (the `-high` agents take one item each); since the items of a batch are submitted one at a time, a member not yet classified counts as risky, so a hide decided for an earlier member needs approval (operator decision 2026-10-02, OD-282). An item claimed again keeps its earlier batches.
- **Digests** post one per address channel, only inside business hours (off-hours automatic actions roll into the first business-hour digest); each digest's Pause pauses that address; fraud and regulatory escalations stay immediate.

## 6. State model [v1]

### 6.1 SQLite tables [proposed; accepted 2026-09-27, OD-162]

Normalized tables per entity (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-150; Fable/Opus review). Column lists are [proposed]. Types [proposed]: keys and identifiers `TEXT NOT NULL`; counts, versions and fencing tokens `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`; booleans `INTEGER NOT NULL` (0/1); JSON columns `TEXT` validated by Pydantic on read and write; timestamps `TEXT` (UTC ISO-8601); `STRICT` tables; foreign keys from per-address tables to `addresses`; `senders`, `sent`, `threads` and `gate` rows are kept like their retention exemption (§6.5). All timestamps are UTC ISO-8601 text. Every table has `schema_version` where rows are migrated individually.

| Table | Key | Columns (summary) |
|---|---|---|
| `addresses` | `address_id` | email, display_name, sensitivity, stage, paused, outbound, preset (C, or D: built in step 4, held back from v3.0.0, OD-516; `CHECK` since migration 0038), classifier_id, actor_id, per-address overrides (JSON), created_at, removed_at (addresses are marked removed, not deleted, because items refer to them; operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-167) |
| `cursors` | `address_id` | uidvalidity, last_uid, deferred_uids (JSON), version |
| `leases` | `address_id` | holder, fencing_token, expires_at |
| `probe` | `address_id` | special_use (JSON), permanent_keywords, saves_sent, max_message_bytes, host, probed_at |
| `items` | `stable_id` | address_id, uid, uidvalidity, message_id, locator (JSON), status, stale, prechecked, decision_source, proposed_by, suppressed_action, review, human_correction (JSON), classification (JSON), facts (JSON), proposal (JSON), pinned_models (JSON), batch_id, content_hash, hash_version, duplicate_message_id, expiry_count, clarification_rounds, created_at, updated_at, schema_version |
| `excerpts` | `stable_id` | classifier_text, actor_text (each ≤ 4,000 chars), classifier_chars (the window the classifier excerpt was cut at: 4,000, or 1,500 before OD-558); deleted with the item |
| `grants` | `grant_id` | stable_id, action_hash, content_hash, principal, status (`issued`, `approved`, `consumed`, `voided`; operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-168), stepup_nonce_id, expires_at, consumed_at |
| `nonces` | `nonce_id` | purpose, bound_hash, person, created_at, expires_at, consumed_at |
| `jobs` | `job_id` | queue (`actions`, `slack_out`, `fetch`; `model` removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031)), address_id, payload (JSON; action jobs carry only a grant ID), attempts, max_attempts, timeout_s (claims expire after 6x it), created_at (FIFO tie-break) (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-169), visible_at, claimed_by, claim_expires, state (`queued`, `claimed`, `done`, `dead`), last_error |

| `gate` | (`address_id`, `pair_key`) | reviewed, correct, fraud_misses, unsafe, pinned_ids, passed_at (`ollama_digest` dropped by 0038; rows for local and fallback keys kept, R-D8) |

| `eval_runs` (V1.3, migration 0020) | `run_id` | pair, model digest (Ollama's before v3.0.0), set version, created_at, metrics (JSON), gate_passed, result file path (§16.2) |
| `model_calls` (V1.3, migration 0018; 0040) | id | ts, address, preset, stage, role, outcome, digest, token counts and durations; from 0040 (v3.0.0 step 4) `backend`, `model`, `fault`, `ms`, `tries` for Jev's calls and probes; numbers only, pruned with `log_retention_days` (§7.5) |
| `routes` | (`address_id`, `surface`) | route_ref, thread refs (JSON) |

Indexes: a partial index `items(address_id, updated_at) WHERE status IN (<open statuses>)` feeds "Needs you" and `ecf inbox`.

### 6.2 Statuses and transitions

`Status` is a `StrEnum`. The transition table is data (`Mapping[Status, frozenset[Status]]`) plus a guard table keyed by (from, to) (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-037). The only writer is `transition()` in `ecf_server`. The rules are tested with a Hypothesis `RuleBasedStateMachine` driving `check_transition()` through random walks, and example tests drive `transition()` against SQLite. SQLite itself enforces the single writer (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-181): an authorizer installed on every connection refuses any write to `items.status` outside `transition()` and any insert into `items` outside `create_item()`, whatever the SQL form; connections disable the statement cache so the check always runs. The state diagram (§22.1) is hand-drawn until V1.0 and generated from the table afterwards.

- **Terminal:** `observed`, `executed` (can still be undone), `undone`, `rejected`, `cancelled`, `resolved_manual`, `resolved_by_mailbox`.
- **Open:** `new`, `classified`, `awaiting_claude`, `proposed`, `held`, `awaiting_approval`, `awaiting_stepup`, `approved`, `delayed`, `executing`, `failed`, `failed_unknown`, `expired`, `needs_clarification`, `clarified`, `needs_human`, `undoing`, `undo_failed`. [M3] `answer_proposed`.
- `auto` is a decision, not a status.

| From | To | Guard / note |
|---|---|---|
