| `new` | `classified` | Jev classification recorded (preset D, built in step 4, held back from v3.0.0, OD-516; the local classifier before v3.0.0) |
| `new` | `awaiting_claude` | preset C |
| `new` | `observed` | `ecf backfill` without `--act`: recorded and pre-checked, nothing done (terminal; operator decision 2026-09-30, OD-221) |
| `classified` | `awaiting_claude` | actor-needed after a classification: preset C (operator decision 2026-10-02, OD-269), and D (built in step 4; held back, OD-516) |
| `awaiting_claude` | `classified` | C, Claude classification (D has no Claude fallback while Jev is down in v3.0.0, OD-510) |
| `awaiting_claude` | `proposed` | the Claude actor |
| `classified` | `proposed` | rules/actor done |
| `proposed` | `executing` | automatic, grant issued; only when live, or in assist for label, flag, escalate and leave (OD-182) |
| `proposed` | `awaiting_approval` | policy needs a person; only when live (OD-182) |
| `proposed` | `needs_clarification` | actor asked |
| `proposed` | `observed` | shadow stage (terminal) |
| `proposed` | `held` | assist stage, action not yet allowed |
| `held` | `proposed` | only when the address is live |
| `held` | `resolved_manual` | |
| `awaiting_approval` | `approved` | reversible approval only; everything else goes through `awaiting_stepup` |
| `awaiting_approval` | `awaiting_stepup` | step-up required |
| `awaiting_approval` | `rejected`, `expired` | |
| `awaiting_approval` | `proposed` | Fix changes the decision |
| `awaiting_stepup` | `approved` | origin = approval |
| `awaiting_stepup` | `clarified` | origin = answer on a payment/fraud item |
| `awaiting_stepup` | `expired` | TTL |
| `awaiting_stepup` | `rejected` | origin = approval: an approval queued for step-up can still be rejected (V1.2 step 7b) |
| `approved` | `executing` | |
| `approved` | `delayed` | a send on a `high` address |
| `delayed` | `executing`, `cancelled` | 10 minutes of awake time |
| `expired` | `awaiting_approval` | origin = approval (after a first expiry, or `ecf approve` after a second, OD-223) |
| `expired` | `needs_clarification` | origin = answer |
| `expired` | `resolved_manual` | |
| `needs_clarification` | `clarified` | non-risky answer |
| `needs_clarification` | `awaiting_stepup` | answer on a payment/fraud item |
| `needs_clarification` | `needs_human` | when a third round begins: a third question, or an answer expiring in the second round (OD-182) |
| `clarified` | `proposed` | only within the two-round cap |
| `needs_human` | `proposed`, `resolved_manual` | |
| `executing` | `executed`, `failed`, `failed_unknown` | 3 attempts with backoff; a send is retried only when it provably failed before the server accepted it (connection or pre-DATA error), otherwise it goes to Sent reconciliation (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-156) |
| `failed`, `failed_unknown`, `executing` (stuck) | `executing` | `ecf item requeue`; broker reconciles first |
| `failed_unknown` | `executed`, `failed` | a send's outcome settled from the Sent folder (V1.5; OD-322) |
| `failed` | `delayed` | `ecf item requeue` of a send on a `high` address: the 10-minute delay again (V1.5; OD-329) |
| `executed` | `undoing` | reversible actions |
| `observed`, `executed` | `awaiting_claude`, `classified` | `ecf reprocess` classifies an old item again (guard `reprocess`; OD-507) |
| `observed`, `executed` | `proposed` | `ecf reprocess` plans an old item again on its stored classification (guard `reprocess`; OD-507) |
| `undoing` | `undone`, `undo_failed` | |
| `undone` | `proposed` | Fix only |
| any open | `resolved_manual` | `ecf item resolve --reason` (step-up on payment or fraud items) or Slack Dismiss (non-payment, non-fraud) |
| any open | `resolved_by_mailbox` | the email was already moved, archived or deleted in your mail client (checked each check; operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-039) |

- **Guards for stage and clarification** (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-182): `observed` only in shadow, `held` only in assist, `awaiting_approval` only when live, and `executing` from `proposed` only when live or, in assist, for the always-allowed actions. A clarification round is counted each time a question is asked or an answer expires (an expired answer is one of the two rounds); an answer (`→ clarified`, or `→ awaiting_stepup` on payment or fraud items) is accepted only within 2 rounds, and `needs_human` is reached exactly when a third round begins.
- **Held items** appear as one batched digest line and run only after go-live; you can still act by hand in your mail client (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-038). `ecf stage set live` prints held counts by age, says that held items ≤ 7 days execute at once, and offers to resolve older ones (default 7 days) as `resolved_manual`, or "resolve all held".
- **Fix and Correct:** ✅ Correct records `review = correct`; ✏️ Fix records `human_correction` and returns the item to `proposed` when the decision changes (from `awaiting_approval`, or via undo from `executed`); on a `held` item it records the correction and replaces the held proposal, and the item stays `held` until the address is live (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-157); on `observed` items it only records the correction for the gate. Fix and sender confirmation never remove a trigger already fired.
- **Expiry:** `expiry_count` counts approval expiries only and drives "after a second expiry": a second expired approval waits at `expired`, listed in the daily summary, until `ecf approve <id>` offers it again with a fresh grant (`approval.reoffered`, OD-223) or `ecf item resolve` closes it. Answers have their own limit: an expired answer counts as one of the two clarification rounds, so expiring in the second round sends the item to `needs_human` (V1.2 review, 2026-09-30: one shared count made a first approval expiry after an expired answer look like a second). On approval expiry the Slack card is edited in place with a fresh grant and "expired, decide again".
- **Attributes:** `decision_source` (`rule`, `actor`, `human`), `proposed_by`, `suppressed_action`, `review`, `pinned_models`, `prechecked`, `stale`, `model_failed` (V1.3, OD-236; an attribute, not a status; removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031)).
- **Undo:** archive, move and junk move back to INBOX (UID re-resolved by Message-ID); label and flag remove the keyword or flag; mark_read removes `\Seen`; drafts are deleted. Available until retention removes the item.
- **Unknown send outcome:** if the probe found the provider saves sent mail itself, the broker searches `\Sent` for the pre-generated Message-ID and settles `executed` or `failed`; otherwise (ecf appends its own copy only after a confirmed send) → `failed_unknown`, escalated.
- **Short IDs:** a unique hex prefix of at least 8 characters is accepted wherever `<id>` is.

**Review fixes** (V1.2 review, 2026-09-30; code: `approvals.py`, `answers.py`, `items.py`, `backfill.py`, `schedule.py`): an answer waiting for step-up is told apart from an approval by the item's state (`answer_pending`), never by the caller: `ecf reject`, `ecf approve` and `approve --pending` refuse it and point to `ecf answer <id>`. `request` and `ask` check the transition before writing, so a refused one leaves the live card's proposal and question alone. Any move to a terminal status voids the item's open grants and deletes its send delay in the same transaction, so closing a delayed send (resolve, Dismiss, gone from the mailbox) leaves nothing to run; the countdown also skips items no longer `delayed`. One item's error no longer stops the expiry loops (logged and skipped). A backfill pass decides before saving its progress and picks up anything a failed pass left undecided in its range. A due time set during a check (an Undo click) is kept when the check ends, so the Undo runs within a minute.

**A used grant** (V1.2 review, 2026-09-30; code: `execute.py`, `approvals.requeue`): when an action's job finds its grant already `consumed`, the action may have run before a crash or an expired claim, so the item goes to `failed_unknown` (audit `action.outcome_unknown`) and is never run again unchecked. `ecf item requeue` may retry a hide action there (a person decides); it refuses a send whose grant was used, until V1.5 reconciles against the Sent folder: check Sent, then `ecf item resolve`.

### 6.3 Message identity

- `stable_id = sha256(address_id | normalized Message-ID | content_hash)`.
- `content_hash` = hash of the decoded text parts and the raw attachment bytes from raw MIME, normalized for line endings, charset and trailing whitespace; size excluded; `hash_version` stored (version 1 includes attachment bytes). **Version 1 layout** (V1.1 build, 2026-09-28): SHA-256 over the prefix `ecf-content-v1\0`, then every leaf MIME part in document order as a kind byte (`t` for text/plain or text/html not marked as an attachment, `a` for anything else), an 8-byte big-endian length and the data; text is decoded to Unicode with LF line endings and trailing whitespace removed per line and at the end, then UTF-8 encoded; other parts contribute their transfer-decoded bytes. Headers are not included. **Version 0 (partial)** is for messages over `max_message_bytes`, whose content isn't fetched: SHA-256 over the prefix `ecf-partial-v1\0`, then Message-ID, Date, From and Subject (each length-framed), then each leaf part's section, type and encoded size from BODYSTRUCTURE. Headers that change between deliveries (Received, Delivered-To) are left out, so a re-delivered large message still matches its first record (V1.1 build, 2026-09-28).
- No Message-ID: `sha256(address_id | UIDVALIDITY | UID)`.
- **Parsing malformed headers** (V1.1 build, 2026-09-29): messages are parsed with Python's modern email policy; if its header parser fails on malformed input, the whole message is parsed again with the older, more tolerant `compat32` policy (encoded words decoded by ecf), counted as a defect, with the same content hash. Python 3.12.3's modern parser raises `IndexError` on, for example, a truncated `Message-ID` or some address headers (found by the fuzz tests on CI; later 3.12 releases and 3.13 don't), and 3.12.3 is Ubuntu 24.04's system Python.
- A reused Message-ID with different content creates a second record and sets `duplicate_message_id`.
- Outside UIDVALIDITY recovery and rollback re-fetches, a `stable_id` collision at a new UID is recorded as a duplicate delivery and not re-actioned, unless the headers a reader judges it by differ (From, display name, Reply-To, Subject; an `identity_digest` kept in the item's facts): then it is a new item, analyzed in full, with trigger 5 ("Message-ID reused") (V1.1 review, 2026-09-29). Items made before the digest was kept count as unchanged.
- Provider IDs live in the opaque `locator`.

### 6.4 Cursor, leases, grants

- **Cursor** (service-owned, conditional on `version`): `{uidvalidity, last_uid, deferred_uids[]}`. If UIDVALIDITY changes: re-fetch by INTERNALDATE since the last processed message, deduplicate by `stable_id` (messages without a Message-ID matched by `content_hash` plus INTERNALDATE), drop and re-queue `deferred_uids` the same way, re-resolve open locators by Message-ID search, and post an informational "mailbox reset detected" notice.
- **Recovery in V1.1** (V1.1 build, 2026-09-29): the cursor records `recovering_until` (migration 0007). On a UIDVALIDITY change, ecf re-fetches INBOX mail since the day before the arrival (INTERNALDATE) of the last message read under the old UIDVALIDITY or of the earliest deferred message, whichever is older (the cursor keeps `deferred_since`, migration 0009; V1.1 review, 2026-09-29: using the time ecf read a message missed a backlog read days late), rewinds the cursor to just before it, re-points open items by Message-ID and audits `mailbox.reset`. While re-fetching, a message it already has (same `stable_id`, or without a Message-ID the same content hash and arrival date, which locators now record) is re-pointed to its new UID, not created again or recorded as a repeat delivery. The check reports `reset_recovered` and how many items were re-pointed. Once recovery is done, open items still pointing at the old UIDVALIDITY weren't found again and close as `resolved_by_mailbox`.
- **`resolved_by_mailbox` in V1.1** (V1.1 build, 2026-09-29): each check closes open items whose message is no longer in INBOX (under the current UIDVALIDITY) through `transition()`.
- **Leases:** claims carry `claim_expires` and the fencing token; stale tokens are rejected. All leases are cleared at service start (one process in v1). `executing` is reconciled against mailbox state before any retry.
- **Grants** bind `stable_id`, `content_hash`, the canonical action hash (action, target, template id and text, draft text, resolved recipient), the executing principal and an expiry. Single-use (conditional update). The broker re-resolves the locator and verifies `content_hash` before acting. Requeuing a send voids its grant and needs a new approval plus step-up. `ecf approve --pending` issues one batch nonce over the hash of the listed grant IDs.
- **Keywords** carry the install ID (`$ecf_<install>_<t>`); this install's own keywords without a local record (after a restore) are adopted silently; another install's keywords pause the address (§13.6). Phishing is `$ecf_<install>_phishing` from v3.0.0; mail labelled before keeps `$ecf_<install>_spam_or_phishing` (no relabel, OD-508, §8.6), as does mail planned before the upgrade and approved after it, and Undo removes whichever the item's `done` record names.

### 6.5 Retention and expiry

- Terminal items are deleted after `log_retention_days` (default 90, range 1-3650) by a daily local job in batches of 1,000. The audit log is never pruned, and neither are items that fired a fraud or regulator trigger (operator decision 2026-09-29, OD-217).
- **Exempt from pruning** (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-040): `senders`, `sent`, `threads`, `gate` and eval labels, so first-time-sender status and loop prevention survive.
- **As built in V1.2** (step 11a, 2026-09-30; code: `ecf_server/retention.py`): the service runs the job once a day from its timer (the last run is kept as `retention.last_run`). It deletes terminal items whose last change is older than `log_retention_days`, with their excerpts, grants, delays, escalation rows and Slack card records, and keeps items that fired a fraud, weak fraud or regulator trigger or were quarantined (the weak signal is kept too, as a fraud signal). Finished and dead jobs and used or expired step-up nonces older than the same age go as well. Open items, the audit log (table and files) and the OD-040 tables are never touched. Each run is audited (`retention.run`, with counts). `ecf retention show` gives the setting and the last run; `ecf retention set <days>` (1-3650) needs step-up, is audited (`retention.changed`), applies at the next daily run, and when it lowers the value sends a Security Notice (history goes sooner; the delay is 0 in local mode, OD-074).
- **Slack post records** (V1.2 review, 2026-09-30): the same job deletes records of one-off posts (digests, daily summaries, stale lists, alerts, answers, notices) older than `log_retention_days`. Item cards go with their item; "Needs you" and a burst card whose first item remains are kept.
- **Approval expiry** (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-041): sends after `approval_ttl_days_send` (4 days, so a long weekend doesn't lapse them), everything else after `approval_ttl_days` (14); per address. Step-up requests expire with the same TTL. On expiry nothing executes and the grant is voided.
- **Stale items:** open records are never auto-closed (except `resolved_by_mailbox`). After `stale_item_days` (30; operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-042) an open item gets `stale = true`, shown at the top of "Needs you" and `ecf inbox`, and listed in the daily summary until resolved; stale `held`, `new` and `awaiting_claude` items appear as one count line.
- **Unclicked batch buttons** (V1.3 step 12b): what a digest's "Approve all N reversible" or a review post's "All others correct" button binds is deleted by the same daily job 14 days after it was posted, when the approvals it lists have expired (a click re-checks every grant anyway).
- **`item.classified` outlives its item** (v3.0.0 step 5, OD-507, D12, P20): each classification's field values (enum, level or boolean; never text), the model and 16-hex digest prefixes are an audit row (~350 B), never pruned like the rest of the audit log, so the values stay after retention deletes the item: what classified what is the record the go-live gate and a later review need. The daily JSONL copy doubles it (about 50-60 MB a year at 200 emails a day). `slack_calls` (§13.4) is pruned with the logs.
- Retention decreases follow the announce flow (§9.6).

## 7. Classification and sender authentication [v1]

### 7.1 Schema v3 (2026-10-13, OD-498; v2 and v1 below)

Enum, ordinal and boolean fields only; one schema per install. Schema v3 (v3.0.0 step 1c, stage S2; operator decision 2026-10-13, OD-498; `planning-docs/v3.0.0-OPERATOR-SCHEMA.md` draft 3 §1, §9, §10, §15) is schema v2 with every field and value unchanged, level texts on `priority`, and five yes/no **fixed safety items** after v2's fields: `bank_detail_change`, `regulator_claim`, `phishing`, `claims_internal`, `private_individual` (`ecf.schema.FIXED_ITEMS`; wording approved by the operator 2026-10-13). Stage S2 is additive: nothing reads the fixed items yet, and the rules compiler refuses a condition on one until S3 (S2 review F2, 2026-10-13) (rules, policy, hide blockers, alerts, the Claude queue, review, the gate's accuracy and sender confirmation still read `category` and `sender_type`; they move in stage S3, when the overlapping `category` and `sender_type` values go). **Readers switch** (S3a, 2026-10-13, merged fb49b30; OD-500; `planning-docs/S3-READERS-SWITCH.md` draft 2): the fixed rules (§8.6) and every Python reader (policy's hide blockers and approval mode, alert emails, the Claude batch guard, own review and the review line) read each item through `ecf.schema.fixed_item`: the item is true, or one of its v2 source values holds (`FIXED_FROM_V2`); it only ever adds risk. In S3a the sources include the four values S3b removes (`category` `vendor_change_request`, `regulatory`, `spam_or_phishing`; `sender_type` `team`), so a classification that answers the old value and not the item (or the reverse) loses nothing while Claude still answers v3 with them; S3b deletes that half and keeps the kept sources (`sender_type` `regulator`; `person`, `friend`, `family`). Rules may read the items (S2's refusal lifted); a rules file can't test a removed value (`ecf.schema.REMOVED_VALUES`: refused with its replacement, e.g. `use regulator_claim: true`), `staff` included through its v1 alias. The schema text, its values and its digest don't change in S3a; S3a is never released alone (S3b removes the values, rewords, migrates with 0037).

**Values removed** (S3b, 2026-10-13, merged 21f62c6; OD-500; `planning-docs/S3-READERS-SWITCH.md` draft 2 §2, §3, §12): the four v2 values the fixed items now say are gone from schema v3: `category` `vendor_change_request` (→ `bank_detail_change`), `regulatory` (→ `regulator_claim`) and `spam_or_phishing` (→ `phishing`), and `sender_type` `team` (→ `claims_internal`); `regulator`, `person`, `friend` and `family` stay, and the fixed rules read them too (raise-only, P2). Reworded (operator-approved 2026-10-13, plan §12; each text stands alone, naming no field or value, P12): the `category` description (a fake email gets the value of what it pretends to be; the order to choose in), `account_security` (genuine or fake), `marketing` (adds other unsolicited bulk mail, P11) and `sender_type: unknown` (also a colleague of ours, genuine or not). After the first two S3b runs (`08016ba3`, `307e702d`; both failed the gate on `v2-acct-phish-callback-signin`, answered `account_security`, not phishing, `fraud_risk` low: the dropped `account_security` sentence had carried the "call a number" cue), `fraud_risk: medium` added "or to call a number or follow a link to secure an account" inside its sentence (operator decision 2026-10-13). With that text `mid-pay-today-or-suspend` ("pay 2,940 today or service is suspended") got `fraud_risk` low in 2 of 3 fresh runs (`93b81c72`, `ac11f6ca`), against medium in every recorded run with the original text (6 S3b-era runs, plus all earlier Sonnet, Haiku and Gemma runs in the eval archive), likely because the account-lure clause sat inside the medium sentence; so the clause became its own sentence: "Any request to move money, data, credentials or access on this email's say-so, whatever the pattern. A request to call a number or follow a link to secure an account counts too." (operator decision 2026-10-13, EDT). With the de1a2ff text, `v2-acct-phish-callback-signin` got `fraud_risk` medium in 3 of 3 runs but `phishing` true in only 1 of 3 (`75115bf7` yes; `93b81c72` and `ac11f6ca` no); before S3b the S2 runs gave medium and phishing true 2 of 2. With the two-sentence text it got `fraud_risk` medium in both runs and `phishing` true in 1 of 2 (`1a8708cf` yes, `024ec270` no), so 2 of 5 since the cue was added; always escalated by the fraud rule, never unsafe. Adding the cue to `phishing`'s description is left open (an operator decision), watched in later runs. The schema stays `version: 3` (v3 never shipped): the released v3 text is S3b's, and S2's never shipped (P9). Its digest (`schema-4278ecc26adcf354`) and Claude's prompt digest (`849bf956…`) change (both after the second `fraud_risk` change below; `schema-fef505501c5019cf` and `bf847c93…` in runs `75115bf7`, `93b81c72` and `ac11f6ca`; `schema-0e2a07357a7526a2` and `6359c0e2…` in the first S3b runs), so C gates start again, as with S2. `ecf.schema.fixed_item` reads the item and its kept sources only (`KEPT_SOURCES`); S3a's bridge (the removed values as sources, the fixed rules' bridge clauses, `review._with_items`) is deleted. The safety core is `SAFETY_FIELDS` alone (`SAFETY_VALUES` removed): `check_safety_core` refuses a shipped schema that holds a removed value, an extension can't add one back (`_clashes`, since the local model was still asked v2, which has them, until v3.0.0 removed it), and the extension heading names no category. **Presets A and B** (removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031); from then only old results, labels and migration 0037 use `from_v2`, P6) were still asked v2 (prompt, `num_predict`, prompt digest and `local_key` unchanged); `ecf.schema.from_v2` brings their answer to v3 (D3): the fixed items it lacks derived first (`with_fixed`), then a removed value read as its field's least informative value (`category` `other`, `sender_type` `unknown`, as `evalrun.null_classification` does; `REMOVED_READ_AS`). The classifier, the decision models (`systemone`), preset B's Gemma source (`claude_eval._completed`), `ecf eval rescore` and, in SQL, migration 0037 (§11.9) use it; so does a v3 answer recorded before S3b with a removed value: in `ecf eval rescore` its implied item is set true even where the answer gave false, as 0037 does (diff review B2; counted in `rescored_from.items_raised`). A `--no-new-wording` run (the frozen v2.0.0 text, no items) plans on its answer with the items derived (`evalrun.planned_view`): the fixed rules no longer read the removed values, so without them its `vendor_change_request` would miss the fraud guard (judgment call, raise-only; scored as asked).

```yaml
version: 3
fields:
  category:
    type: enum
    description: "What this email is primarily about. A fake email gets the value of what it pretends to be (a fake invoice is an invoice). When several fit, choose in this order: a sign-in or security alert; money (a bill to pay, then a payment made or received, then an account or policy we hold); then what the email is about; a plain notice, a personal note or none of these last."
    values:
      invoice:               "Asks us to pay: a bill, invoice, overdue reminder or renewal (business or personal)."
      payment_confirmation:  "Confirms money we paid: a receipt, order confirmation or 'payment received' from someone we pay."
      remittance:            "Tells us money is coming to us: remittance advice, a customer's 'we've paid', a refund or payout."
      billing_inquiry:       Question or dispute about a charge, invoice or balance.
      customer_request:      Customer asking for help, service or information that isn't about a charge, a defect or buying.
      sales_inquiry:         Someone asking about buying from us or about our prices.
      partnership:           "One-to-one proposal to work together: a pitch, an offer, a collaboration."
      bug_report:            Reports a bug, defect, outage or incident.
      marketing:             "Sent to many: newsletters, promotions, advertising, and other unsolicited bulk mail."
      notification:          Informs only, and fits no other value.
      action_alert:          "Machine or service asking someone to act on a system, not on account access: expiring certificate or domain, quota reached, backup or job failed."
      account_security:      "Sign-in alert, password reset, verification code, or security warning about an account, genuine or fake."
      shipping:              "About a delivery: tracking, delivered, missed, returns."
      appointment:           Meeting or service booking, or a reminder for one (dentist, salon, restaurant, car service).
      travel:                "Flights, trains, hotels or rental cars: itineraries, tickets, check-in, changes."
      finance:               "About an account or policy we hold, asking for no payment: statements, balances, interest or dividends, rate or policy changes, tax forms, beneficiary reviews."
      school_or_family:      School, childcare, activities or family logistics (pickups, schedules, who does what).
      private:               Personal note from a person, not about the business, that fits no other value.
      other:                 None of the above.
  priority:
    type: ordinal
    description: How soon a human should look at this.
    levels:
      low:    "Can wait; nobody needs to see it soon."
      medium: Look at it within a working day.
      high:   Look at it today.
      urgent: "Needs attention within hours: a deadline today, an outage, or money or access at risk."
  requires_action:
    type: boolean
    description: Someone on our side must do something.
  requires_reply:
    type: boolean
    description: The sender expects a written reply from us.
  payment_related:
    type: boolean
    description: Money moving or owed (a payment sent, received or requested, an amount owed, or payment instructions); not a question about prices, plans or quotes.
  deadline_mentioned:
    type: boolean
    description: States or implies a specific due date or time limit.
  sender_type:
    type: enum
    description: The sender's apparent role toward us, judged from content. (Whether they are internal or external is computed, not judged.)
    values:
      vendor:    Someone we buy from or who serves us (personally or for the organization), includes notices about accounts, bookings or orders.
      customer:  Someone we sell to or serve.
      regulator: Government agency or regulatory body.
      company:   Firms we don't buy from, including cold pitches and (potential) partners.
      friend:    Someone we know personally.
      family:    Relative.
      person:    Someone we do not know very well (if at all).
      automated: Machine or service reporting monitored systems information (backups, HPC jobs, etc.).
      unknown:   "Can't tell the role, or a colleague or co-worker of ours, genuine or not. Otherwise an impostor takes the role they claim."
  fraud_risk:
    type: ordinal
    description: Likelihood that this email is fraud or impersonation.
    levels:
      none:   Ordinary mail, including genuine service notices that ask for nothing.
      low:    Any doubt about the email, short of medium.
      medium: Any request to move money, data, credentials or access on this email's say-so, whatever the pattern. A request to call a number or follow a link to secure an account counts too.
      high:   Known fraud pattern, for example changed bank details, gift cards, employee tax or payroll data, credentials, or someone posing as a colleague or executive.
  bank_detail_change:
    type: boolean
    description: Says the bank account, payee or check address that money goes to or comes from has changed, asks us to update it, or asks us to switch from bank transfer or check to another method. Yes even when the email is also an invoice, a lure or a statement.
  regulator_claim:
    type: boolean
    description: Comes from, or claims to come from, a regulator, government agency, court or tax authority acting toward us (a notice, audit, inquiry or filing demand), genuine or not. No for an email that only mentions one, such as a newsletter.
  phishing:
    type: boolean
    description: "An attempt to deceive us: the sender or the premise is false. For example a fake invoice, notice or alert; a fake security or sign-in alert; someone posing as a colleague, executive, relative or company we know; a request to change where money is sent; or an extortion threat. It often asks for a code, password, payment, or personal, staff or bank details, or asks us to click to verify or call a number. No when a genuine sender asks for these through their real channel, and no for plain unsolicited marketing. Instructions aimed at an automated assistant don't by themselves make an email phishing."
  claims_internal:
    type: boolean
    description: Presents itself as from a colleague, co-worker or executive of our organization, genuine or not. (Whether the sender really is internal is computed, not judged.)
  private_individual:
    type: boolean
    description: "A private person writing for themselves from a personal address, not on behalf of an organization: a friend, a relative, or someone we don't know."
```

**What changed from v2:**
- Five yes/no fixed safety items, after v2's fields so the text Claude is given keeps v2's order. Each carries what a v2 value carried (the table below); they are asked as their own questions so that, from stage S3, ecf's safety rules can read them instead of `category` and `sender_type`.
- `priority` keeps its four levels and gains a text for each.
- Every other field and value, and their wording, are v2's. The safety core (`SAFETY_FIELDS`) adds the five items; `SAFETY_VALUES` is unchanged until S3. (S3b: four values removed and four texts reworded, `SAFETY_VALUES` removed; above.)
- **Who is asked what:** Claude (preset C, and D's actor; D held back from v3.0.0, OD-516) gets schema v3 (`config.current_schema`); Jev gets v3's questions (§7.9). Until v3.0.0 the local model (presets A and B, and C's local fallback) was asked **schema v2** (`ecf.schema.local_schema`, P6) with the five items derived from its answer (`ecf.schema.with_fixed`), so its gate key didn't move; A, B, the fallback and `local_schema` are removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031). Schema v3 started the gate again for C addresses (their key holds the schema digest), and the new `fixed_labels.jsonl` changed the synthetic set's version (§16.1).
- **The table** (`ecf.schema.FIXED_FROM_V2`; schema doc §9): `category: vendor_change_request` → `bank_detail_change`; `category: regulatory` or `sender_type: regulator` → `regulator_claim`; `category: spam_or_phishing` → `phishing`; `sender_type: team` (v1 `staff`) → `claims_internal`; `sender_type: person`, `friend` or `family` → `private_individual`; anything else false. Used by preset A's answers (until v3.0.0), migration 0036 (stored classifications, §11.9) and `ecf eval rescore` (a v2 result's answers), and, more strictly, by the eval labels (§16.1). From S3b the table is how a v2 answer gets its items before `from_v2` reads its removed values; `fixed_item` reads only its kept rows (`sender_type` `regulator`, `person`, `friend`, `family`).

**Schema v2** (`v2.0.0` to `v2.2.3`; 2026-10-08, OD-475): enum, ordinal and boolean fields only. Schema v2 serves work and personal mail alike (operator decision 2026-10-08, OD-475; plan `planning-docs/SCHEMA-V2-PLAN.md`), so an install that watches both kinds of address needs nothing special. It shipped in `v2.0.0` and replaced v1, which stays loadable for results and labels made before it (`ecf.schema.load_schema_v1`); from v3 it stays loadable too (`ecf.schema.load_schema_v2`) for old results and labels; the local model, which was asked it, is removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031).

```yaml
version: 2
fields:
  category:
    type: enum
    description: "What this email is primarily about. Pick the first that fits: vendor_change_request, regulatory, spam_or_phishing, account_security; then what the email is about (money: invoice, then payment_confirmation or remittance, then finance); notification, private and other last."
    values:
      invoice:               "Asks us to pay: a bill, invoice, overdue reminder or renewal (business or personal)."
      payment_confirmation:  "Confirms money we paid: a receipt, order confirmation or 'payment received' from someone we pay."
      remittance:            "Tells us money is coming to us: remittance advice, a customer's 'we've paid', a refund or payout."
      vendor_change_request: Says the bank account, payee or check address that money goes to or comes from has changed, or asks us to update it, or to switch from bank transfer or check to another method. Takes precedence over every other value, even when the email is also an invoice, a lure or a statement.
      billing_inquiry:       Question or dispute about a charge, invoice or balance.
      customer_request:      Customer asking for help, service or information that isn't about a charge, a defect or buying.
      sales_inquiry:         Someone asking about buying from us or about our prices.
      partnership:           "One-to-one proposal to work together: a pitch, an offer, a collaboration."
      bug_report:            Reports a bug, defect, outage or incident.
      regulatory:            Regulator, government agency, court or tax authority acting toward us (notice, audit, inquiry, filing demand), or someone claiming to be one.
      marketing:             "Sent to many: newsletters, promotions, advertising."
      notification:          Informs only, and fits no other value.
      action_alert:          "Machine or service asking someone to act on a system, not on account access: expiring certificate or domain, quota reached, backup or job failed."
      account_security:      "Sign-in alert, password reset, verification code, or security warning from a service we use, that asks for nothing beyond signing in as usual. One that asks you to send a code or password, click to verify, or call a number is spam_or_phishing."
      shipping:              "About a delivery: tracking, delivered, missed, returns."
      appointment:           Meeting or service booking, or a reminder for one (dentist, salon, restaurant, car service).
      travel:                "Flights, trains, hotels or rental cars: itineraries, tickets, check-in, changes."
      finance:               "About an account or policy we hold, asking for no payment: statements, balances, interest or dividends, rate or policy changes, tax forms, beneficiary reviews."
      school_or_family:      School, childcare, activities or family logistics (pickups, schedules, who does what).
      spam_or_phishing:      Unsolicited junk or an attempt to deceive, including a fake invoice, notice or alert, and a fake security or sign-in alert.
      private:               Personal note from a person, not about the business, that fits no other value.
      other:                 None of the above.
  priority:
    type: ordinal
    levels: [low, medium, high, urgent]
    description: How soon a human should look at this.
  requires_action:
    type: boolean
    description: Someone on our side must do something.
  requires_reply:
    type: boolean
    description: The sender expects a written reply from us.
  payment_related:
    type: boolean
    description: Money moving or owed (a payment sent, received or requested, an amount owed, or payment instructions); not a question about prices, plans or quotes.
  deadline_mentioned:
    type: boolean
    description: States or implies a specific due date or time limit.
  sender_type:
    type: enum
    description: The sender's apparent role toward us, judged from content. (Whether they are internal or external is computed, not judged.)
    values:
      vendor:    Someone we buy from or who serves us (personally or for the organization), includes notices about accounts, bookings or orders.
      customer:  Someone we sell to or serve.
      regulator: Government agency or regulatory body.
      team:      Colleague or co-worker acting on behalf of the organization.
      company:   Firms we don't buy from, including cold pitches and (potential) partners.
      friend:    Someone we know personally.
      family:    Relative.
      person:    Someone we do not know very well (if at all).
      automated: Machine or service reporting monitored systems information (backups, HPC jobs, etc.).
      unknown:   Can't tell the role (an impostor takes the role they claim).
  fraud_risk:
    type: ordinal
    description: Likelihood that this email is fraud or impersonation.
    levels:
      none:   Ordinary mail, including genuine service notices that ask for nothing.
      low:    Any doubt about the email, short of medium.
      medium: Any request to move money, data, credentials or access on this email's say-so, whatever the pattern.
      high:   Known fraud pattern, for example changed bank details, gift cards, employee tax or payroll data, credentials, or someone posing as a colleague or executive.
```

**What changed from v1:**
- `category` gains six values for personal mail: `account_security`, `shipping`, `appointment`, `travel`, `finance`, `school_or_family`. `invoice` (personal bills), `payment_confirmation` (receipts and orders), `vendor_change_request` (an account's bank or login details, or sending money a new way) and `regulatory` (government agencies, courts, tax authorities) are widened; `notification` is reworded so it no longer overlaps the new values; `action_alert` no longer lists security warnings (now `account_security`). `notification` and `action_alert` stay separate, so an action alert is still never hidden (OD-472).
- `sender_type`: `staff` is renamed `team`; `company`, `friend`, `family` and `person` are added.
- `fraud_risk` keeps its four levels and every other field is unchanged (the Phase R review showed dropping `none` would widen automatic hiding).
- **Safety core** (`ecf.schema.SAFETY_FIELDS`, `SAFETY_VALUES`; the loader refuses a shipped schema without it): the fields `fraud_risk`, `payment_related`, `priority`, `requires_action`, `requires_reply` and `deadline_mentioned` with their v1 kinds and levels, and the values `regulatory`, `vendor_change_request`, `spam_or_phishing`, `notification`, `action_alert` (category) and `team` (sender_type). (`SAFETY_VALUES` removed in v3.0.0 S3b, OD-500, §7.1.)
- A rules file written for v1 still applies: the rules compiler reads `staff` as `team` and names the rules that did (`rules.V1_ALIASES`); stored rules are never rewritten. Since v3.0.0 (S3a, 2026-10-13, merged fb49b30; OD-500; `planning-docs/S3-READERS-SWITCH.md` draft 2), a condition on `team` (or `staff`) is refused, with `claims_internal: true` as its replacement; and applied rules copied from the v2 starter rules are converted once (§8.6).
- Reworded after the first v2 eval (operator decision 2026-10-08, part of OD-475): `account_security` covers only alerts that ask for nothing beyond signing in as usual, and one asking to send a code or password, click to verify or call a number is `spam_or_phishing`, which now names fake security and sign-in alerts; `school_or_family` covers arranging family logistics, and a relative's note that only shares news or thanks is `private` (§21.2).
- `account_security` back to the `v2.0.0` text (operator decision 2026-10-11, after classifier plan stage 1, §21.2): item 2's "about access to an account ... may ask you to review or change something in the account itself" let the local model file phishing posing as an account alert as `account_security` (with `fraud_risk` high); the `v2.0.0` clause "asks for nothing beyond signing in as usual" is restored, the rest of item 2's texts stay. Prompt digest `66f9f63c`, schema digest `schema-0d96e766c568d58a`. The labelling text (§16.1) is unchanged.
- `school_or_family` stays one category, not split into school and family (operator decision 2026-10-08): both get the same starter rule (label, flag on a deadline, actor if a reply is needed), fewer categories help the local model, and the sender is already in `sender_type` (`family`). Known cost: 2 synthetic cards of family news (`home-family-note`, `home-giftcard-thanks`) are classed `school_or_family` where the label says `private` (§21.2). Revisit only with a schema change.

**Schema v1** (`v1.0.0`; changed 2026-10-07, OD-472):

```yaml
version: 1
fields:
  category:
    type: enum
    description: What this email is primarily about.
    values:
      invoice:               Bill or invoice requesting payment from us.
      payment_confirmation:  Confirmation that a payment was sent or received.
      remittance:            Remittance advice or payment details from a customer.
      vendor_change_request: Request to change a vendor's bank, payment, or contact details.
      billing_inquiry:       Question or dispute about a charge, invoice, or account balance.
      customer_request:      Customer asking for help, service, or information.
      sales_inquiry:         Prospective customer asking about buying or pricing.
      partnership:           Partnership proposals, vendor pitches, collaboration.
      bug_report:            Report of a bug, defect, outage, or incident.
      regulatory:            Anything involving a regulator or regulation (e.g. FDA, SEC, FTC, IRS, state agencies, compliance notices, audits, filings).
      marketing:             Newsletters, promotions, cold outreach, advertising.
      notification:          Automated messages that only inform (receipts, shipping, account activity).
      action_alert:          Automated alert from a service we use that asks someone to act (expiring certificate or domain, security warning, quota reached, backup failed).
      spam_or_phishing:      Unsolicited junk or an attempt to deceive, including fake alerts that push you to a link or a payment.
      private:               Personal correspondence from a person, not about the business, that fits no other value.
      other:                 None of the above.
  priority:
    type: ordinal
    levels: [low, medium, high, urgent]
    description: How soon a human should look at this.
  requires_action:
    type: boolean
    description: Someone on our side must do something.
  requires_reply:
    type: boolean
    description: The sender expects a written reply from us.
  payment_related:
    type: boolean
    description: Money moving or owed (a payment sent, received or requested, an amount owed, or payment instructions); not a question about prices, plans or quotes.
  deadline_mentioned:
    type: boolean
    description: States or implies a specific due date or time limit.
  sender_type:
    type: enum
    description: The sender's apparent role toward us, judged from content. (Whether they are internal or external is computed, not judged.)
    values:
      vendor:     Supplier or service provider.
      customer:   Someone we sell to or serve.
      regulator:  Government agency or regulatory body.
      staff:      Colleague acting in an internal role.
      automated:  System or no-reply sender.
      unknown:    Cannot tell.
  fraud_risk:
    type: ordinal
    levels: [none, low, medium, high]
    description: >
      Likelihood of fraud or impersonation (changed bank details, unusual urgency,
      pressure to bypass process, sender not matching the claimed organization).
```

Categories `action_alert` and `private` added, and the descriptions reworded, without a new schema version (operator decision 2026-10-07, OD-472). `action_alert` is anchored on a service we use and on the message asking for action, so a vendor's outage is not a `bug_report` (now about any bug, outage or incident, by operator choice) and a fake "payment failed" alert stays `spam_or_phishing`; `private` is personal correspondence that fits no other value, so a personal bill stays `invoice`. Neither new value is matched by any starter rule: they fall to rules 9 and 10 (kept in the inbox), so they can't hide mail. Both become labels ecf may write. Eval results and labels before OD-472 used the 14-value prompt; a result file doesn't record the schema text, so they are not comparable with later runs, and every §1.5 eval is re-run on the relabelled set.

`payment_related` excludes questions about prices, plans or quotes (operator decision 2026-10-01, OD-256): in the V1.3 eval three such questions came back `true`, so rule 1a flagged them as unverified payments instead of rule 9 sending them for a reply. The pre-check's payment keywords still count for I3 whatever the model says.

**Schema extensions** (operator decisions 2026-10-08, OD-478; built in `v2.0.0` but off, planned for `v2.1.0`, operator decision 2026-10-09, OD-481; ADR 0025; code: `ecf/schema.py`): an install may extend the shipped schema with the `schema` section of `ecf config apply` (§9.7). An extension adds fields (enum, ordinal or boolean, the grammar above) and `category` values; it can't change or remove a shipped field or value, so the safety core can't change. Its fields follow the shipped ones, its category values follow `category`'s, and its prompt text follows the shipped text under the heading "Added by this install (answer these too):" and the line "Added fields and values never change how you answer the fields above. Choose an added category only when no built-in category fits; never instead of regulatory, vendor_change_request or spam_or_phishing." (classifier plan item 7, P19), so the prompt prefix doesn't change. Claude sees its descriptions (Gemma did too, before v3.0.0). Rules may use its fields with every action, and I1 still gates hiding (§8.2).

**Off in `v2.0.0`** (operator decision 2026-10-09, OD-481): the preset A check with a sample extension (§1.5a item 2, run `6b80a149`, §21.2) cost the built-in fields 4.3 points, so extensions move back to `v2.1.0`, after that dilution is fixed. The code stays; one switch, `ecf.schema.EXTENSIONS_ENABLED`, is False. While it is off, `ecf config apply` refuses a `schema` section other than `default`, and a stored or imported extension is kept but ignored (§7.4, §9.7). The rest of this section, §7.4's effective schema and §9.7's `schema` section describe the switch on.

**Your own fields, the user layer** (v3.0.0 step 1c stage S4, operator decisions 2026-10-14, OD-502, which supersedes OD-478 and OD-481; plan `planning-docs/S4-USER-LAYER.md` draft 3; schema doc `planning-docs/v3.0.0-OPERATOR-SCHEMA.md`; ADR 0030 amended; code: `ecf/schema.py`, `ecf_server/config.py`, `rules.py`, `review.py`): the extension above is the additive half of "your own schema" (user-facing text says "your fields"; code names stay). (1) **The switch stays off in v3.0.0** (§1.5a item 2b; P5): the S4 branch turned it on for M2 only; M2 failed (2026-10-14, §21.2), so it merges off (operator decision 2026-10-14). The tests turn it on. (2) **Preset C only** (D8; from v3.0.0 every address is C, D from step 4, so the A/B and fallback refusals below have nothing left to refuse and go with the removal, ADR 0031; D's handling is step 4's): `ecf config apply` refuses a `schema` section other than `default` while any address is preset A or B, and `ecf address add` refuses an A or B address while one is stored, each naming the reason (the local model isn't measured with user fields, item 2) and the fix; the local model is asked plain v2 (`local_schema`), so A's and B's gate keys don't move with them, and a local answer is checked against the schema without them (`without_extension`; a rule reads them as unknown). `claude_queue_timeout` can't be turned on for a C address (operator decision 2026-10-14; C is Claude-only, PLANNING §2; step 4 removes C's fallback). (3) **No stored-but-ignored copy** (P11): import and restore drop a bundle's `schema`, and with it the applied rules that read its fields or added values (diff review R1: otherwise the rules wouldn't compile and the bundle would be refused, so a C install's backup couldn't be restored); everything else imports as before, and the output names the fields and the rules left out, with their count (into an A/B install with the reason; into a C-only one "re-apply your config file (fields and rules) with ecf config apply"). (4) **Caps unchanged for C** (D7): per classify read today 7,663 bytes of schema (5,999 text + 1,664 JSON schema); at the caps about 13 KB (measured 2026-10-14); `ecf config apply` and `ecf doctor` print the bytes per read (P16). The 16 KB budget and P11's once-per-spawn delivery are step 3's. (5) **Unknown handling** for every field ecf doesn't fix (P14; §8.6). (6) **`priority` is fixed for good** (D12): the fixed fields are the 11 of `ecf.schema.FIXED_FIELDS` (the safety set, `priority`, the workflow fields); the replaceable default fields are `category` and `sender_type`, only added to in S4 (value replacement and default-off are S4b, after v3.0.0, D1).

Content rules added in S4: a description on every field, value and level (an ordinal's `levels` must be a mapping of level to text; a list is refused, R10; the shipped v3 has one on each, tested); an enum user field without a catch-all (`other`, `unknown` or `none`) warns, and a user field may reuse those three although another field has them (two user fields may both have `other`; D15, P12); added `category` values still need new names; a `{label: {field: x}}` rule is refused at apply on a user field whose values repeat another field's value or a label name (`policy.labels` makes them keywords, P12); a description that writes one of the 11 fixed field names as a field name is refused, listing the names: a name with an underscore (`fraud_risk`, `bank_detail_change`) wherever it stands as a word, a one-word name (`priority`, `phishing`) only as an identifier: in backticks; maybe quoted, marked up or bracketed (`"phishing"`, `'priority'`, `**priority**`) and followed by `:`, `=`, `->`, `=>`, an arrow or a full-width colon (review R2); after `set`; or followed, after any of those, by one of the field's values (`phishing true`, `priority (high)`); case is ignored (`ecf.schema.fixed_as_field`, operator decision 2026-10-14 narrowing P10). The same words in plain English ("a high priority customer", "phishing attempts") warn, as does naming `category`, `sender_type` or another user field (D9b); values aren't checked, being common words; §12.1); an added value can't take the name of a built-in label or of a fixed, default or applied rule id, always (P2, C8), nor of a field: ecf's 13 (`FIXED_FIELDS`, `category`, `sender_type`) or the user's own (review R7); descriptions are printable ASCII (review R2: no look-alike letters or full-width marks).

| Cap | Limit |
|---|---|
| Fields | 8 |
| Values or levels per field | 16 |
| Added `category` values | 4 (22 + 4 = 26) |
| Description, per field or value | 180 characters |
| The extension's prompt text | 4,000 characters |

Content rules: names match the field and value patterns; descriptions are one line of printable text (no line breaks, control or format characters), not starting with `-` or `:`; an added enum or `category` value can't equal any enum value of any field (shipped or added), a built-in label (`policy.BUILTIN_LABELS`) or a rule ID in force, since it may become a label; an added ordinal's `levels` are a mapping of each level to its text (as Level texts below; classifier plan item 7; a list was accepted before S4, R10), each text following the description rules and counting in the 4,000 characters; ordinal levels are unique (they never become labels, so `none` or `high` may repeat another field's level); `rule` and `safety` are reserved field names (eval results keep them beside the fields). Every bad value name, level and description is listed, not only the first. Only `schema: default` means "no extension": `{}`, `[]`, `""`, `0`, `false` and `null` are checked and refused. The extension keeps the operator's order of fields and values (it is the prompt's order): it is stored, cached and compared in that order, so a reorder is a change with its own digest. A file over a cap is refused before step-up with every violation listed (`schema_limit`, §15.3), e.g. `schema: 9 fields, limit 8`, `schema.fields.contract_stage: 18 values, limit 16`, `schema: extension text 4,612 characters, limit 4,000; shorten descriptions or remove a field`; any other problem is `invalid_input`, also listing every one. The caps are fixed in code (`ecf.schema.MAX_EXT_*`). Whether the worst-case prompt with a full extension fits Gemma's context: by the §21.2 token counts (rare CJK 3,816 + v2 about 170 + a maximal extension about 770, about 4,760) it fits `num_ctx` 6,144 (OD-477), but no run has used a full extension: unverified, and moot from v3.0.0 (Gemma removed, ADR 0031).

### 7.2 Computed facts (service only; never taken from a model; sent to one only by exemption)

| Fact | Definition |
|---|---|
| `sender_origin` | `internal` only if `auth_result = pass` **and** the From address is in the internal set: its normalized domain in `org_domains`, or the address exactly in `org_addresses` (no Gmail folding; V1.6, OD-431, OD-432); else `external`. With no internal set it is always `external`. |
| `auth_result` | ecf's own DMARC evaluation (§7.3): `pass` (aligned, valid DKIM), `fail` (more than one From header, or every aligned signature broken under an enforcing policy; OD-192), otherwise `none`. Provider Authentication-Results are never used. Messages over `max_message_bytes` are always `none`. |
| `sender_seen_before` | a human-confirmed category for this sender at this address, **or** at least 3 earlier DMARC-pass messages spread over 14 days or more (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-043). For bank-detail triggers only a human-confirmed category counts (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-044). Senders on the shipped shared-platform list (invoicing, e-signature, payment-notification services) never count as seen. The list (initial list OD-158; finalized 2026-09-29, operator decision, OD-197) holds each vendor's sending domains, researched 2026-09-29: verified on the vendor's own page: `intuit.com` (`quickbooks@notification.intuit.com`, quickbooks.intuit.com help), `freshbooks.com` (support.freshbooks.com), `stripe.com` (docs.stripe.com), `squareup.com` (squareup.com help), `hellosign.com` (`noreply@mail.hellosign.com`, help.dropbox.com), `pandadoc.net`, `pandadoc.email`, `getpandadoc.com` (support.pandadoc.com), `zohoinvoice.com` (fallback sender; zoho.com help); on the vendor's page as summarised by a search engine, the page itself not loadable (unverified): `docusign.net`, `echosign.com`, `adobesign.com` (Adobe Sign's newer sender), `bill.com`, `waveapps.com`; third-party or user-forum sources only (unverified): `xero.com` (`post.xero.com`), `paypal.com`. `quickbooks.com` was removed (no source shows it as a sender). Stripe, PandaDoc, Zoho Invoice and Tipalti can also send from the customer's own domain, which no list can recognise. Not listed yet (proposed in SPEC, pending further research): `coupahost.com`, `meliopayments.com`, `tipalti.com` (third-party sources only); SAP Ariba, Wise, Venmo, GoCardless, Gusto, ADP, Paychex (no sending domain found); `dropboxsign.com` (not a sender). |
| `reply_to_mismatch` | Reply-To domain differs from the From domain, unless it matches the sender's recorded expected Reply-To (`ecf sender set-reply-to`) |
| `sender_verified` | the sender is human-verified for rule 1a (`ecf sender set-verified`, OD-065); turns off only the `unverified_payment` trigger and rule 1a (V1.2 step 10c) |
| `recipient_mismatch` | the monitored address is not in To or Cc (replayed signed mail) |
| `bulk_signal` | `List-Id` or `List-Unsubscribe`, `Auto-Submitted` not `no`, a no-reply sender, `Precedence: bulk|list|junk`, `X-Autoreply`, or an empty Return-Path. Counts toward hide corroboration only when `auth_result = pass` and the sender is not first-time (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-045). |
| `content_unscanned` | message over `max_message_bytes`; a text part over `max_scan_bytes_per_part`; more than 24 MiB of text in the message, or more than 256 IBAN-like numbers in one text with none valid (§8.5, v2.1.0), or more than 4,096 heads of a listed country tried in full (v2.2.2); attachments on a payment-keyword item; a document attachment from a first-time sender; any attachment on a `high` address |
| `payment_keyword` | a payment keyword (`keywords.yaml`) in the subject or text (§8.5); rules may read it since V1.3 (OD-262) |
| `gift_card_keyword` | a gift-card term (`keywords.yaml` `gift_card`) in the subject or text; money only for impersonation (V1.6, OD-457) |
| `bec_opener` | at least two different phrases from `keywords.yaml` `bec_opener` in the text the triggers read (§8.5): the opening message of an executive-impersonation scam, before any money is named (operator decision 2026-10-08, OD-479) |
| `tax_form_request` | a phrase from `keywords.yaml` `tax_form` (W-2, wage and tax statements, payroll records, pay stubs) and one from `data_request` (send me, send them to this address, as one PDF) in the text the triggers read (§8.5): a request for employee tax or payroll data, the W-2 scam (operator decision 2026-10-09, OD-482) |
| `sender_hash` | SHA-256 of the lower-cased From address: the key of the `senders` table, used to find a confirmed category (V1.3, §7.4b); never shown or sent anywhere |
| `from_org_address` | the From address is in `org_addresses`, exactly or after Gmail folding (V1.6, below) |
| `impersonates_internal` | the sender isn't internal by `from_org_domain` or `from_org_address` but claims to be someone in the internal set (V1.6; §8.5 trigger 7) |
| `self_sent` | on Gmail only, the From address is the watched address and Gmail labels the message `\Sent` (V1.6, OD-446, below) |
| `known_sender_auth_regressed` | the sender has enough DMARC-pass history (OD-043's 3 passes over 14 days; a confirmed category alone doesn't count; never on a shared platform) and this message's `auth_result` is `fail`; `none` doesn't count (forwarding, lists and late verification give it to known senders). A fraud reason (§8.5, OD-490). In the eval it is recomputed from a card's expected `sender_seen_before` and `auth_result`. Not readable by rules in v2.1.0 (R3-P15). |
| `risky_attachment` | an attachment that runs or renders as a page when opened: HTML and web archives, SVG, HTA, scripts, shortcuts, executables, disk images (`keywords.yaml` `risky_attachment`), by the extension of its whole name or its content type, so `application/octet-stream` with such an extension counts; unnamed inline parts don't count. A hide blocker (§7.6 I1); with a payment, credential or gift-card keyword, a `fraud_weak` reason (§8.5). Not readable by rules in v2.1.0 (R3-P15). |
| `link_count` | links in the text parts: anchors with an href in HTML, `http(s)://` URLs in plain text; saturates at 500. Recorded for measurement only. |
| `link_text_mismatch` | a visible HTML anchor's text names a site (a URL, a `www.` name, or a bare domain with a common top-level domain) other than its href's (both reduced to an approximate registrable domain; no public-suffix list). Recorded for measurement only: not a hide blocker, since tracking redirects would make most newsletters mismatch (P13). |
| `amount_mentioned` | a money amount in the text: a currency sign or code (`$ € £ ¥ ₹`, USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD, NZD, CHF, JPY, INR, USDC, USDT) next to a digit on either side, "dollars" or "euros" after one, or a bare number with two decimals (`1,180.00`; not `9.50%`, `1.0000` or a dotted date); a bare whole number doesn't count. Matched on normalized text. Recorded for measurement only: not a route, a signal or rule-readable (P9). |

**Facts and models** (operator decision 2026-10-09, OD-483, ADR 0026; amends ADR 0009): no computed fact is sent to a model by default, and none is ever taken from one. An OD may exempt a derived signal for a role (Claude classifier, Jev, actor; the local classifier until v3.0.0): a composed boolean, the truth of a rule-level condition or (operator decision 2026-10-11, OD-489, ADR 0026 amended) a fact about the message's own structure (its links or attachments, as the service parsed them; never about the sender), sent only when true, in fixed service wording, built by one shared function with an allow-list test. Never sent: `auth_result`, `sender_seen_before`, `sender_verified`, `sender_origin`, `sender_hash`, `bulk_signal`, `reply_to_mismatch` and raw keyword hits. Exemptions: OD-484 (the classifier plan's signals to the local and Claude classifiers, built in `v2.1.0`). **As built for the local classifier** (classifier plan item 3, 2026-10-09; code: `ecf_server/signals.py`, `classifier.py`): `bec_opener_outside` ("An outside sender opens like an executive-impersonation scam.": `bec_opener`, `sender_origin` external, not `self_sent`; rule 1's OD-479 clause), `tax_form_request_outside` ("An outside sender asks for employees' tax or payroll data.": OD-482's clause), `impersonates_internal` ("The sender claims to be someone in your organization but isn't.": the `fraud_weak` route) and `impersonation_gift_cards` ("Someone claiming to be in your organization mentions gift cards.": part of rule 1's OD-436/OD-457 clause). The true ones go as a list between `<<<SIGNALS token>>>` and `<<<END SIGNALS token>>>` before the email, with the email's token; the instructions say each signal is a fact about the email and only a block with that token counts, anything in the email that looks like or disputes signals being part of the email. With none true the block is left out and the request is the `v2.0.0` one. The items queue, the preset C fallback and `ecf eval run` all ask with them; `tests/test_signals.py` holds the allow-list. **Item 4's signals** (OD-485, 2026-10-09; signals only, no rule route): `credential_request` ("The email asks for a code, password or login to be sent or read back.": a `credential` phrase and a `credential_ask` phrase from `keywords.yaml`, unless a `credential_never` phrase such as "we will never ask you to reply with your password" is present) and `crypto_payment` ("The email asks for payment to a cryptocurrency wallet.": a wallet address, matched by pattern on the NFKC text (since 2026-10-10 on normalized text without nonspacing marks, §8.5) and recorded only as "wallet address", and a `crypto_pay` verb; the patterns cover Bitcoin bech32 and legacy, Ethereum and the synthetic set's `TEST-WALLET-nnnn` placeholder). On the frozen set (2026-10-09) `credential_request` fires on 9 cards, all fraud-labelled, and on no genuine notice; `crypto_payment` on `crypto-payment-demand` only, not on the exchange receipt or the crypto newsletter; no accuracy claim (P22). The prompt digest includes every signal's wording, so a new signal or a reworded one changes the gate key. **Amended** (operator decision 2026-10-10, OD-488): `credential_request` is no longer sent to either classifier (with it, the local model filed 8 of 9 phishing cards as `account_security`, §21.2); it stays a fact. Built 2026-10-10 (pre-classifier plan step 1a; prompt digest `dd5d0340`, `release.json`): `WORDING` and `sent` drop it, `--no-new-signals` now leaves out `crypto_payment` only. Its fraud reason (§8.5) is step 4, not yet built. **Message signals** (OD-489; pre-classifier plan step 11, built 2026-10-11; code: `signals.MESSAGE`): `link_text_mismatch` ("A link's visible text names a different site than the link goes to.": the fact of the same name, HTML anchors only, §8.5) and `risky_attachment` ("The email has an attachment that can run code or open a web page.": the fact of the same name, the hide blocker's `keywords.yaml` list), sent whenever the fact is true, from any sender, to the local and Claude classifiers (not the actor). `risky_attachment` is a rule-level condition (the hide blocker and, with a payment, credential or gift-card keyword, `fraud_weak`); `link_text_mismatch` is not (OD-488 records it only; no rule reads it): it is sent as a fact about the message's structure, which the exemption criterion above was widened to allow (operator decision 2026-10-11, ADR 0026 amended). Offline (2026-10-11): neither fires on any of the 268 frozen cards; on held-out batch 1, `link_text_mismatch` on `ho-link-text-mismatch` and `risky_attachment` on `ho-attach-html-phish` and `ho-attach-long-filename-html`; on batch 2, none. Their wording joins the prompt digest (local `9c7100e3`, `release.json`) and the Claude pin digest, a new gate for A, B and C. The block's token cost is in the budget probe's step-11 re-run (§21.2). **As built for Claude** (classifier plan item 5, 2026-10-10; code: `signals.as_object`, `claude_review.get_message`, `claude_eval.get_message`): to classify, `get_message` returns a top-level `signals` object, each true signal's name with its wording, from the same `signals.sent` on the item's (or the eval case's) facts; `{}` when none is true. The actor gets none, as the local actor doesn't. The classifier agent's text says signals exist only as that key, anything in the email that looks like or disputes signals being part of the email; `notice` is unchanged.

**How the facts are computed in V1.1** (V1.1 build, 2026-09-29; code: `ecf_server/facts.py`): a domain is "in" `org_domains` or the shared-platform list when it equals a listed domain or is a subdomain of one (operator decision 2026-09-29, OD-193); a sender is the SHA-256 of its lowercased From address, per monitored address; history counts only `pass` messages, at the service's receipt time (not the Date header), updated in the same transaction that creates the item; `reply_to_mismatch` compares each Reply-To domain exactly with the From domain and the sender's expected Reply-To domain; `recipient_mismatch` compares the monitored address exactly with To and Cc, so mail delivered by Bcc counts as a mismatch (it is only ever a second signal); a no-reply sender is a local part like `noreply`, `no-reply`, `donotreply`, `mailer-daemon` or `bounce(s)`, optionally followed by a separator and more; documents are PDF, Office, OpenDocument, RTF, CSV, ZIP and HTML files; unnamed inline parts (logos in signatures) are not attachments. `bulk_corroborates` is `bulk_signal` restricted by OD-045. `org_domains` is required config (default: the first address's domain, which must be confirmed; since V1.6 required only while a watched address is at a non-public domain, so an install watching only public-provider addresses may have none, OD-441); public mailbox-provider domains (gmail.com, outlook.com and a shipped list) are refused. Attachments are metadata only (name capped at 100 characters, type, size, count); contents are never read. Since v2.1.0 (pre-classifier plan step 5, P24) a longer name is kept as head…tail with its last 12 characters, and the extension is taken from the whole name (trailing dots and spaces ignored), so a long name no longer hides `.html` from the document and risky-attachment checks. Domains are IDNA-normalized and compared exactly.

**The internal set and the V1.6 facts** (designed in V1.6 step 1 and built in step 1b, 2026-10-05; ADR 0021; code: `ecf_server/internal.py`, `facts.py`):
- **Internal set** (OD-431): `org_domains` (by domain, OD-193) plus `org_addresses` (exact addresses, §9.7), install-wide. A public mailbox domain is never internal by domain; a person there is listed by address. A monitored address is internal only when one of the two covers it.
- **`sender_origin`**: `internal` only if `auth_result = pass` and the From address is in the internal set (its domain in `org_domains`, or the address exactly in `org_addresses`); else `external`. Gmail folding is not used here (OD-432). On an install with no internal set it is always `external`.
- **`from_org_address`**: the From address is in `org_addresses`, exactly or after Gmail folding (a folded match is the same account, OD-432). `from_org_domain` is unchanged.
- **`impersonates_internal`**: the sender isn't internal by `from_org_domain` or `from_org_address`, and the message claims to be someone in the internal set (§8.5 trigger 7, OD-436); a reason goes on the card.
- **`self_sent`** (operator decision 2026-10-05, OD-446): on Gmail only, the From address is the watched address itself and Gmail has the message labelled `\Sent`, read with `X-GM-LABELS` at fetch in Gmail mode (V1.6 step 3, §18); off Gmail it is false. The mailbox, not the message, says so; no sender can set a label in the account. Gmail delivers mail an account sends to itself without a DKIM signature (tested 2026-10-05, §18); a forged copy of your own address carries no `\Sent` label. `auth_result` stays `none`, so such mail never feeds sender history, hide corroboration or own-mail recognition.
- **As built in V1.6** (step 1b, 2026-10-05; code: `ecf_server/internal.py`, `facts.py`, `triggers.py`, `config.py`, `rules.py`, `data/starter_rules.yaml`, `data/keywords.yaml`, `cards.py`): the internal set, the three facts, trigger 6 by address, impersonation (§8.5), rules 1, 1b and 1a (§8.6), the gift-card keywords, `org_addresses` in `ecf config apply` with forward targets and the dialog line (§9.7), and the export data format 2 (OD-442; an older version refuses the bundle). Impersonation compares local parts across providers without dots or a `+tag` on either side, so `pat.lee@outlook.com` matches `patlee@gmail.com`. `address add`, `init` and `doctor` followed in step 2 (§10.2, §13), `self_sent` from Gmail's labels with Gmail mode in step 3 (§18), and `ecf rules test` and the eval with `org_addresses` and card profiles in step 6b (OD-443, §8.6, §16).
- **Gmail folding** (OD-432): for `gmail.com` and `googlemail.com` only: lower-case, `googlemail.com` becomes `gmail.com`, everything from the first `+` dropped, dots in the local part removed. Used for `from_org_address`, duplicate `org_addresses` entries and impersonation; never for `sender_origin`.
- **Why an exact gmail.com address can be internal:** an account sending over SMTP with `From:` another gmail.com address has it rewritten to its own (verified 2026-10-05, V1.6 step 0, §21.1; verified send-as aliases not tested), so a gmail.com From with an aligned `d=gmail.com` pass came from that account. Addresses at other providers may be listed (operator decision 2026-10-05, OD-447), but each is only as strong as its provider's check that a user sends only as themselves, unverified for every provider but Gmail (§12.2); the same already holds for any user within an org domain.

### 7.3 DKIM and DMARC (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-046)

- At fetch time the service verifies every DKIM signature on the raw message (`dkimpy` + `dnspython`), finds the From domain's DMARC record per **RFC 9989** (May 2026; obsoletes RFC 7489 and RFC 9091) using its DNS Tree Walk (no Public Suffix List), applies `p=`/`sp=`/`np=`/`t=` (`pct` removed) and relaxed/strict alignment (verified 2026-09-27, datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc9989). `dkimpy` verifies signatures only; ecf implements the DMARC steps.
- **Recipe:** parse `d=`/`s=` from every signature; prefetch keys on a thread pool into the DNS cache; verify each with `DKIM(msg).verify(idx=i, dnsfunc=…)` through a cache-backed function that accepts a `timeout` keyword (API confirmed in dkimpy's source, verified 2026-09-27); From-aligned signatures first. Ed25519 needs PyNaCl via `dkimpy[ed25519]` (verified 2026-09-27, PyPI).
- **Strictness** (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-047): a signature with `l=` counts as unverified (dkimpy reports it valid; ecf checks the tag). The signature must cover From, Subject, Date, To, and when present Reply-To; otherwise `auth_result = none`. The MIME headers (Content-Type, MIME-Version, Content-Transfer-Encoding; operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-048) are required only for payment and fraud rules (operator decision 2026-09-28, OD-187, narrowing OD-048): when present but unsigned, ecf records `mime_headers_signed = false`, and the item counts as `auth_result = none` for every payment or fraud rule, both when a payment keyword or a deterministic fraud signal is found at fetch and when the classifier later marks it `payment_related`; otherwise it keeps `pass`. Reason: Purelymail signs neither Content-Type nor MIME-Version (real-service test 2026-09-28, §21.1), so the full rule made every internal message trip the org-domain fraud trigger. Extra unsigned copies of any of these headers make it unverified. More than one From header is `fail` and a fraud trigger.
- **DNS:** ordinary DNS (it can be forged on a hostile network; this document owns the limit and SECURITY.md summarizes, operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-049). Results are cached in SQLite across checks, respecting TTLs but capped at 10 minutes (the business-hours check interval; V1.1 review: shorter than a longer interval, so never staler), with negative caching; a TTL of 0 isn't cached (RFC 1035 §3.2.1). Lookups run in parallel with a 1.5 s timeout and 3 s lifetime, within a per-check DNS budget (30 s [proposed]) after which results are `none`; `none` results caused by the budget are retried next check. A message's parallel prefetch asks at most 32 names and each checks the budget. **V1.1 review (2026-09-29):** a DNS error on the way to the DMARC policy (the author's record or the tree walk) gives `none`, not a fall-through to a parent's record, which could swap strict alignment for relaxed (RFC 9989 §4.10.1 leaves DNS errors to the receiver); at most 8 DKIM signatures are checked, those that could align first (RFC 6376 §6.1); a header block dkimpy can't read (a line without a colon, a non-ASCII name) gives `none`, not a crash; a bare CR in the header block gives `none` and fraud trigger 8, since dkimpy splits header lines only at CRLF/LF and Python's parser also at a lone CR, so a signed message could show an unsigned Subject or Reply-To; an internationalized From domain is compared in A-label form. RFC 9989 §3.2.13 defines a non-existent domain by NXDOMAIN only (checked 2026-09-29, rfc-editor.org), so `np=` is applied only then. Encrypted DNS (DoH) to a resolver you choose is to be opt-in (`dns.doh_url`), since it shows every sender domain to that resolver (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-050); not built yet (`ecf settings set` refuses the key).
- **Limits:** SPF can't be evaluated after delivery (a design judgement), so SPF-only senders stay `none`; forwarded and list mail often breaks DKIM (ARC is a later item); a DNS failure yields `none`, never `pass`; mail verified days late (computer off, keys rotated) yields `none`.
- **Evaluation in V1.1** (V1.1 build, 2026-09-29; code: `ecf_server/senderauth.py`): `pass` needs at least one valid, aligned DKIM signature meeting the strictness rules; a DMARC record is not required for `pass` (without one, alignment is exact, or relaxed through the Organizational Domain found by the tree walk). Each signature's outcome is one of `valid`, `bad_signature`, `bad_body_hash`, `no_key`, `bad_key`, `dns_error`, `format`; dkimpy returns False for key and DNS problems, so ecf tells them apart from broken signatures by what its own DNS function saw. **`fail`** (operator decision 2026-09-29, OD-192): more than one From header; or the From domain's effective policy (after `sp`/`np` and `t=y`) is quarantine or reject, signatures aligned with it are present, and every one of them is broken (`bad_signature` or `bad_body_hash` with the key present). A missing aligned signature is never `fail`, because the sender may pass DMARC by SPF, which ecf can't check after delivery. Discovery and Organizational Domains follow RFC 9989 §4.10 (read 2026-09-29, rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9989): the Author Domain first, then a tree walk from the parent, shortened to 7 labels, stopping at `psd=`, discarding names with several records. Checked against public DNS for gmail.com, mail.whitehouse.gov and the operator's test mail subdomain (2026-09-29). The DNS cache caps TTLs at the check interval (600 s by default) and does not cache errors.
- **Results stored and shown on cards:** `dkim_domains_valid`, `dmarc_policy`, `alignment`, `mime_headers_signed` (OD-187).
- **Provider Authentication-Results are not trusted** (`trust_provider_authentication_results: false`, fixed everywhere including dev; reviewer recommendation confirmed by the operator 2026-09-26, OD-051; also OD-017): no provider documents stripping forged ones (G1-32).
- **Health:** `doctor` resolves a known `_dmarc` TXT and a DKIM selector; `[ecf-alert] System Error` ("sender authentication unavailable") when 0 of ≥ 20 signed messages pass in a day. V1.1 shadow reports the share of real payment mail ending at `none` before the header rule is locked in.
- dkimpy's last release was 2024-07-04 (verified 2026-09-27, PyPI): a maintenance risk to watch.
- In dev, OpenDKIM signs synthetic senders so the check runs end to end.

### 7.4 Schema compiler

YAML (`ruamel.yaml`, YAML 1.2, safe loader, duplicate keys rejected) → `CompiledSchema`: a Pydantic model built with `create_model`, enum fields as `Literal[...]` so the JSON schema has no `$ref` (snapshot-tested), ordinal fields keeping level order, a `cast` at the dynamic-model boundary for pyright, and a stable `prompt_block` used as an unchanging prompt prefix. Descriptions go into the prompt and the constraint. Output: the `record_classification` input schema (validated strictly by the service) for Claude; typed questions for Jev (§7.9). Ollama's JSON-schema `format` for the local model is removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031).

**Level texts** (classifier plan item 2, 2026-10-09; code: `ecf/schema.py`): an ordinal's `levels` may be a list or a mapping of each level, in order, to its text; the texts are printed under the field like an enum's values and count in the digest. `fraud_risk` uses it; `priority` kept a list in v2 and has level texts from schema v3.

**Schema v2** (OD-475; code: `ecf/schema.py`): `load_schema()` returns the shipped schema (v2 then; v3 from OD-498, with `load_schema_v2()` for older results), cached, and refuses one without the safety core (`check_safety_core`); `load_schema_v1()` reads v1 for older results and labels. Ordinal levels must be lowercase names and unique (v1 and v2 pass). `CompiledSchema.digest` (`schema-` + 16 hex of SHA-256 over the version and each field's name, kind, description, values and value descriptions in order) names what the models are asked: it is stored in each item's `pinned_models.schema` (the integer `1` before v2) and is part of every gate key (§9.3). `items.schema_version` records the schema an item's classification follows (2 from v2; migration 0034 maps older items).
