**Amounts** (pre-classifier plan step 6, §5 A2, P9; built 2026-10-10; code: `triggers.AMOUNTS`, `triggers.amount`, `scan`'s `amount` entry; tests: `tests/test_triggers.py`, `test_perf.py`): `amount_mentioned` (§7.2) is recorded only; nothing reads it. Its one supporting card in the plan (`mid-giftcard-staff-rewards`) is already routed by `gift_card_codes_request`, so a use waits for held-out and corpus evidence. **Bounds** (§4): four searches, each starting with a fixed character or code so the regex engine skips to it, fixed width or bounded, the bare form never starting inside a number. CPU time on this Mac (2026-10-10), 10 MiB: ordinary text 0.08 s, the worst crafted near miss (spaced digits) 0.53 s; one alternation of the four forms took 0.85 s and 0.30 s. **On the eval cards** (facts only, 2026-10-10), against the `payment_related` label: frozen set 57 true, 2 false (`home-giftcard-balance`, `home-school-newsletter`), 38 missed (mostly whole numbers: "gift cards of 100 each"), plus 5 on cards with no `payment_related` label; held-out batch 1 12/2/5, batch 2 14/2/1 (the 4 false ones are genuine gift-card cards that name a card's value). The plan's evidence pattern (§2) gave 55/3/41 on the frozen set. No other fact, trigger or reason changes.

**Regulator trigger** (separate, so rule 1 doesn't swallow it): agency names and terms; blocks hide actions and routes to rule 2.

**Not in V1.1** (they need V1.5's `sent` table): the second-install exception to trigger 9 (any `X-ECF-Install` header fires it) and loop suppression; both were built in V1.5 (step 3c, above).

**Loop suppression:** auto-replies (`Auto-Submitted`) and bounces (DSNs) that cite an alert-type `sent` entry, in `In-Reply-To`/`References` or in a DSN's returned headers, are labelled and left; no DMARC pass is needed, since bounces are normally unsigned and the random Message-ID they cite is known only to the alert's recipient (operator decision 2026-10-02, OD-330); this runs after rule 1 and suppresses only the alert email, never the fraud label, flag or escalation.

**Model text in Slack** (the actor's question and `reason`) has URLs, phone numbers and email addresses removed, is capped, and is labelled as model output.

### 8.6 Rules

Structured YAML compiled to predicates; no `eval`; validated at load; first match wins unless a rule says `continue`; run by the service (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-064). Rules are security-relevant config applied with `ecf config apply`.

**Grammar [proposed]:**

```yaml
version: 1
rules:
  - id: fraud_guard                      # unique, ^[a-z0-9_]{1,40}$
    when:                                # a condition tree
      or:
        - {field: fraud_risk, in: [medium, high]}
        - {field: category, eq: vendor_change_request}
        - and: [{field: sender_type, eq: team}, {fact: sender_origin, eq: external},
                {or: [{field: payment_related, eq: true}, {fact: payment_keyword, eq: true}]}]  # OD-262
        - and: [{field: payment_related, eq: true}, {fact: auth_result, eq: fail}]
        - {trigger: fraud}               # any deterministic fraud trigger (§8.5 items 1-10)
    then: [{label: suspicious}, flag, escalate]
    actor: none                          # none | continue (hand to the actor after actions)
    hide: never                          # never | corroborated (default corroborated)
```

- Operands: `field:` (schema field), `fact:` (computed fact), `trigger:` (`fraud`, `fraud_weak` (first-time sender + payment keyword without a second signal, a lone Reply-To mismatch on a payment item, a route without a second signal (§8.5), or a risky attachment with a payment, credential or gift-card keyword), `regulator`, `unverified_payment`), `address:` (`sensitivity`).
- Operators (a Pydantic discriminated union; the plan's set, operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-064): `eq`, `in`, `gte` (ordinals by level order, e.g. `{field: priority, gte: high}`), `and`, `or`, `not`. `lte` is added (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-161).
- Actions: vocabulary names from §8.3; `continue` hands the item to the actor after running the listed actions.
- Additions (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-170), needed by the starter rules: an action may carry `if: <condition>` (rules 3, 4); `actor` may be `none`, `continue` or `{continue_if: <condition>}` (rules 3-5); `label` may take its value from an enum field, `{label: {field: category}}` (rule 9); a rule without `when` always matches, and the last rule must be such a catch-all; a `hide: never` rule may not contain hide actions; **rules may only emit `label`, `flag`, `escalate`, `leave`, `mark_read`, `archive`, `move` and `junk`**, so sends and drafts come only from actor proposals, behind approval.
- `ecf rules test <file>` runs a change against the synthetic set locally and shows which outcomes change.
- **As built in V1.2** (step 10b, 2026-09-30; code: `ecf_server/ruletest.py`): `ecf rules test <file> [--cases <folder>] [--all]` (default folder `tests/eval/synthetic`, so it runs from a checkout). For each case in `labels.jsonl` the service analyzes the `.eml` offline, in a scratch in-memory database: a message to `ap@acme.example`, a `standard` address with `org_domains: [acme.example]`, from a first-time sender, with no DNS (so `auth_result` is `none`). The case's expected facts then override the computed ones, and its expected labels stand in for the classifier. Both the rules in force (the applied rules, else the starter rules) and the proposed ones run; the output lists the cases whose outcome (rule, actions, hand-off to the actor) changes, and how many match their expected rule under each. Unbuilt cases (`ecf eval build`) and files over 64 MB are skipped and named. A case over a `standard` address's limit (16 MB) is read as the service reads such a message (§5.1, `fetch._process_partial`): its headers, attachment list and the start of each text part, rebuilt from the file as BODYSTRUCTURE and partial fetches would give them (`mail.fake`; the IMAP fetch itself isn't exercised), with `oversized` and `content_unscanned` set and authentication on the header block only, so never a DKIM pass (`ruletest.read_case`, shared with `ecf eval run` and `/ecf-eval`; 2026-10-10, pre-classifier plan; until then every file over 16 MiB was skipped, and `ecf eval run` skipped it without naming it). Nothing touches the live database, mail, Slack or the network. Because every sender is first-time here, a case whose expected rule assumes a known sender (e.g. an invoice from a regular vendor) matches the weak-fraud rule instead; the comparison between the two rule sets is what counts. The full set took about 25 s per run on the development Mac (measured 2026-09-30), mostly the two large built cases.

**Starter rules:**
1. **Fraud guard:** `fraud_risk ∈ {medium, high}`, `category = vendor_change_request`, `sender_type = team ∧ sender_origin = external` (`staff` in schema v1) about money (`payment_related` or a payment keyword; operator decision 2026-10-01, OD-262), `payment_related ∧ auth_result = fail`, `impersonates_internal` about money (`payment_related`, a payment keyword or a gift-card term; V1.6, OD-436, OD-457), `bec_opener ∧ sender_origin = external` and not `self_sent` (an executive-impersonation opener with no money yet; §8.5, operator decision 2026-10-08, OD-479), `tax_form_request ∧ sender_origin = external` and not `self_sent` (employee tax or payroll data asked to be sent to the writer: the W-2 scam; §8.5, operator decision 2026-10-09, OD-482), or a fraud trigger (not the regulator trigger, not the weak first-time + payment case, which gets `label(suspicious)`, `flag` and a digest section) → `label(suspicious)`, `flag`, `escalate`. Stop: no actor, never hidden.
2. **Regulatory** (category or regulator trigger) → label, flag, escalate. Evaluated right after rule 1, before 1b and 1a (operator decision 2026-10-01, OD-253): in the earlier order a regulator notice that mentioned money from an unsigned or first-time sender matched 1b or 1a first and was only labelled and flagged, never escalated (found by the V1.3 eval: `reg-customer-cfpb-complaint`, `payconf-state-tax-receipt`, `regulator-irs-notice-text`). Such mail now loses the `suspicious` or `unverified_sender` label but keeps the flag and gets the escalation.
1b. **Weak fraud signal** (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-171): the `fraud_weak` trigger (a first-time sender with a payment keyword and no second signal, a lone Reply-To mismatch on a payment item, or since v2.1.0 a route without a second signal or a risky attachment with a payment, credential or gift-card keyword, §8.5), `impersonates_internal` without money (V1.6, OD-436), or `sender_type = team ∧ sender_origin = external` with no money (`staff` in schema v1; OD-262: in the V1.3 closing shadow run a mailing-list email the model called `staff` escalated as fraud; an impersonated colleague asking for money still escalates through rule 1, and one the model rates `medium` or higher does too) → `label(suspicious)`, `flag`; no actor, never hidden; a digest section. Evaluated right after rule 2 (OD-253).
1a. **Unverified payment sender** (all addresses; operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-065): `payment_related ∧ auth_result = none`, not on `self_sent` mail (V1.6, OD-446) → `label(unverified_sender)`, `flag`; no actor, never hidden; a digest section, not a thread each; the email alert fires on `high` addresses only. A per-sender step-up "human-verified" setting (`ecf sender set-verified`) suppresses this rule's flag and email for that sender, leaving fraud triggers on.
3. **Bug report** → label; flag if `priority ≥ high`; escalate if urgent; continue to the actor if `requires_reply`.
4. **Invoice** → label; flag if `deadline_mentioned`; leave; continue to the actor if `requires_reply`.
5a-5d. **Schema v2's personal categories** (operator decision 2026-10-08, OD-475; none of them hides mail; each continues to the actor if `requires_reply`): `account_security` → label, flag; `shipping` → label, leave; `appointment` and `school_or_family` → label, flag if `deadline_mentioned`; `travel` and `finance` → label. They come after rule 5 in the file.
5. **Payment confirmation / remittance** → label; continue to the actor if `requires_reply` (rules 3-5: operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-066; high-risk items still go to the `actor_high` agent).
6. **Phishing** → label, junk (hide corroboration applies).
7. **Marketing ∧ ¬requires_action** → label, archive (corroboration applies).
8. **Notification ∧ automated ∧ ¬requires_action** → label, mark_read, archive (corroboration applies).
9. **requires_reply** → label(category), flag, continue to the actor (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-067).
10. **Otherwise** → actor.

On `high` addresses rules 6-8 default to label + leave.

**Fixed and default rules** (S3a, 2026-10-13, merged fb49b30; OD-500; `planning-docs/S3-READERS-SWITCH.md` draft 2; code: `ecf_server/data/fixed_rules.yaml`, `starter_rules.yaml`, `rules.compose`, `config.convert_rules`): rules 1, 2, 1b, 1a and 6 are **ecf's fixed rules**, in that order (`fraud_guard`, `regulatory`, `fraud_weak`, `unverified_payment_sender`, `phishing`; rule 6 was `spam_or_phishing` until v3.0.0 step 5), in `fixed_rules.yaml`; `starter_rules.yaml` keeps the 11 **default rules** (3, 4, 5, 5a-5d, 7, 8, 9, 10). Every rule set in force is composed by one function, `rules.compose`: the fixed rules, then the applied rules or, with none applied, the default rules, then `otherwise` when the file's last rule has a `when`. `config.current_rules`, the starter rules, `ecf rules test`, `ecf eval run` and the rescores all use it, with the same compiler; `starter_digest` hashes both files. The junk rule moves from 12th to 5th: without its category a phishing email answered `account_security` would otherwise reach the default rule first.
- **Fixed rules read the items** (each item clause also reads its kept v2 sources, raise-only, P2): rule 1 adds `bank_detail_change`, and its claimed-colleague clause is `claims_internal` (or sender_type `team`) from outside about money; rule 2 is `regulator_claim`, sender_type `regulator` (new, P1; so a regulator's newsletter now escalates every time, with no cap, accepted in Phase R P1 and watched for in S3b's runs) or the regulator trigger; rule 1b's claimed-colleague clause reads `claims_internal`, and its private-individual clause `private_individual` or sender_type `person`, `friend` or `family` (`friend` and `family` new, P2) from outside about money; rule 6 is `phishing`. **S3a only** (P3): each item clause also reads its removed value (`category` `vendor_change_request`, `regulatory`, `spam_or_phishing`; sender_type `team`), so the fixed rules fire as the v2 starter rules did on a v2 answer, plus the raise-only clauses; S3b deletes them. The `spam_or_phishing` id and label are kept in S3 (P16); step 5 renames them (below).
- **A rules file** (applied with `ecf config apply`, or tried with `ecf rules test`) replaced the default rules only (until S4: from S4 it is layered over them, "Three layers" below). It can't use a fixed rule's id ("rule fraud_guard is one of ecf's fixed rules, run first; remove it from your file"), can't test a removed value (refused with its replacement, §7.1), may read the fixed items, and no longer has to end with a catch-all: ecf appends `otherwise` (no actions, `actor: continue`); the id `otherwise` is refused anywhere but a last rule with no `when`. A fixed rule's id is reserved: a schema extension can't add it as a value. Compiled sets are cached (P8): the fixed rules per schema, a composed set per schema and rules text (`config.current_rules` on the stored JSON), so a change to either compiles afresh.
- **Applied rules from v2** (P7): every applied set copied from the starter rules holds the fixed ids. At service start, after the migrations, and on an imported or restored bundle's staged copy, `config.convert_rules` strips each fixed-id rule identical to the v2 starter text (`starter_rules_v2.yaml`, kept byte for byte: the starter file was the same at v2.0.0, v2.1.0, v2.2.0 and v2.2.3, SHA-256 `fda6a698…`, SHA-1 `432aec87…` (the plan's figure), checked with git 2026-10-13) and keeps the rest in order, audited `config.rules_converted`; it is idempotent. A **customised** fixed rule stops it: the stored rules stay as they are (audited `config.rules_converted`, outcome `denied`, once per stored document), don't compile, and the starter rules apply with a System Error (and `ecf doctor`'s schema check) naming the changed rule and the fix; an imported or restored bundle with one is accepted the same way (the rest of its rules still checked), not refused. A document of only unchanged fixed rules becomes `rules: default`. A refused applied set is cached as refused, so it isn't compiled again (nor logged) for every item. v1.0.0's starter text differs (`staff`): its copies count as customised. The pre-upgrade check can't list it (phase 1 runs the installed version's code, §11.10); after the upgrade the new CLI names each such rule (v3.0.0 step 5, OD-508), and the System Error and `ecf doctor` show it.
- **Rule 6 (5th in the fixed order) renamed `phishing`** (v3.0.0 step 5, OD-508; `rules.LEGACY_FIXED_IDS`): its id and label were `spam_or_phishing`; it fires on schema v3's fixed item `phishing: true`, not on spam. No relabel (§6.4). The old id stays ecf's: a rules file can't use it as a rule id or in `default_rules_off` (refused, naming the rename; it stays allowed as a label), a schema extension can't add it as a value, and `convert_v2` strips an identical v2 starter copy as before, while a customised one stops the conversion with a System Error that names the rename. A rule of your own named `phishing`, allowed before, is refused the same way, with the hint to give it another id; the new CLI names it after the upgrade (§11.10).
- **`ecf rules test`** stands each card's labels in for the classifier with the operator's hand-set fixed items (`fixed_labels.jsonl`) and the items its labels imply (`derive_labels`) added (card-stated, then hand-set, then derived), and composes the proposed rules with the fixed rules, so a proposal can't change what the fixed rules decide.

**Three layers** (v3.0.0 S4, operator decisions 2026-10-14, D2, P3, P4, P17, P23, P24, OD-502; code: `rules.compose`, `layered`, `check_layers`, `layer_lines`, `strip_defaults`, `fallback_rules`; `config._rules`, `rules_problem`, `rules_warnings`, `mark_pre_layers`): `compose(schema, text)` builds (1) ecf's fixed rules; (2) the file's rules with new ids, in file order; (3) the default rules in their own order, each default the file **replaces** (a rule with the same id) taking that default's position (spliced, P4; "rename it to keep both"), each id in the file's optional `default_rules_off: [ids]` left out; (4) ecf's `otherwise`, unless something before it matches everything. The file's layer compiles without an appended `otherwise` (P3). A rule with no `when` is allowed only as the file's last rule, and never with a default rule's id (review R3: the rules after it would never run while the dry run says they do, and a bare same-id rule would replace a default with a catch-all mid-list). A file whose last rule has no `when` is a catch-all: the defaults can't run, so it stays the replace case (D2); only a bare last rule counts, a condition that is always true (`requires_reply in [true, false]`) isn't detected (P23, said in the admin guide). **Refused at apply** (and by `ecf rules test`, `check_layers`; P17): an off id that isn't a default rule; a fixed rule's id or `otherwise` in the off list; an id both in the file and in the off list; a repeated off id; an off list in a catch-all file. **At load** an unknown off id is skipped with a warning (`rules.default_off_unknown`; `ecf doctor` shows a `rules` warning and the next dry run says so): a later release may rename a default. **Default rule ids are part of the rules-file format**: renaming one is a major version (OD-480). The dry run and apply say which case applies ("your rules run after ecf's fixed rules and before ecf's default rules", or "your last rule matches everything, so ecf's default rules don't run"), each replacement and where it runs, each default turned off, and the file's rules that can hide (`HIDE_ACTIONS`; D14). **Every validator checks the composed set** (P2, P3): apply (`config._rules`, move targets and labels from user fields across the set), the rules-in-force check against a new schema, `rules_problem`, `ecf rules test` and the dry run; the off list is in the cached text, so the cache shape is unchanged. **Stored files** (P3): a pre-S4 stored file without a catch-all (possible only on S3-era dev installs; v2 required one) changes meaning, its rules now running before the defaults; the first S4 start records it (`rules.pre_layers`) and the dry run of any `ecf config apply` and `ecf doctor` name it until rules are applied again. **Converted v2 files** (P24): `convert_rules` also strips each copy of a default rule identical to the shipped text, only when the composed set is unchanged by it (a v2 file ends in its own catch-all, the replace case, where dropping a copy that isn't followed by every other default unchanged would change it). **Unknown handling** (P14, R17): a condition on a field ecf doesn't fix (`category`, `sender_type`, user fields) is unknown when the classification lacks the field, holds a value the field doesn't have, or a non-boolean on a boolean; Kleene logic as before, and a rule matches only on true, so only results under `not` change (today's composed rules have no `not` over a field: `fixed_rules.yaml` negates facts only). A fixed field (`ecf.schema.FIXED_FIELDS`, 11) compares as it is: an absent fixed item reads false (step 1c P13), and no stored classification lacks one (every accepted classification has every field of its schema, tested, P28). **Fallback** (P2, C11): `config.current_rules` never raises: applied rules that don't compile give way to the starter composition, and if that fails too, to the fixed rules and `otherwise`. **Not in S4** (S4b, after v3.0.0, D1): default-off fields, value replacement for `category` and `sender_type`, dropping a fixed clause on a removed `sender_type` value (S3 decision 3).

**Values removed** (S3b, 2026-10-13, merged 21f62c6; OD-500; `fixed_rules.yaml`): the bridge clauses are deleted, so the fixed rules are plan §4's text: rule 1's bank-detail clause is `bank_detail_change` and its claimed-colleague clause `claims_internal` from outside about money; rule 2 is `regulator_claim`, sender_type `regulator` or the regulator trigger; rule 1b's claimed-colleague clause is `claims_internal` from outside; rule 6 is `phishing`. A removed value reaches a fixed rule only through the item `from_v2` derives from it (§7.1). `ecf rules test`'s stand-in reads card labels through the label map (§16.1). `rules.load_v2_starter` (tests only) compiles the frozen v2 starter text against schema v2.

**Schema v2** (OD-475, OD-476; code: `data/starter_rules.yaml`, `rules.py`): rules 1 and 1b test `team` where they tested `staff`. Rule 1b also matches a `person` from outside about money (`payment_related` or a payment keyword): a colleague writing from a personal address that the model can't place as `team`, and that `org_addresses` doesn't list, would otherwise escape the OD-262 clauses (Phase R finding S5); it gets `label(suspicious)` and `flag`, never hidden. A rules file written for v1 still compiles: `rules.V1_ALIASES` reads `sender_type` `staff` as `team`, and `CompiledRules.aliased` names the rules that used it; stored and applied rules are never rewritten. (Since v3.0.0 S3a, OD-500: a condition on `team` is refused, and applied copies of the v2 starter rules' fixed rules are stripped once, above.) A `{label: {field: x}}` action whose field an item's classification lacks is dropped rather than failing the item (C2).

**Routes** (v2.1.0, OD-490): no rule changes; the route reasons are on the `fraud` trigger (rule 1, `{trigger: fraud}`) and `fraud_weak` (rule 1b) (§8.5). The invariants I1-I4 are also tested with a hand-written custom rule set and with every fact rule 1 reads (`tests/test_policy.py`); with custom rules the plan after classification need not escalate again, since the pre-check's own escalation stands.

**V1.6 additions** (designed in step 1, built in step 1b, 2026-10-05; OD-436, ADR 0021; code: `ecf_server/data/starter_rules.yaml`, `rules.py`): rule 1 adds `impersonates_internal` with money (`payment_related` or a payment keyword, as OD-262) → label suspicious, flag, escalate; rule 1b adds `impersonates_internal` without money → label suspicious, flag, a digest section; neither is hidden. Rule 1a doesn't fire on `self_sent` mail (OD-446): the mailbox, not DMARC, shows it came from the account. The grammar's `fact:` operand accepts `from_org_address`, `impersonates_internal` and `self_sent`. `sender_origin` keeps its meaning for the existing staff clauses (OD-262).

```yaml
  - id: fraud_guard                      # 1
    when:
      or:
        - ...                            # the clauses above
        - and:                           # impersonation about money (OD-436, OD-457)
            - {fact: impersonates_internal, eq: true}
            - or:
                - {field: payment_related, eq: true}
                - {fact: payment_keyword, eq: true}
                - {fact: gift_card_keyword, eq: true}
        - and:                           # an impersonation opener from outside (OD-479)
            - {fact: bec_opener, eq: true}
            - {fact: sender_origin, eq: external}
            - not: {fact: self_sent, eq: true}
        - and:                           # employee tax forms asked for from outside (OD-482)
            - {fact: tax_form_request, eq: true}
            - {fact: sender_origin, eq: external}
            - not: {fact: self_sent, eq: true}
        - {trigger: fraud}
  - id: fraud_weak                       # 1b
    when:
      or:
        - {trigger: fraud_weak}
        - and: [{field: sender_type, eq: staff}, {fact: sender_origin, eq: external}]
        - {fact: impersonates_internal, eq: true}   # without money (OD-436)
```

### 8.7 Reply templates [proposed shape]

Stored in the settings table, changed with `ecf config apply` (security-relevant):

```yaml
version: 1
templates:
  - id: received                 # ^[a-z0-9_]{1,40}$
    enabled: false               # the shipped "received" template is disabled
    subject: "Re: {subject}"
    body: |
      Hello {sender_name},

      Thank you, we received your message and will reply if anything else is needed.
```

Variables are only `{sender_name}` and `{subject}`, inserted as plain text (CR/LF stripped, RFC 2047-encoded in headers). The template text is part of the grant hash.

## 9. Stages, sensitivity, approvals and step-up [v1]

In v1 the OS user is the sole admin and approver; there are no roles (M2).

### 9.1 Stages

`STAGE` per address, enforced by the service; shown as "Watching only / Labels only / Full".
- **shadow:** decide and post, change nothing.
- **assist:** only label, flag, escalate and leave execute (available from V1.2; `stage set assist` needs step-up; `live` needs the go-live gate, built in V1.3 (§9.3); operator decision 2026-09-29, OD-209); other actions become `held` (§6.2). Its purpose is watching the Undo rate on automatic labels; `ecf stage status` shows days in assist.
- **live:** full policy.
- `ecf stage status|set` is admin-only; `stage set live` needs step-up; an override needs a written reason, step-up and a post. Rollback and `ecf pause` are instant.

**As built in V1.2** (step 10a, 2026-09-30; code: `ecf_server/stages.py`, `ecf/cli_admin.py`): `ecf stage status` lists each address's stage with its label, days in it, sensitivity, whether paused, and held items. `ecf stage set <address> shadow|assist [--reason]`: moving forward (shadow to assist) needs step-up, bound to the address and its current stage; going back is instant; `live` was refused until the V1.3 go-live gate (OD-209), built in V1.3 step 6b (§9.3). Every change is audited (`stage.changed`, with the reason) and posted in the address's channel. `ecf sensitivity set <address> standard|high [--reason]`: raising is instant; lowering needs a reason and step-up, and sends a Security Notice (§13.3). Changing sensitivity also changes the address's default size limits (§5.1) unless `max_message_bytes` is set for it.

### 9.2 Review

Item cards have ✅ **Correct** and ✏️ **Fix**; review posts have **All others correct** (items not Fixed on that post; shows "reviewed N of M"). It never counts items with a payment, fraud, regulator or `content_unscanned` signal, nor any item on a `high` address: those need their own Correct or Fix; `ecf stage status` and the go-live dialog show individual and bulk counts (operator decision 2026-09-30, OD-239). Review posts are batched: one per address channel per business hour, ≤ 20 items; 100% of items until the gate count is reached, then `review_sample_rate` (10%). A **Show excerpt** button reveals the first ~200 characters of the stored excerpt, to you only (an ephemeral reply, not kept in channel history; `ecf item show` is the durable path; operator decision 2026-09-29, OD-214). `ecf stage status` shows progress ("73/100 reviewed, 91% accurate, 27 to go"). **As built in V1.3** (step 6a, 2026-09-30; code: `ecf_server/review.py`): the Slack thread posts one review post per address channel per business hour, listing emails the model classified that haven't been reviewed (all of them until the address's gate count, then a stable sample at `review_sample_rate`; an email the sample leaves out is marked so, and one shown is marked asked and not repeated, its buttons still working). Each line gives the email, what the model said (labelled as model output: category, priority, fraud risk, payment) and what ecf would do. Buttons: Fix on every line (a form with the five fields a person corrects: category, priority, fraud risk, payment, sender type), Correct on lines that need their own review (OD-239), and All others correct for the rest; a post holds at most 20 emails and 25 buttons (Slack's limit), so it lists fewer when many need their own button. A review records `correct` or `fixed`, whether the category was right, and whether it was individual or bulk; the first review wins; audited `review.recorded`. `ecf stage status` shows "N/target reviewed, A% accurate, K to go (I one by one, B with All others correct)". Settable from V1.3: `review_sample_rate` (install, 0-100), `escalations_per_hour` (install or address, 1-200) and `label_folder` (address; any folder but INBOX, checked against the mailbox when used). `escalations_per_hour` now applies: escalations other than fraud, quarantine and regulator ones (including those the model found, by its plan's fraud guard or regulatory rule; OD-212) beyond the cap in the last hour roll into one "N more escalations" thread per hour, most severe first. Item cards (escalations, questions, approvals) don't carry Correct or Fix yet; reviews come from review posts.

**Fixed items** (S3a, 2026-10-13, merged fb49b30; OD-500): "All others correct" also never counts an item with a bank detail change, regulator claim, phishing or claimed-colleague signal (`fixed_item`); the review line adds the items that hold ("bank change, phishing"); the Fix form has 13 fields: `category`, `priority`, `sender_type`, `fraud_risk`, `payment_related`, the five items, `requires_action`, `requires_reply`, `deadline_mentioned` (then any extension field; a field the schema lacks is left off). An item the Fix answers (or leaves as shown, which the form submits) is kept as given; only items it leaves out are derived from a changed source field (`review._with_items`, removed in S3b).

**Values removed** (S3b, 2026-10-13, merged 21f62c6; OD-500): `review._with_items` is removed. No `category` or `sender_type` value implies an item any more and the items are on the Fix form, so a Fix records only what it changed; an item the person doesn't answer keeps the model's answer (0036 covers Fixes made before v3, 0037 those that held a removed value, §11.9). The Fix form offers v3's values only.

### 9.3 Go-live gate

- **standard:** ≥ 100 reviewed items, category accuracy ≥ 85%, 0 fraud-guard misses. **Accuracy** (S3a, 2026-10-13, merged fb49b30; OD-500), P4: reviewed items with no Fix (verdict `correct`) over reviewed items, until stage S4 gives user-field data; fixed-field accuracy (no Fix to one of the 10 fixed fields: `fraud_risk`, `payment_related`, the five items, `requires_action`, `requires_reply`, `deadline_mentioned`, from `classification` vs `human_correction`, an item a classification lacks read as false) and category accuracy are shown in the check, not gated. (The local fallback's gate, removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031), counted a reviewed item when its shadow classification agreed with the reviewed truth on every Fix-form field.) `gate.GATE_VERSION = 2` joins the gate's inputs, which the tick keeps in memory only: it makes the tick recompute a gate not yet passed, but an address already live, or whose pass was already announced for its key, keeps its category-era pass until migration 0037 (S3b) clears stored `gate.passed_at`. S3a is never released alone, so no install runs with that gap. No real review data to measure the change on (accept 0 reviewed items, ecf1009 1; Phase R). **Old passes** (S3b, 2026-10-13, merged 21f62c6; P4, S3a review A3): migration 0037 clears every stored `gate.passed_at`, counts kept, so no pass measured on category accuracy carries over, for any preset (an A or B key that the schema change doesn't move included); a rollback merges `gate` from live (`downgrade._merge`), so v2 has no pass either. **Demotion** (S3b, 2026-10-13, merged 21f62c6; diff review B1; code: `stages.demote_after_gate_change`): the tick drops a `live` address only when its key changes, which an A or B key doesn't, so once, at the first service start on schema 37 (after the migrations and the rules conversion), every `live` address with no stored pass goes to `assist` through `stages.set_stage` (audited `stage.changed`, posted), reason "the gate definition changed (S3b); back to assist until its gate passes (§9.3)"; an address whose latest move to `live` was an override (OD-234, `override` in its audit row) stays live. The setting `stages.gate_v2_demoted` marks it done, so later starts do nothing (a restored bundle's settings lack it, so a restore runs it again, which only demotes).
- **Gated accuracy from v3.0.0 S4** (operator decisions 2026-10-14, D4, P22, P30, OD-502; code: `review.record`, `review.reviewed`, `gate.compute`, `gate.note_version`): a review is accurate when its Fix changed none of the 13 `FIXABLE` fields (the 11 fixed fields of `ecf.schema.FIXED_FIELDS`, `category`, `sender_type`; a Fix setting an item the classification lacks to false isn't a change); `review.record` writes it as `gated_ok` at record time, and `reviewed()` reads a review without the key (from before S4) by its verdict (`correct`). A Fix to one of your own fields is counted (`user_fixed`) and shown, not gated. `gate.GATE_VERSION = 3`; no demotion (a version 2 pass counted every Fix, and no user field existed then). `gate` rows carry no version, so the first tick under a new version writes an audit row (`gate.version`, from and to). The check shows the fixed items' and the other fixed fields' accuracy apart ("items 97%, fields 84%"), so `priority`, the noisiest field, doesn't hide the items. **Edit cost** (D3, P15): C's pins hold the whole effective schema digest, so any schema edit on C, a description typo included, drops live C addresses to assist, restarts the review count under the new key and needs a passing `/ecf-eval` (a full or `--fraud-only` run) and 100 reviews (200 on `high`) before live again; the step-up dialog and the Security Notice say so per address. The cost is temporary: step 4 narrows the key with Jev's (P12).
- **Unsure fields (preset D, OD-511; code: `review.record`):** a Fix that sets a field Jev was unsure of (`facts.jev.unsure`) to what ecf already treated it as, yes (`fraud_risk`: `low`), counts as a correct "unsure", not a gated-field miss (`gated_ok`; the review records `unsure_ok`). A Fix to another value, or to a field Jev wasn't unsure of, counts as today.
- **high:** ≥ 200 reviewed, ≥ 90%.
- **both:** every fraud-guard case in the synthetic set passes with the address's current pair (0 misses), 0 misses on any real fraud among reviewed items (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-069), 0 unsafe proposals on payment/fraud items, the injection set at 0; Wilson 95% lower bound reported.
- Synthetic-set results are keyed by (pair, pinned IDs; an Ollama digest before v3.0.0) and shared across addresses; reviewed counts are per address. `stage set live` names a missing result and offers `ecf eval run --fraud-only`. A summary post announces when an address meets its gate.
- A go-live override (written reason, step-up, post) can waive only the reviewed count and accuracy, never the safety gates: fraud-guard 100%, injection set 0, unsafe payment/fraud proposals 0 (§16.5; operator decision 2026-09-30, OD-234).
- The gate is bound to the pair's pinned model IDs (and, before v3.0.0, the local model's manifest digest), and from v2.0.0 to the classification schema (operator decision 2026-10-08, OD-475): a change drops the address to assist until the safety gates (§16.5) pass. `claude_pins.local_key()` is the local model's key (`<Ollama digest>+<schema digest>`; the effective schema's digest, with the install's extension, OD-478), used for preset A's gate, the fallback's gate, `ecf eval run` results and preset B's choice of Gemma run (all removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031)); B and C pins carry the schema digest too. So the upgrade to v2.0.0 starts every address's gate again, and the v1 synthetic results no longer count; `ecf upgrade` lists every address as affected when `release.json`'s `classifier_schema` changes (§11.10). From v2.1.0 the key also carries the classifier's prompt digest (`<Ollama digest>+<schema digest>+<prompt digest, 16 hex>`; `classifier.prompt_digest`: SHA-256 over the system prompt, the user message template, `MAX_INPUT_BYTES` and the model options, not the keyword list, so a keyword patch restarts no gate; classifier plan 0.3, Q3), so new wording starts every A and B gate again; `release.json` carries the shipped `prompt_digest`, and `ecf upgrade` lists every address as affected when it differs or either release lacks one (Q6; the upgrade from v2.0.0 is such a case). `GET /v1/upgrade/state` reports the shipped and the effective (with the install's extension) prompt digests apart. From v2.1.0 C pins also carry `prompt`, 16 hex of `claude_review.prompt_digest` (SHA-256 over the schema fields `get_message` sends and the signals' wording; classifier plan Q4), so a change to Gemma's prompt alone restarts no C gate, and the signals' arrival in v2.1.0 starts every C gate again once. From v3.0.1 C and D pins also carry `actor_prompt`, 16 hex of `plugin_digest.actor_prompt_digest()` (SHA-256 of the raw `agents/actor.md` template, before its agent name is filled in; OD-523; code: `claude_pins.pins`, before D's early return), so a release that edits the actor's instructions drops `live` C and D addresses to `assist` (the tick's reason names "the actor's instructions"), restarts their review count under the new key and needs a fresh `/ecf-eval`. From v3.0.2 `claude_review.prompt_digest` covers the schema fields `get_message` sends, the signals' wording, the excerpt preparation (`excerpt.VERSION`) and the classifier's instructions (`classifier_template`: `plugin_digest.classifier_prompt_digest()`, SHA-256 of the raw `agents/classifier.md` template shared by `ecf-classifier`, `ecf-classifier-high` and the eval classifiers; OD-524), so a release that edits `classifier.md` does the same to `live` C addresses (the tick's reason names "the classifier's or actor's instructions"); D's key doesn't move (its `prompt` is Jev's stored digest). **Limit:** other text the classifier or actor sees is code, not a template, and is in no key: the tool descriptions of `get_message`, `record_classification` and `propose_action` (`ecf/mcp_server.py`), the classifier and actor agents' descriptions and tools (`claude_wrapper.AGENTS`), `claude_review.NOTICE` and the spawn prompt (`claude_review.spawn_prompts`); they change only in a release (P11; v3.0.2 P5). The unpinned eval key (`claude_eval.models_for`, comparison only) holds no `prompt_digest`, so comparison runs before and after a `classifier.md` edit share a key; their results record the difference (`ecf eval compare`'s "different prompt", §16.5; v3.0.2 P10). The v3.0.1 upgrade moves every C and D key once (nothing was `live` then); `ecf upgrade --to 3.0.0` drops a `live` address (3.0.0 can't reproduce a 3.0.1 gate row's key; `downgrade.py` keeps the live `gate` rows), and so does upgrading again (P12). The v3.0.2 upgrade moves every C key once, with the same rollback effect.
- **Decided 2026-10-01 (V1.3 step 6b):** an **unsafe proposal** on real mail is an email with a payment or fraud signal for which the actor (the local actor when this was decided) proposed a hide action (mark read, archive, move, junk) or a send, whether or not policy then refused it, so the check measures the model, not the safety net (operator decision 2026-10-01, OD-260). The **synthetic result** that counts is the latest `ecf eval run` for the address's model digest, and it must be on the current version of the set (a hash of `labels.jsonl`, which changes with any card or confirmation) with 0 unsafe cases; after a change, `ecf eval run --fraud-only` is the shorter rerun (operator decision 2026-10-01, OD-261).
- **As built in V1.3** (step 6b, 2026-10-01; code: `ecf_server/gate.py`, `stages.py`): the service computes the gate for the pinned Ollama digest, never taking it from a caller: reviewed count and category accuracy of emails classified by that digest (waivable), with the Wilson 95% lower bound shown; fraud-guard misses (a Fix whose corrected labels reach rule 1, 1a, 1b or 2 when the model's labels reached none of them, OD-069), unsafe proposals (OD-260) and the synthetic result (OD-261), none waivable. The service records where the set lives when an eval run starts, and checks its version itself. `ecf stage status` shows each non-live address's gate. `ecf stage set <address> live [--override --reason …] [--held run|resolve-older|resolve-all]` prints each check and the held emails by age, then asks for step-up bound to the address, the digest, a snapshot of the gate, the override and the held choice, so a gate that changes after the dialog refuses it. An override needs a written reason and can't waive a failed safety check (OD-234). Going live records the gate as passed for that digest, posts the change with the gate's result and any override, and handles held emails (§6.2): those up to 7 days old run, with your Fix applied where there is one (OD-157; the rule's actions, the actor isn't asked again); older ones stay held unless `--held resolve-older` or `resolve-all` marks them handled by hand (the go-live step-up covers payment and fraud emails). Each minute the service posts "Ready for live" once when an address first meets its gate for a digest, and moves a `live` address back to `assist` (audited, posted) when the pinned digest differs from the one its gate passed with. **Changed in V1.3 step 12b** (2026-10-01; ADR 0006): the synthetic result counts only for a run that went to its last case with both the classifier and the actor (operator decision 2026-10-01, OD-263); a stopped run, one cut by the 8-hour cap or one with `--no-classifier` or `--no-actor` is saved for its figures, shown in `ecf eval status` with why ("stopped after N cases", "without the actor"), and never passes; runs saved before this change are refused as predating the check. Going live by override records the model's digest but not a pass, so "Ready for live" still posts when the gate is later met. **V1.3.1** (2026-10-01; code: `stages.tick`, `gate.inputs`): the minute tick computes an address's gate only when it can still post "Ready for live": never for an address already announced for the current digest, and otherwise only when a cheap fingerprint of the gate's inputs has changed since the last tick (the digest; the count and latest change of the emails that digest classified, recording a review now counting as a change; the sensitivity; the latest config change; the latest sender confirmation; the latest eval run for the digest; the set's `labels.jsonl` size and time). `ecf stage status` and `stage set live` always compute it afresh. Review sampling counts reviews for the pinned digest only, so after a model change every email is asked about again until the new digest's count is reached.

### 9.4 Sensitivity

`standard` or `high`, enforced by the service.
- `ecf address add` requires a choice and suggests `high` on keywords (`ap`, `payable`, `invoice`, `billing`, `finance`, `payroll`, `treasury`, `accounting`, `remit`).
- Upgrading is immediate. Downgrading is CLI only, admin + step-up + reason, announced in Slack; `sensitivity_downgrade_delay_minutes` is 0 in local mode (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-070), so there is no window and no Cancel.

### 9.5 Approvals

- **Slack buttons** name the action ("Approve: archive email", "Approve: send template 'received'"); first writer wins; the frozen action is loaded by grant ID, never from the payload. Payment items say "This acts on the email only. ecf never pays anything." Each approval shows the frozen action, recipient, auth/fraud facts and hash.
- **Reversible approvals** (mark_read, archive, move, junk, draft_reply) on any address are one click in Slack from your member ID and can be undone. A draft is approved one at a time, on a card that shows all of it or with `ecf approve <id>` (OD-551).
- **CLI:** `ecf approve|reject <id>`; `ecf approve --pending` prints waiting step-up items, asks you to confirm the list, handles at most 10, never batches sends or drafts (each gets `ecf approve <id>`, OD-551), then uses one OS authentication for the rest.
- **"Approve all N reversible"** on digests binds the fixed set of grant IDs shown when posted and excludes outbound (sends and drafts, OD-551), fraud-guard, unverified-sender, every `high_risk_route` item, regulator, `content_unscanned` and `high`-address items.
- **Sends on `high` addresses:** approver + step-up + a 10-minute delay (`delayed`), announced in Slack with Cancel (also `ecf cancel <id>`) and emailed when email alerts are on (`Operator Input Needed`, "send scheduled in 10 minutes"). The delay counts only awake time.
- Slack shows "Queued for your computer (N waiting)" for items needing step-up; the service raises a desktop notification.
- **As built in V1.2** (step 7b, 2026-09-29; code: `ecf_server/approvals.py`, `execute.py`, `ecf/cli_items.py`): built and tested with fake proposals and a fake executor, since nothing proposes an action needing approval before the classifier (V1.3) and `live` waits for the go-live gate (OD-207, OD-209). An approval records the proposal, moves the item to `awaiting_approval` and issues a grant bound to the item, its content hash and the exact actions, expiring after 4 days for sends and 14 otherwise (OD-041). The card's Approve and Reject buttons carry the grant ID; the action is always loaded from the grant. The first decision wins (every transition checks the status it expects). Step-up is needed for every send, every irreversible action, and hiding (mark read, archive, move, junk) a fraud, quarantine or regulator item (OD-213); anything already waiting at `awaiting_stepup` goes through step-up however it got there. Clicked in Slack, such an approval waits at `awaiting_stepup`: the card says "Queued for your computer (N waiting)" and keeps only Reject, and a desktop notification names `ecf approve <id>`. From the CLI the step-up runs there and then; its dialog names the action, the sender, the subject and the address. An approval queued for step-up can still be rejected (a new edge, `awaiting_stepup → rejected`, §6.2). `ecf approve --pending` lists waiting approvals (at most 10 non-sends, plus the sends and drafts separately), asks, and approves the list with one step-up bound to those grants; sends and drafts are refused there and need `ecf approve <id>` each (drafts since OD-551). A send on a `high` address goes to `delayed` for 10 minutes of awake time: the service's timer counts down with the monotonic clock (stopped during sleep), the time left survives a restart (migration 0016), the card says "Sending in N minute(s) unless you cancel" with Cancel, and it is said again after a wake (wall time more than 120 s ahead of monotonic time between ticks). `ecf cancel <id>` or Cancel ends it as `cancelled` and voids the grant. Expiry runs each tick: an approval whose grant ran out goes to `expired` and its grant is voided; after a first expiry it returns to `awaiting_approval` with a fresh grant and the card says "Expired, decide again"; after a second it stays `expired`. Approved actions run from the `actions` queue: the grant is consumed once (put back for a retry), 3 attempts with backoff, then `failed`, and the card says what happened. `ecf item requeue <id>` runs a failed or stuck action again under a new grant (step-up again for a send). V1.2 has no real executor for approved actions: it fails them with "not available until V1.3" (hiding and moving) or "V1.5" (sends). The runner is on the service's 60 s timer in V1.2; V1.3 moves it into the checks worker, which holds the address lease that mailbox changes need.
- **Changed in V1.5** (step 15b, 2026-10-04; code: `ecf/cli_items.py`; found in the closing run, §21.1): `ecf approve <id>` first prints the sender, subject and address and what is proposed: each action, which ones need the approval, a send's recipient and template or allow-list entry, a draft's recipient and its whole text (marked as written by ecf's model), and the model's reason; then asks "Approve?" (default no; `--yes` skips the question, not the step-up). Before, it approved without showing anything, so a draft, which needs no step-up, was approved unseen at the computer. `ecf item show` prints the same proposal while it is undecided; since OD-551 it and `ecf approve` also list each action left out and why (on decided items too).

- **Old mail's approvals** (v3.0.0 step 5, OD-507; plan §2, §3.5, P9): an item a scan or reprocess marked never hides on its own (`historical`: every hide is `approve`), gets no card and stays out of "Approve all". `ecf approve --scan <run id>` lists every waiting approval of the run (sender, subject, action), then approves them with one step-up bound to exactly that grant set (purpose `approve_scan`, as `approve_batch`); a send or a draft is listed apart, for `ecf approve <id>` (drafts since OD-551). `ecf approve <id>` still works one at a time.

### 9.6 Step-up

**Required for** (operator decisions 2026-09-27, OD-071, OD-072, OD-077): every send (`forward_internal`, `reply_template`) on any address; every irreversible action; answers and sender-category confirmations on payment or fraud items from any surface (OD-076; a Slack answer waits at `awaiting_stepup`; a sender confirmation is made only at the computer, the Slack button replying with the `ecf sender confirm` command, OD-247); from V1.3 an item is a payment or fraud item also when the classifier calls it payment-related or gives it a medium or high fraud risk, as policy's I3 test does (operator decision 2026-10-01, OD-265), and any confirmation that would count for bank-detail triggers; `item requeue` of a send; `item resolve` of payment or fraud items; `restore`; `slack set-tokens` and member-ID changes; `slack remove`; export-key and `export_dir` changes (prompt shows the key fingerprint, which you re-type); `sender set-reply-to`; `sender set-verified`; `settings set claude_model_override`; `alerts set`; the step-up settings key `classifier_high_batch` (`claude_queue_timeout` removed in v3.0.0, ADR 0031); sensitivity downgrades; go-live and go-live override; security-relevant config changes; send-limit changes and `outbound resume`; `outbound enable`; manual export and import (scheduled export needs none); retention changes; `destroy`. **As built in V1.2** (V1.2 review, 2026-09-30) also: every forward stage move (`stage set` to `assist`, and to `live` once it exists; going back is instant); hiding a fraud or regulator item (OD-213); `address remove` when any open item is payment or fraud (OD-218); every `sender confirm`, since any confirmation counts for the bank-detail trigger (§8.5); `config apply` for any section. `--help` marks each such command "(step-up)".

**Mechanism** (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-073: the service always performs the check; a result reported by the CLI is never trusted):
1. The service issues a single-use nonce bound to (grant or change hash, person), expiring with the approval TTL.
2. `ecf approve` / `ecf stepup` asks for OS authentication:
   - **macOS:** the service runs LocalAuthentication (Touch ID or password) from the LaunchAgent in your login session; reuse duration 0 and a fresh context per nonce (tested 2026-09-29, §21.1: works from the LaunchAgent without `ProcessType=Interactive`; the reply block runs on a background thread and needs no run loop, so the service waits on it from a worker thread with a timeout and withdraws the request with `invalidate` at the timeout).
   - **Linux:** the CLI passes the password you type over the 0600 socket and the service runs PAM (`python-pam`, which checks only the running user's password), or (from M5, OD-224; V1.2 builds PAM only) polkit `CheckAuthorization` on desktops with an agent and ecf's polkit policy installed (a one-time `sudo` at `ecf service install`), with a bus-name or pidfd subject (pidfd needs a newer polkit, unverified); `auth_self` only, never `auth_self_keep`. Attempts are rate-limited (5 per 10 minutes, service-wide; built in V1.2 as `stepup.MAX_TRIES`) so a same-user process can't lock the account through `pam_faillock` (unverified, M5).
3. The prompt text names the action, recipient and address. The result is bound to the nonce and consumed once. If the service can't perform the check, the action is refused.

**Purposes added in v3.0.0 step 5** (OD-507; the service recomputes each bound hash from its own count): `backfill_act` (`ecf backfill --act` with more than 500 emails to classify: address, range, `act` and the count), `reprocess` (`ecf reprocess` with more than 500 to classify again or 500 that could change the mailbox: address, range, options and both counts), `approve_scan` (`ecf approve --scan`: the run and its exact grant set). `--yes` skips a question, never a step-up.

**As built in V1.2** (step 2, 2026-09-29; code: `ecf_server/stepup.py`, `stepper.py`; security review of the V1.2 plan): a nonce is issued for a *purpose* and a *target* (a grant, a setting and its new value, ...); the service loads the target and computes both the bound hash and the dialog text itself, so a client can't make the dialog say one thing and the action do another. The nonce carries a 4-character code that the CLI prints and the dialog repeats. Before the dialog the service recomputes the hash and refuses if the target changed since the nonce was issued. One authentication runs at a time across the service, with a 60 s timeout that withdraws the dialog. A verified nonce must be used within 2 minutes; a nonce the CLI asks for expires after 10 minutes. At most 5 verifications per 10 minutes, service-wide. Step-up routes accept only the CLI token, never an MCP profile token. `ecf stepup test` runs the whole path and changes nothing. `ecf-server dev` uses a fake that approves, so it never shows a real dialog. Audit events: `stepup.requested`, `stepup.verified`, `stepup.refused` (with the reason), `stepup.consumed`; never a password.

**Real-mail corpus** (operator decision 2026-10-07, OD-466; ADR 0022; built 2026-10-07): `corpus_fetch` binds the source email, the folder as requested, host, port, output path, total, byte cap and order (never the password); `corpus_merge` binds the source files' sha256s and the output path. Both are refused on an `ecf-server dev` service, whose step-up is a fake (§16.7). A consumed nonce's target, which names the source address and output path, stays in `nonces` until retention.

**Stated limit:** in v1, step-up confirms your intent inside one OS account; it is not a security boundary against malware already running as you (§12.2).

**Dialog text** (V1.2 review, 2026-09-30; code: `ecf/text.py`): prompts carry email subjects and senders, which the sender controls, so the dialog text and the CLI's step-up lines are cleaned: control and format characters (escape sequences, right-to-left overrides, zero-width marks) removed, line breaks and runs of spaces collapsed, capped at 400 characters.

### 9.7 Security-relevant configuration

`org_domains`, `org_addresses` (V1.6), the forward allow-list, the move-folder allow-list, templates, the action policy, rules and `export_schedule` are changed only with `ecf config apply <file>` (validated, diff shown; operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-075), with step-up and a Slack announcement. `security_config_delay_minutes` is 0 in local mode (reviewer recommendation confirmed by the operator 2026-09-26, OD-074), so there is no Cancel. `export_dir` and the export keys change only through their own fingerprint step-up.

**As built in V1.2** (step 10b, 2026-09-30; code: `ecf_server/config.py`, `ecf/cli_admin.py`): the config file shape (accepted by the operator 2026-09-30, OD-225; `export_schedule` added in V1.5, `org_addresses` in V1.6; sections in `config.SECTIONS`):

```yaml
version: 1
org_domains: [acme.example]                     # public mailbox domains refused (§7.2); [] only per OD-441
org_addresses:                                  # V1.6: exact addresses, optional name (OD-431, OD-433)
  - {address: pat.lee@gmail.com, name: Pat Lee}
forward_allow_list:                             # each in org_domains or exactly in org_addresses (OD-437); never monitored
  - {id: ap_lead, address: lead@acme.example}   # id ^[a-z0-9_]{1,40}$
move_folders: [Receipts]                        # not INBOX; rules may `move` only to these
action_policy:
  standard: {archive: approve}                  # only mark_read, archive, move, junk; auto | approve
rules: {version: 1, rules: [...]}               # §8.6
templates: {version: 1, templates: [...]}       # §8.7
export_schedule: daily                          # V1.5: daily | weekly | off
schema:                                         # the schema extension (§7.1, OD-478); off in v2.0.0 (OD-481)
  fields:
    contract_stage:
      type: enum
      description: Where a contract discussed in the email stands.
      values: {none: No contract discussed., draft: A draft is being exchanged.}
  category_values:
    legal_notice: Letter from a lawyer or court about us.
```

Every section is optional; an omitted one stays as it is, and `<section>: default` returns it to its shipped value (the starter rules, the shipped templates, the §8.3 policy, or an empty list; operator decision 2026-09-30, OD-225). `org_domains` has no default and refuses it. A reset is a change like any other: diff, step-up, audit and Security Notice, and it must keep the other sections valid. At most 50 entries per list; the file at most 48 KB. `action_policy` has no `high` key: `high` is a hard ceiling, and every other action's policy is fixed (§8.3). A change to one section must keep the others valid (new org domains must still cover the forward allow-list; new move folders must still hold every applied rule's `move` target). Alert routes are refused (alert routes use `ecf alerts set`), as is any unknown key; `export_schedule` (`daily`, `weekly`, `off`) is a section from V1.5 step 8b (it was refused before, OD-206). `ecf config apply <file>` shows the diff per section, asks, then needs step-up; `--yes` skips the question, not the step-up. The step-up target is the whole validated document: the service computes the dialog text from it, and the bound hash covers the document and the configuration it replaces, so a nonce can't apply another document, and a change made in between voids it. With the delay at 0 in local mode (OD-074) the change applies at once: stored in the settings table (`org_domains`, `config.<section>`), audited (`config.applied`, with the document's SHA-256 and the per-section changes) and sent as a Security Notice. The dialog and the notice list the riskiest sections first and count any that don't fit (V1.2 review, 2026-09-30); the order as built in V1.6 (`config.RISK_ORDER`): forward allow-list, rules, action policy, org domains, org addresses, export schedule, templates, move folders; from v2.0.0 `schema` comes just before rules. In V1.2 only `org_domains` has a reader; rules, the action policy and the move folders are read from V1.3, the forward allow-list and templates from V1.5. Without applied rules, the starter rules apply.

**The `schema` section** (v2.0.0, operator decisions 2026-10-08, OD-478; code: `ecf_server/config.py`, `ecf/cli_admin.py`): `{fields, category_values}`, both optional but not both empty, checked against §7.1's caps and content rules (the reserved names are the built-in labels and the rule IDs in force, or in the same file); `schema: default` removes the extension. It is validated before `rules`, in `config.validate` and so in the importer, which keeps `config.schema` through `config.KEY`. Rules in the same file compile against the new effective schema; otherwise the rules in force (or the starter rules) must still compile against it, so removing a field or value a rule uses is refused naming the rule (the OD-452 pattern), and a rule ID can't equal an added value. The dry run always prints the budget line, `schema: N of 8 fields, M of 4 category values, X of 4,000 characters`, with ` (near the limit)` from 80% of any cap (fields, category values, values per field, text), and the prompt lines the extension adds (`+`) or drops (`-`). The change line, and so the step-up dialog, the audit and the Security Notice, reads `schema: changes the classifier prompt: fields +a, -b; category +c` (`reset to built-in schema: …` for `default`). The step-up dialog and the Security Notice always lead with `changes the classifier prompt; live addresses go back to assist`, whatever the summary's length cuts. Applying it changes the schema digest, so live addresses drop to assist until their gates pass again (§9.3), in the same transaction that stores it (audited `stage.changed`, reason naming the schema; each address gets its stage post). Removing an added `category` value that confirmed senders use is refused, naming them by category, sender domain and address (sender records hold no sender address). `rules: default` re-checks the starter rule IDs against the added values; `rules.compile_rules` itself refuses a rule ID that is an added value, so `ecf rules test` and `current_rules` enforce it too. An imported bundle whose extension is over a cap is a bad bundle (review fixes 2026-10-08, OD-478).

**While extensions are off** (`v2.0.0`, operator decision 2026-10-09, OD-481): `ecf config apply`, dry run included, refuses a `schema` section other than `default` (`invalid_input`: "config: schema: schema extensions arrive in v2.1.0 (SPEC §7.1); remove the `schema` section"). `schema: default` still removes a stored extension: the rules in force must compile against the shipped schema (else apply rules in the same file), the removal of an added `category` value confirmed senders use is still refused, and the change line reads `reset to built-in schema: unused while extensions are off: …` without the lead; no address drops to assist, since the effective schema doesn't change. An imported bundle's extension is checked against the caps and content rules as before, then kept but ignored, like a stored one; the bundle's rules must compile against the shipped schema. Accepted rather than refused because refusing would leave a backup from an install that applied an extension (on a release candidate) impossible to restore, and ignoring it is what a stored extension gets anyway.

**The `schema` section from v3.0.0 S4** (your own fields; operator decisions 2026-10-14, OD-502; code: `ecf_server/config.py`, `importer.py`, `restore.py`, `addresses.py`, `ecf/cli_admin.py`, `cli_import.py`, `cli_upgrade.py`): while the switch is off the refusal above stands, with the text "config: schema: your fields are off in this release (SPEC §7.1, §1.5a); remove the `schema` section". With it on: **refusals** (§7.1): any address at preset A or B (naming them and the fix; and `ecf address add` refuses an A or B address while fields are stored), any C address with the local fallback on (`claude_queue_timeout`, turned on before S4; P1, operator decision 2026-10-14; the fix: turn it off) (neither can occur from v3.0.0, ADR 0031), the content rules, a fixed field's name in a description, an added value named like a built-in label or a fixed, default or applied rule id, a `{label: {field: x}}` on a user field whose values repeat another field's value or a label name. **Dry run and apply** (`Result.notes`, printed by the CLI after the changes): the budget line with the bytes of schema per classify read (`…; 8,729 bytes of schema per classify read (shipped 7,663)`, P16), the warnings (no catch-all; a description naming a default or user field), the privacy line ("privacy: your field and value names and descriptions go to Anthropic with each Claude classification request, and the chosen values with each actor request (preset C); never put email content or secrets in them", D10, §12.4) and, for a `rules` section, how it layers (§8.6), or, without one, the stored rules' warnings (a pre-S4 file without a catch-all, an off id ecf skips). **The lead** in the step-up dialog and the Security Notice (P15): "changes the classifier prompt; live addresses go back to assist; a /ecf-eval run and reviews (ap 100, hi 200) are needed before live again; ". **Import and restore** drop the bundle's `schema` from the staged copy (P11; `importer.drop_schema`), and the applied rules that read its fields or added `category` values (review R1; `importer.rules_on_fields`: a condition, an `if`, a `continue_if` or a `{label: {field: x}}` on one of its fields, or a `category` condition on an added value; the other rules are kept and checked as before, and with none left the default rules apply), say so in the preview and the result naming its fields and the rules left out (into an install with A or B addresses with the reason; otherwise "re-apply them with ecf config apply (a dialog, step-up and a Security Notice) before ecf uses them"), and the import's Security Notice repeats it; nothing stored is left unused. `ecf address add`'s refusal of an A or B address applies only while the switch is on (review R4; off, a stored extension is ignored, and `ecf doctor` warns about it beside an A or B address). **First start** with a stored extension not yet in use: §7.4 (`config.activate_stored`); the `ecf upgrade` pre-check lists the C addresses it would move (`extension_pending`).

**As built in V1.6** (designed in step 1, built in step 1b, 2026-10-05; code: `ecf_server/config.py`, `internal.py`; ADR 0021): a new section, `org_addresses`:

```yaml
org_domains: [acme.example]          # may be [] only when no watched address is at a
                                     # non-public domain (OD-441); public domains refused
org_addresses:                       # exact addresses (OD-431); optional name (OD-433)
  - {address: pat.lee@gmail.com, name: Pat Lee}
  - {address: dana@acme.example, name: Dana Ruiz}   # an org-domain entry only adds a name
forward_allow_list:                  # each in org_domains or exactly in org_addresses (OD-437)
  - {id: ap_lead, address: lead@acme.example}
```

- `org_addresses`: at most 50 entries; `address` bare (no display name), lower-cased, IDNA domain, at most 254 characters; no two entries for the same address, or the same Gmail account after folding; `name` optional, at least 2 words, at most 100 characters, no control characters; `default` → `[]`. A monitored address may be listed, which makes it internal (the operator's choice, OD-431).
- `org_domains` may be `[]` only while no watched address is at a non-public domain (OD-441; otherwise refused, naming the domains); `default` is still refused.
- **Forward targets** (OD-437): in `org_domains`, or exactly in `org_addresses`; never a monitored address. A newly added target at a public provider is named first in the `config apply` step-up dialog: "<address> (+N more) is a personal account your organization doesn't control; " (`config.personal_targets`). Removing an `org_addresses` entry or an org domain that a forward entry needs is refused until that entry goes too, as for `org_domains` (operator decision 2026-10-05, OD-452).
- Risk order in the dialog and notice: as listed above (`config.RISK_ORDER`).
- Exports carry `config.org_addresses`, and the bundle's data format is 2 (OD-442; §11.9).

### 9.8 Outbound enablement and reminders

`ecf outbound enable <address>` (step-up); on `high` addresses first review ≥ 20 suppressed proposals with ≥ 95% marked correct. Reminders: 7 days after an address goes live, a Slack DM plus a summary-channel post with suppressed counts and `ecf outbound report <address>`; then weekly, up to 4 times; then a monthly summary line. `ecf outbound snooze|dismiss` (logged). `status` and `doctor` always show "outbound: off (N suppressed)".

**As built in V1.5** (step 3b, 2026-10-02; code: `ecf_server/outbound.py`, `ecf/cli_outbound.py`; route `POST /v1/addresses/{id}/outbound` with `value` `on` or `off`): `ecf outbound enable <address>` needs step-up bound to the address, its outbound state and sensitivity ("ecf: let <address> send approved template replies and internal forwards"), audits `outbound.enabled` and sends a Security Notice (build decision 2026-10-02: turning sending on is announced like other security-relevant changes). On a `high` address it is refused, before any step-up, until at least 20 items with a suppressed send have a review and at least 95% of those reviews are "correct" (a Fix counts against), with no override. `ecf outbound disable <address>` is instant, needs no step-up, audits `outbound.disabled` and stops approved sends (OD-323): one in the 10-minute delay is cancelled; one queued to run has its grant voided, so it fails at the runner without sending; the command lists them. Sends still awaiting approval are refused at execution while outbound is off. Reminders, `report`, `snooze` and `dismiss` arrive in step 6.

**As built in V1.5** (step 6, 2026-10-02; code: `ecf_server/outbound_remind.py`, `ecf/cli_outbound.py`; migration 0028; routes `GET /v1/addresses/{id}/outbound` and `POST` with `value` `snooze` (`days` 1-90, default 7) or `dismiss`). **Reminders** count from when the address first went live (a drop to `assist` after a model change doesn't restart them) and run while outbound is off and the address isn't paused: day 7, then every 7 days, 5 in all, each `[ecf-alert] Operator Input Needed: outbound off (<address>)` on the desktop, by DM and in the summary channel (Slack only when `operator` alerts are routed there), with the suppressed count, how many you reviewed and marked correct, and the commands; then one line a month in the summary channel only ("Outbound still off": held back this month and in all). Build decisions, accepted by the operator 2026-10-02: "weekly, up to 4 times" means 4 after the first; the "monthly summary line" is its own summary-channel post, not a line in the daily summary; a computer that slept past a reminder sends one on waking, not the missed ones, and the next counts from then; no reminders once outbound has ever been turned on for the address (turning it off later is a choice). `ecf outbound snooze <address> [--days N]` holds them for 1-90 days; `ecf outbound dismiss <address>` ends them for good; both are refused while outbound is on, need no step-up and are audited (`outbound.reminders_snoozed`, `outbound.reminders_dismissed`; each reminder `outbound.reminded`). **`ecf outbound report <address>`**: outbound, stage and sensitivity; the track record (suppressed, reviewed, marked correct) and, on `high`, what the enablement gate still needs; the latest 20 suppressed proposals with action, sender, subject and review; send limits with the last hour and day, and whether the breaker stopped sends; the latest 20 sends with their status; the reminder schedule. `ecf status` and `ecf doctor` show `outbound: on` or `outbound: off (N suppressed)` for every address. **Fix** (same step): the `high` enablement gate counted a review post's `asked` and `not_sampled` marks as reviews; only `correct` and `fixed` count now.

### 9.9 Clarifications

An **Answer** button opens a Slack modal; answers are authorized to you; first answer wins; mirrored to the thread. Thread replies aren't read. `ecf answer` is a human answer. At most 2 rounds, then `needs_human`. MCP answers (RESPOND) are not in v1 (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-087). No MCP answer counts as human confirmation on payment, fraud or `high` items, and MCP never approves. SECURITY.md lists what a compromised Slack account can do (approve reversible actions, answer non-payment items, pause, resume, undo, dismiss, cancel a delayed send (OD-213), see short excerpts). **For SECURITY.md in V1.5** (V1.2 review, 2026-09-30; from the click handlers as built: `approvals.py`, `answers.py`, `digests.py`, `escalations.py`, `pause.py`): a click from your member ID can approve an action that needs no step-up, reject any approval (including one queued for step-up), cancel a delayed send, answer an item that isn't payment or fraud, undo unverified-sender labels, dismiss an item with no payment, fraud or regulator signal, pause and resume, and show an excerpt (only to the clicker). It can't send, act irreversibly, hide fraud or regulator email or answer on payment or fraud items: those wait for step-up at your computer, so the remaining risks are denial (rejecting, cancelling, pausing) and a queue of step-up requests you didn't start, each of which names its action in the dialog. Sender confirmation isn't done from Slack: the Confirm category button replies only to you with the `ecf sender confirm` command, which you run at your computer with step-up (§7.4d, §9.6: OD-210 planned the button for V1.3, OD-247 decided it only replies with the command), so it isn't on this list.

**As built in V1.2** (step 7c, 2026-09-29; code: `ecf_server/answers.py`, `ecf/cli_items.py`): built and tested with fake questions (the actor that asks arrives in V1.3). A question moves the item to `needs_clarification` and posts a card ("ecf has a question (round N of 2)") with Answer and Show excerpt. The question is model output: links, email addresses and phone numbers are removed, it is capped at 300 characters, and card and form label it "Question from ecf's model (it can be wrong)". **Answer** opens a Slack form showing the question (at most 2,000 characters); `ecf answer <id> [text]` answers from the CLI. The first answer wins. The answer is kept with the item, mirrored to the card's thread, and audited by length only. On a payment or fraud item an answer needs step-up bound to a hash of the answer (OD-076). From the CLI it happens there and then. From Slack the answer waits at `awaiting_stepup` (card and desktop notification name `ecf answer <id>`), and `ecf answer <id>` at the computer shows it and confirms it with step-up. A waiting answer expires after 14 days: the question opens again as a new round. A third question, or an answer expiring in the second round, sends the item to `needs_human` ("Needs you: two rounds of questions didn't settle it"). `approve --pending` never lists answers.


## 10. Human interfaces [v1]

### 10.1 Slack (one app per install, Socket Mode)

- **Channels:** one private channel per address (`ecf-<install>-<address_id>`) plus `ecf-<install>-summary`. Found or created robustly (on `restricted_action`/`name_taken`: instructions, then re-detect); route references stored; teardown archives only recorded routes (deletion only on Enterprise, verified 2026-09-26, docs.slack.dev). `slack install` and `address add` invite your member ID to every channel ecf creates; `doctor` checks it. Anyone in a private channel can invite others, so the daily summary lists members other than you and the bot, and a Security Notice fires when they change (operator decision 2026-09-29, OD-215).
- **Identity:** per-address display name and icon via `chat:write.customize` (shown in threads too, tested 2026-09-29, §21.1); DMs are never customized and use the `D…` channel ID from `conversations.open` (G1-21), cached (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-083).
- **Scopes:** `chat:write`, `chat:write.customize`, `groups:write`, `groups:read`, `users:read`, `im:write`, `pins:write` (all confirmed 2026-09-29, §21.1); app-level token with `connections:write`; manifest `messages_tab_enabled: true`, `messages_tab_read_only_enabled: true`, `socket_mode_enabled: true`. **No** `groups:history`, `reactions:write` or `commands`. Interactivity only; no Events API subscriptions.
- **Content:** category, priority, sender, subject, a way to open the email (the provider's webmail search URL by Message-ID where known, percent-encoded with a fixed host; otherwise `ecf item show <id>`), and the actor's one-sentence question. No body; a short excerpt only on **Show excerpt**. Email-derived text is escaped `plain_text`; unfurls off.
- **Posts** (paced ≤ 1/s/channel through the Slack output queue): threads only for items needing a person; the pinned **"Needs you"** in the summary channel (top 20 plus counts and `ecf inbox`; edited in place only when content changes; header "Buttons work only while <computer> is awake; last connected <time>"); hourly business-hours digests with Undo and Pause; the daily summary at `business_hours.start` (open, stale and expired items, `content_unscanned` counts, outbound suppressed counts, last backup and where it went, backlog growth, newer models and releases; hours on battery removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031)); DMs for personal reminders. Stale-item and Claude-queue reminders are sent once when the condition starts, then only in the daily summary. No idle posts.
- **Buttons:** Approve/Reject (verb-specific), Answer, ✅ Correct, ✏️ Fix, All others correct, Undo, Approve all N reversible, Cancel, Confirm sender category, Show excerpt, Dismiss (non-payment, non-fraud; `resolved_manual`), Pause and Resume (per digest for that address; on the pinned message for all addresses). Hiding (mark_read, archive, move, junk) a fraud or regulator item needs step-up; Undo never removes a fraud or regulator label or flag; Dismiss excludes regulator items too (operator decision 2026-09-29, OD-213). **Every click is accepted only from your configured Slack member ID**; others are refused and logged (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-084).
- **Handler:** the Socket Mode listener acknowledges immediately and calls `views.open` at once (only the ack and `views.open` run on listener threads, inside Slack's 3 s `trigger_id` window); decisions go to a queue. `api_app_id`/`team_id` re-checked, payloads deduplicated, actions loaded from the grant.
- **Install:** `ecf slack install` takes a one-time configuration token (not stored; expires after 12 h, verified, G1-25) and calls `apps.manifest.create`; you click "Install to Workspace" and create the app-level token; it asks for your member ID, confirmed by a DM button click from that ID (during `ecf init`, through a temporary Socket Mode connection); the tokens go over the socket to the service, which stores them. `ecf slack reauthorize` changes scopes, edits existing cards where the message still exists and re-posts the rest. After a revoked token, `ecf slack set-tokens` (hidden prompts, step-up, Security Notice; checks `auth.test` `team_id`/`api_app_id` match) comes first.
- **Sleep:** Socket Mode delivers clicks only to a connected client, and "Needs you" shows "last connected <time>" (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-118). Tested 2026-09-29 (§21.1): on AC power, a click on a sleeping Mac woke it briefly (a DarkWake of a few seconds, triggered by the network traffic), and the service received and acknowledged it; a form (`views.open`) requested during that wake returned success but didn't appear on the phone. So a click handled while the Mac sleeps must be safe without a form, and form buttons need an awake Mac (anything that needs a form replies "open ecf on your Mac"). On battery, unverified.
- **Dead-man's switch:** every tick reschedules a `chat.scheduleMessage` ("ecf hasn't checked in since <time>") a few intervals ahead (3 intervals; built in V1.2 as `deadman.AHEAD`) and cancels it on a clean stop, so a stopped service, tripped breaker or dead laptop still reaches you.
