The socket is created by ecf (umask 0o077, bind, `chmod 0600`) in a 0700 directory and passed via `serve(sockets=[...])`, because uvicorn's own setup applies 0o666 (verified 2026-09-27, uvicorn `server.py`); `log_config=None`; `uds=<path>` set in `Config` for its log line. `init` and `doctor` check the socket path fits `sun_path` (104 bytes macOS, 108 Linux). Over the socket `request.client` is `None`; nothing keys on client host. Errors are RFC 9457 problem+json (§15.3). Routes: §15.1.

### 11.5 Telemetry receiver

Bound once at start on a loopback port (port 0, recorded in settings), served by a **separate two-route app** (`/v1/metrics`, `/v1/logs`) on its own `uvicorn.Server` in the same event loop, so the main API is never reachable over TCP. `ecf claude` reads the port and gets a per-session bearer token passed in `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`. Accepts `application/json` only (OTLP http/json; operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-117).

**As built in V1.4** (step 6, 2026-10-02; code: `ecf_server/telemetry_app.py`, `telemetry.py`): the service binds 127.0.0.1 port 0 at start and serves the receiver with its own `uvicorn.Server` in its own thread; the port is kept in memory and returned by `POST /v1/sessions` with a per-session bearer (32 random bytes; only its SHA-256 is kept), not stored in settings. Unknown bearer: 401; a body that isn't `application/json` or carries `Content-Encoding`: 415; over 8 MB: 413. From `/v1/logs` it keeps only each `api_request`'s sequence, model, `query_source`, input, output and cache tokens, `duration_ms` and `cost_usd` (accepted when present; in Claude Code's documentation, not seen in the 2026-10-02 test), and each `tool_use_id`'s first sequence (since V1.4 step 13, OD-307: each request's end time from `event.timestamp` instead of sequences, and each `subagent_completed` with `model_swapped`: its run and final model); model and source must look like IDs (else `unknown`); everything else, including the identity fields, is dropped as it is parsed. `/v1/metrics` answers 200 and keeps nothing: the log events carry the same figures per request (operator decision 2026-10-02, OD-286). The bearer ends with the session.

### 11.6 Secret stores

- **macOS:** Keychain via `keyring`. **The service is the only writer** (the CLI sends an app password over the socket). The V1.0 gate test (§21.1, 2026-09-27) found that the item's access rule trusts the **interpreter binary by its code hash** (uv's and Homebrew's Pythons are ad-hoc signed), so any process running the same Python binary, from any path, reads silently; neither mitigation is possible (a private copy has the same hash; user-presence items need an Apple entitlement, error -34018). Decision (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-163; `docs/adr/0001-keychain-access.md`): accept this as a stated limit (§12.2) and make the service never hang:
  - the service turns Keychain user interaction off for its own process (`SecKeychainSetUserInteractionAllowed(False)` via PyObjC, tested 2026-09-27: an untrusted read failed in 0.02 s with -25293 instead of waiting on a dialog), so a read it isn't trusted for fails at once and the service waits with "secret store needs you" (like a locked store). Apple deprecated this call in macOS 10.10; the macOS 27.0 SDK still exports it (`SecKeychain.h`, read 2026-10-27), and no supported call does the same for legacy keychain items (§21.2, 2026-10-27). If the call (or PyObjC's Security module) is missing or fails, or the setting can't be read back or still reads as on afterwards, the service starts without secrets instead of reading with prompts on, and `ecf doctor` and `ecf status` say why; a macOS that turned both the set and the get call into do-nothing stubs would get past this (OD-569);
  - a Python change under ecf (a different patch release or rebuilt interpreter) changes the hash; `ecf doctor` and `ecf status` detect it (the recorded interpreter hash differs; V1.0). The foreground re-grant arrives with `ecf upgrade` in V1.5: it runs with prompts on, using the same interpreter binary, where you enter your login password and choose Always Allow (it does: tested 2026-10-02, §21.2; the fallback, if it ever stops working, is that the service re-writes each secret after you re-enter it); the re-grant is its own command, `ecf service regrant`, which `ecf upgrade` runs, since Python can change without an ecf release (V1.5 plan);
  - `uv tool upgrade` with an unchanged interpreter keeps access (tested).
  - **As built in V1.5** (step 8c, 2026-10-03; code: `ecf_server/regrant.py`, `ecf/service_unit.py`; OD-348): `ecf service regrant` refuses while `ecf watch` runs the service, stops the unit if it runs, runs `ecf-server regrant --install <name>` with the terminal attached (the `ecf-server` next to this `ecf`, so the unit's interpreter), and starts the unit again afterwards, also when the re-grant fails or is interrupted. `ecf-server regrant` refuses while the service holds its instance lock (exit 3), turns Keychain prompts on, says to choose Always Allow, and reads every secret ecf may keep (`mailbox/<id>` for each current address, `slack/bot`, `slack/app`, `models-api-key`, `jev-api-key` (since v3.0.0 step 2a), `export-signing-seed`; absent ones are skipped). Only when every read succeeds does it record the new interpreter hash (`updated_by` `regrant`), which clears the warning; a refused read records nothing and exits 1. Audited as `secret.regranted` (counts and the refused name, no values). On Linux both say no re-grant is needed. `ecf doctor`'s fix and `ecf status` point to the command. A macOS test reads a real `ecf-test-*` item written by the same interpreter (silent); the dialog and Always Allow for a changed interpreter were measured by hand (§21.2) and are not repeated by the tests.
- **Linux** (chosen automatically and shown by `doctor`; operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-096): (1) Secret Service (GNOME Keyring, KWallet, KeePassXC) via `keyring` when a D-Bus session and unlocked keyring exist (after a reboot, unreadable until you log in; unverified, M5); (2) otherwise `systemd-creds --user` (TPM2 if present, else the host key; decrypted at service start via `LoadCredentialEncrypted=`; adding a secret runs `systemd-creds encrypt --user`, updates the unit and restarts the service; behavior unverified, M5); needs systemd 256+ (verified 2026-09-27, systemd NEWS); (3) otherwise refuse to start and explain. No passphrase-file fallback.
- **Distributions** (package sites checked 2026-09-27): systemd 256+ on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (259.5), Ubuntu 25.10 (257.9), Debian 13 (257.13), Fedora 43/44/45 (258/259/262), Rocky Linux 10 (257); not on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (255.4), Debian 12 (252.39), Rocky 9 (252). Alma/RHEL 10 very likely 257 (unverified). v1 supports Linux desktops via Secret Service and headless Linux is best-effort (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-097). A root system-unit fallback for older systems is decided in M4. README documents `loginctl enable-linger` and importing the session environment for notifications (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-098).
- **Secret names** [proposed]: service `email-classify-filter/<install>`, accounts `mailbox/<address_id>`, (from M6, in progress: `gmail-client` and `gmail-token/<address_id>`, Phase R P7), `slack/bot`, `slack/app`, `models-api-key`, `jev-api-key` (the TypeSafe key, v3.0.0 step 2a, OD-503; read by `ecf service regrant` and deleted by `ecf destroy` with the others, never exported), `mistral-api-key` (the Mistral key `ecf eval grade` uses, OD-540; handled as `jev-api-key`), `export-signing-seed`. Under `systemd-creds`, credential names can't contain `/`, so `/` maps to `.` (e.g. `mailbox.billing.cred`; operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-172).

### 11.7 Files and permissions

Data directory (`~/Library/Application Support/ecf/<install>` or `~/.local/share/ecf/<install>` [proposed layout]) 0700; database and its `-wal`/`-shm`, socket, logs (rotated at 50 MB, keeping 10 files; operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-160), export temp files and the CLI token file 0600. Full messages are never written to disk. The telemetry receiver listens on loopback only. Only the service writes the rotating log file; the CLI logs to stderr.

### 11.8 Alerts without AWS

Slack plus desktop notifications (macOS `osascript` `display notification`, receiving text only through `on run argv`, shows as Script Editor (unverified, V1.2); `notify-send` on Linux desktops; none headless). Notifications carry no email-derived text; `notifications: off` is available. Email alerts are off by default; `ecf init` asks (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-099); details in §13.3.

### 11.9 Backups, export, import, restore

- **Scheduled export** (`export_schedule`: on, daily, by default; operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-102): a consistent snapshot via SQLite's backup API, encrypted to a stored `age` public key and signed with an Ed25519 key, written to `export_dir`, which `ecf init` asks for and suggests off the data directory's volume (iCloud Drive, Dropbox or an external disk); `doctor` warns if it's on the same volume. Keeps the newest `export_keep` (14). No step-up. The bundle is logical: the allowed tables as JSON lines plus a manifest, read from a backup-API snapshot; the raw database file is never exported, since it holds grants, step-up nonces, jobs and claims (operator decision 2026-10-02, OD-315). Encryption with `pyrage` (age; no `age` program needed), signing with PyNaCl (Ed25519) (operator decisions 2026-10-02, OD-309, OD-319). `System Error` after 2 consecutive failures; the daily summary shows "last backup <time>" and where it went. Time Machine or a live copy is not a substitute (a live database copy isn't a consistent snapshot; unverified).
- **Backup key:** `ecf init` shows once one string holding the age identity and the Ed25519 signing seed, for your password manager (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-103); the running install keeps the seed in its secret store. **V1.5 plan:** the string encodes one 32-byte root value, from which HKDF-SHA256 derives the age identity and the signing seed; the running install keeps only the derived seed and the age public key, so it can't read its own bundles (operator decision 2026-10-02, OD-327).
- **As built in V1.5** (step 8a, 2026-10-03; code: `ecf_server/backup_key.py`, `export_keys.py`, `_age.py`, `ecf/cli_export.py`; operator decisions 2026-10-03, OD-339 to OD-344): step 8 is split into 8a (keys and `export_dir`), 8b (scheduled export) and 8c (the Keychain re-grant). The backup key is shown as `ECF1-` and the 32-byte root in Crockford base32 with a 4-character checksum, in groups of 4 (60 characters); typing ignores case, spaces and hyphens, reads O as 0 and I or L as 1, and a mistyped character fails the checksum (OD-339). HKDF-SHA256 (salt `ecf backup key v1`, one info string per key) derives the age X25519 identity and the Ed25519 seed. `ecf export keys rotate` (also the first key) asks the service for a new key: the service answers with its text once and keeps the derived key in memory only, for 10 minutes; the CLI asks you to type `saved` and then the fingerprint, and a step-up whose dialog names the old and new fingerprints puts it in use: the seed in the secret store (`export-signing-seed`), the age recipient and Ed25519 public key in settings (`export.key`, with a generation number). The root, its text and the age identity are never stored or logged (`key_text` and `backup_key` are redacted from logs) (OD-340). The fingerprint is the first 80 bits of SHA-256 over the age recipient and the public key, 4 groups of 4 Crockford characters (OD-341). A rotation keeps the earlier generations' public halves (`export.keys_previous`), so pruning still recognizes bundles ecf wrote; restoring a bundle made before a rotation needs the old backup key, and `rotate` says so (OD-342). `ecf export dir set <path>` needs a key first, the key's fingerprint typed and step-up; the directory must exist, be writable (a test file is created and removed) and lie outside the data directory. It counts as on the same volume when its device ID matches the data directory's, except under `~/Library/Mobile Documents` (iCloud Drive) or `~/Library/CloudStorage` (Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive), whose files leave the computer; `rotate`, `dir set` and `ecf export keys show` warn about the same volume (OD-344). Both changes are audited (`export.key_rotated`, `export.dir_set`, without the path) and sent as a Security Notice (Slack, desktop, and email when it's on). `settings set export_dir` points to the command.
- **As built in V1.5** (step 8b, 2026-10-03; code: `ecf_server/export_bundle.py`, `scheduled_export.py`, `config.py`, `daily.py`, `service.py`; operator decisions 2026-10-03, OD-343, OD-345 to OD-347): `export_schedule` is a `config apply` section (`daily` by default, `weekly`, `off`; step-up as for any section) and `export_keep` a `settings set` key (14, 1-365). The timer starts an export in its own thread once the last good one is a day (a week) old, on battery too; without a key or `export_dir` nothing runs. Each export: the seed is read from the secret store and checked against the key in settings; `export_dir` is checked again; the next `export.seq` is taken; SQLite's backup API copies the database to a 0600 temp file in the data directory, the tables in `INCLUDED` are read into JSON lines (`settings` without the interpreter hash) and the copy is deleted; the tar.gz (`manifest.json` and `tables/<name>.jsonl`, sorted keys, fixed timestamps) is encrypted to the stored age recipient; the file is `ECFB` and a version byte, a 4-byte header length, the canonical JSON header (format, install ID and generation, kind `scheduled`, created_at, seq, data format 1 (2 from V1.6), schema version, key generation and fingerprint), the ciphertext and a 64-byte Ed25519 signature over everything before it, written as `.<name>.partial` (0600, `O_EXCL`), synced and renamed to `ecf-<install>-<UTC time>Z-<seq>.ecfb`. Partial files left by a crash are removed at the next export. Pruning keeps the newest `export_keep` scheduled bundles among the files whose signature verifies with the current or an earlier key and whose header names this install; anything else in the folder is never touched. A failure (no secret store, seed missing or not matching, folder gone or not writable, a write error) is audited (`export.failed`) and retried after an hour; the second in a row opens `[ecf-alert] System Error` (`export_failed`), routed like other system alerts, and the next success resolves it; success is audited (`export.completed` with seq, size, SHA-256, counts, data format, key generation, pruned count and duration) and shown only in the daily summary ("Last backup <time> UTC to <folder>", or why there's none; OD-347). `ecf export status` shows the schedule, last backup, failures, key and folder; `ecf export now` makes a scheduled backup at once (no step-up, like the schedule). Verified end to end on a dev service, 2026-10-03.
- **Manual `ecf export`** (step-up): encrypted with `age` to a passphrase (scrypt; minimum strength enforced: ecf offers a generated six-word passphrase, and a typed one needs at least 20 characters or 5 words, read without echo; operator decision 2026-10-02, OD-326). **Contents:** items, cursors, config and versions, schema, audit logs, eval labels, gate history, `sent`, `threads`, `senders`, routes and probe results (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-120); never secrets, grants, leases or full messages (excerpts up to 4,000 characters are included). Manifest: install ID, mode, product and data-format versions, creator, counts, per-file SHA-256.
- **As built in V1.5** (step 9a, 2026-10-03; code: `ecf_server/manual_export.py`, `passphrase.py`, `export_bundle.py`, `ecf/cli_export.py`; operator decisions 2026-10-03, OD-349 to OD-351): step 9 is split into 9a (manual export), 9b (reading a bundle, `ecf import --dry-run`) and 9c (applying an import). `ecf export --to <file or folder>` (a folder gets `ecf-<install>-manual-<UTC time>.ecfb`; `.ecfb` is added when missing) offers six words drawn with `secrets` from the BIP 39 English list (2048 words, 66 bits; `data/wordlist/`, MIT, provenance beside it) and asks you to type `saved`; or you type your own twice without echo, which the service accepts with at least 20 characters or 5 different words and no control characters (OD-326, OD-349). The bundle has the scheduled layout with kind `manual`, encrypted with age's scrypt passphrase mode (pyrage doesn't expose the work factor; age's default applies) and signed with the install's seed when a backup key exists, else `signed: false` with 64 zero bytes where the signature goes; `verify` refuses unsigned bundles, and import treats them as foreign (OD-350). The service writes it: an absolute path ending in `.ecfb` in an existing folder outside the data directory, never over an existing file (`O_EXCL` temp file, then a hard link, so a file appearing meanwhile isn't replaced), 0600; step-up is bound to the resolved path; the passphrase is checked before step-up, travels over the socket, and is never stored or logged (OD-351). It shares `export.seq`, is never pruned, is audited as `export.completed` (kind `manual`, `signed`, without the path) and announced as a Security Notice. A locked secret store or a missing or mismatched seed refuses the export rather than writing it unsigned.
- **As built in V1.5** (step 9b, 2026-10-03; code: `ecf_server/bundle_reader.py`, `import_plan.py`, `ecf/cli_import.py`; OD-352 to OD-356, OD-358): reading a bundle never writes it out. The file must be a regular file opened without following a symlink, at most 512 MB. The signature is tried against this install's current and earlier keys (`own`); a scheduled bundle is opened with the typed backup key, and when that key's public half verifies the signature the signer is `typed_key` (what restore will need); otherwise `unknown`, or `unsigned` for a manual bundle without a key; a bundle naming this install but not signed by its key is reported. The plaintext is read as a gzip stream through `tarfile` mode `r|`, member by member: the first must be `manifest.json`; each member must be a regular file (links refused before anything is read), pass `tarfile.data_filter`, appear once, be at most 1 GB, the total at most 2 GB and at most 64 files; only `tables/<name>.jsonl` for an exported table; each file's SHA-256 must match the manifest before it is parsed, every file the manifest names must be present, and row counts must match; each row is a JSON object of strings, numbers, booleans and nulls. Header and manifest must agree; the data format must be this version's or the one before (`bundle_reader.FORMATS`: 1 or 0 in V1.5, 2 or 1 from V1.6), and a schema newer than this install's is refused. `ecf import <bundle> --dry-run` shows the source, the signer, row counts, each address as it would arrive (paused, stage at most assist, outbound off), how many items would be re-posted or marked `failed_unknown`, how many settings and Slack routes would be dropped, what never carries over, and whether this install is empty; without `--dry-run` it is refused until step 9c. **Settings carried over are an allow-list** (operator decision 2026-10-03, OD-358, made stricter than its drop list in building 9b): `org_domains`, the `config apply` sections, `export_schedule`, the `settings set` keys, `log_retention_days`, and alert routes without `email`; every other setting is the source computer's state and is dropped.
- **As built in V1.5** (step 9c, 2026-10-03; code: `ecf_server/importer.py`, `import_plan.py`, `approvals.py`, `ecf/cli_import.py`; migration 0031; OD-357 to OD-361): `ecf import <bundle> [--replace]` shows the preview, asks, asks for this install's name with `--replace`, then needs step-up bound to the bundle's path, SHA-256 and whether it replaces. The target must have no addresses (removed ones count) and no items unless `--replace` with the name typed exactly. A temporary database (0600, in the data directory, deleted afterwards) is migrated to the bundle's schema version (`db.migrate(up_to=…)`), the bundle's rows are loaded (a column the schema lacks is refused; STRICT types, CHECK constraints and foreign keys apply; settings rows replace the migrations' seeds), the remaining migrations run, and then: addresses paused, outbound off, `live` becomes `assist`; `awaiting_approval`, `awaiting_stepup`, `approved` and `delayed` items become `awaiting_approval`, or `needs_human` when the proposal has no actions; `executing` and `undoing` become `failed_unknown` (this mapping is `items.map_imported`, so `items.py` stays the only writer of item status); `origin` (new on `items` and `audit`, migration 0031) is set to the source install ID; `eval_runs.path` is emptied, since the result file stayed on the other computer (the Claude eval skips a run whose file isn't here). Slack routes and open alerts are not copied (alerts describe the other computer; operator decision 2026-10-03, within OD-358). Address IDs, emails and overrides, the kept settings' values, and the config sections (through `config.validate`) are checked; any failure refuses the whole bundle. In one transaction on the live database, `--replace` first clears the target's address and item data (children first, with the old addresses' jobs and item Slack messages), then the staged tables are copied in (audit, model-call and Claude-call rows get new row IDs, appended in order) and the kept settings overwrite the target's; a clash without `--replace` or any failure rolls it all back. Then each re-posted item gets a fresh grant (`approval.reoffered`, why `import`), and its card is posted once Slack routes exist again. Audited as `import.completed` (person, source install and kind, export time, SHA-256, signer, replace, counts, data format, duration) and announced as a Security Notice that names the config sections that changed.
- **As built in V1.6** (code: `ecf_server/export_bundle.py`, `bundle_reader.py`, `import_plan.py`; OD-442): `DATA_FORMAT` is 2, since the settings now carry `config.org_addresses`, which a reader on format 1 would drop silently; import and restore read 2 or 1. `config.org_addresses` is kept on import like the other `config apply` sections (the allow-list follows `config.KEY`). The `downloads` table (the Gmail download budget, §14.3) is in `EXCLUDED` and isn't exported (it counts this computer's recent downloads).
- **Schema v2** (operator decision 2026-10-08, OD-475; code: `export_bundle.py`, `migrations/0034_schema_v2.sql`): `DATA_FORMAT` is 3, so a `v1.0.0` install refuses a v2 bundle rather than read `team` and the new categories as unknown values; import and restore read 3 or 2 (format-1 bundles, from before V1.6, are no longer read). A format-2 bundle is migrated like any older database: migration 0034 maps `staff` to `team` in `items.classification`, `human_correction` and `fallback_shadow.classification` and sets `items.schema_version` to 2, on every `db.migrate` path (service start, import, restore, `ecf rules test`'s scratch database). Going back with `ecf upgrade --to` after settle keeps live `senders` (§11.10): no category was renamed, so their confirmed categories stay valid for v1 (verified in code 2026-10-08: `downgrade.KEPT`; `senders.confirmed_category` holds only category values).
- **Schema v3** (operator decision 2026-10-13, OD-498; code: `export_bundle.py`, `migrations/0036_schema_v3.sql`, `db.py`; built 2026-10-13, uncommitted): `DATA_FORMAT` is 4, following the schema v2 precedent (classifications gain the fixed items, which a version on 3 would ignore; a `v2.x` install already refuses the bundle for its newer database schema); import and restore read 4 or 3 (format-2 bundles, from `v1.x`, are no longer read). Migration 0036 adds the fixed items to `items.classification` and `fallback_shadow.classification` by the §7.1 table, writing only rows with a mapped value and only `true` (an item missing from a stored classification reads as false; schema doc P13); a Fix (`items.human_correction`) gets each item whose source field it sets, true or false as the Fix laid over the model's answer says, so the corrected view stays consistent (a Fix made after the upgrade does the same: when it changes `category` or `sender_type`, `review.record` writes the items derived from the corrected view, `review._with_items`; the items themselves aren't on the Fix form in S2; S2 review F3, 2026-10-13); `items.schema_version` goes to 3 (rows below 3: an item created after 0034 keeps the column default 1 until classified). `items.review` holds no field values and no other table stores a classification (checked in code 2026-10-13; eval result files are outside the database, see `ecf eval rescore`, §16). After 0036, `db.migrate` runs a passive WAL checkpoint (`db.CHECKPOINT_AFTER`). 0036 makes 14 table passes; measured in memory, about 430 ms at 100,000 items, at startup only (accepted 2026-10-13, S2 review F7). Rollback after settle (`downgrade._merge`) copies only `sent`, `threads`, `senders` and `gate` from the live database, so no v3 classification reaches the older version's items; v3 C gate rows are keyed by the v3 schema digest and match nothing there (verified in code 2026-10-13; the snapshot rollback itself is tested on the release path, OD-492).

- **Schema v3 values removed** (S3b, 2026-10-13, merged 21f62c6; OD-500, P9, P4; code: `migrations/0037_schema_v3_values_removed.sql`, `db.py`): migration 0037, separate from 0036, filters on values only, never on `schema_version` (S2-era rows are already at 3): in `items.classification`, `items.human_correction` and `fallback_shadow.classification`, a `category` of `vendor_change_request`, `regulatory` or `spam_or_phishing` becomes `other` and a `sender_type` of `team` (or v1 `staff`) becomes `unknown`, as `from_v2` reads them. Before a value goes, the item it implied is set true (judgment call, raise-only: as S3a's readers read it, so an S2-era answer that gave the old value and not the item keeps its risk); in a Fix only when the Fix doesn't answer the item itself. Rows with no removed value are untouched. `senders.confirmed_category` holding a removed category is cleared (diff review B4; the sender's other history stays, so after a rollback v2 sees it unconfirmed). Then `gate.passed_at` is cleared, counts kept (§9.3). 0037 joins `db.CHECKPOINT_AFTER`. `release.json` `schema_version` is 37. Measured 2026-10-13 by the diff review's performance reviewer on the same 100,000-item file database (WAL, the checkpoint included): 0036 740 ms, 0037 1,012 ms (F2; the readable form is kept, F1). Rollback: the snapshot; `downgrade._merge` copies only `sent`, `threads`, `senders` and `gate`, so no mapped classification reaches v2 (tested on ecf1009 by the checked release path, OD-492, with 0037 and the P7 conversion; not run yet). `DATA_FORMAT` stays 4: import migrates a staged bundle to its version and then runs the normal migrations, so older bundles get 0037.
- **v3.0.0: local models removed** (ADR 0031; R-D7, R-D8, P1, P2, P8, P11, P12, P27): migration 0038 makes every A and B address C and pauses it (removed rows too; §4.3), rebuilds `addresses` with `CHECK (preset IN ('C','D'))` without `fallback_enabled`, `claude_queue_timeout_h` and `fallback_since`, drops `items_model_waiting`, `gate.ollama_digest` and the `fallback_shadow` table, creates `items_claude_waiting` (§4.3), sets `claude_since` for items the fallback had handed off, and deletes alert rows of removed kinds and the settings `resident`, `ollama_log_*`, `daily.model_backlog` and `daily.battery_seconds`; it records the converted addresses in `stages.converted_v3` for the announcement (§4.3). `models_missing` (the model watch's Claude-pin alert) stays. **Kept until v4** (diff review R1, operator decision 2026-10-14): `items.fallback_at`, `model_attempts`, `model_failed` and `model_failed_at` stay in the schema, since each `DROP COLUMN` rewrites the whole `items` table in the migration's one transaction; nothing reads or writes them (`db.UNUSED_COLUMNS`), export leaves them out and import doesn't copy them. **Measured** (2026-10-14, throwaway script, Apple M5, macOS 27.0; a schema-37 database of 100,000 synthetic items, about 8 KB each, 791 MB): 0038 as built took 0.18 s with a WAL peak of 0.4 MB; with the four `DROP COLUMN`s it took 5.6 s with a WAL peak of 786 MB (about the database's size). The rebuild runs through a new no-FK path in `db.migrate` (`db.NO_FK`, the rebuilt table per migration: foreign keys off before the transaction, refused if a transaction is already open; `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` on the rebuilt table's child tables only, and only their rows pointing at it, R4: any row raises `MigrationError`, naming the first five by table and rowid, and rolls back; `ecf-server migrate` prints it, so `ecf upgrade` shows it before rolling back; the connection's own transaction is rolled back and its previous setting restored, best effort, whatever happened, R10). A database that already holds a row pointing at a missing address fails 0038 and the upgrade rolls back (none known to occur). Gate rows are kept (a later release purges them). 0038 joins `db.CHECKPOINT_AFTER`; `release.json` `schema_version` was 38 (41 after 0039-0041, §11.10). `DATA_FORMAT` stays 4 (never released), the drops folded in; import and restore still read 3. A format-4 bundle with A or B addresses or the dropped columns imports with every address C and paused, and the import plan says "converted to C"; `importer.CLEAR` loses `fallback_shadow`. Import and restore refuse a bundle with a preset D address that isn't removed while D is held back (`addresses.D_HELD_BACK`: "preset D (TypeSafe Jev) isn't available in v3.0.0 (OD-516); add the address as preset C"; diff review R11); a removed D address loads. Release note: a bundle older than format 3 is re-exported on v2.2.x first (P26).
- **Fixed rules** (S3a, 2026-10-13, merged fb49b30; OD-500; code: `importer.load`, `config.convert_rules`): an imported or restored bundle's applied rules get the same v2 conversion as the service does at start (§8.6, P7), on the staged copy after the migrations, audited there; a bundle whose rules hold a changed copy of a fixed rule is accepted and kept, as at service start: the starter rules apply with a System Error until it is removed. `DATA_FORMAT` stays 4.
- **`ecf restore <bundle>`** (step-up, Security Notice; operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-121): recovers the same install, keeping Slack routes and gate history (and secrets when the secret store survived), restoring cursors and send history. Bundles must be signed by this install's key, verified against the public key derived from your backup key, never a key inside the bundle; addresses resume at their previous stage after `doctor` passes; security-config and `senders` differences are shown. Restore requires confirming the old computer's service is stopped. **V1.5 plan:** each install has a permanent random ID and a generation that every restore increases, both carried in `X-ECF-Install`; for 7 days after a restore, ecf's own keywords on mail newer than the restored cursor pause the address (Operator Input Needed) instead of being adopted, since another copy may still be running (operator decision 2026-10-02, OD-318). **New machine:** install → `ecf init --restore <bundle>` (asks for the backup key) → `ecf slack set-tokens` → `ecf address set --app-password` per address → `ecf service install` → `ecf doctor`.
- **As built in V1.5** (step 10a, 2026-10-03; code: `ecf_server/restore.py`, `importer.py`, `bundle_reader.py`, `pause.py`, `ecf/cli_import.py`; operator decisions 2026-10-03, OD-362 to OD-373): step 10 is split into 10a (`ecf restore`) and 10b (`ecf init --restore` and the post-restore keyword rule). `ecf restore <bundle>` asks for the backup key (a manual bundle: its passphrase and the backup key), shows a preview (source, whether this install is empty, row counts, each address with its stage and outbound setting, the security-relevant config changes and sender-record changes as counts), asks again when the bundle is older than this install's newest export (`export.seq`), asks you to confirm ecf is stopped everywhere else, asks to go ahead, and needs step-up bound to the bundle's path and SHA-256. The bundle's signature must verify with the key derived from the typed backup key (OD-362); an install with data must already have the bundle's install ID, and an empty one takes it (OD-363). Over existing data a backup-API copy goes first to `<data>/restores/before-restore-<UTC time>.db` (0600, folder 0700; copies older than 7 days are deleted then; OD-370). The bundle loads as for import (temporary database at its schema version, migrated, rows checked, items in flight mapped by `items.map_imported`, eval paths emptied; OD-367), then: addresses paused, stage and outbound kept (OD-366); in one transaction every address and item table is cleared and replaced, Slack routes and alerts included; audit rows keep their IDs (an empty install's own rows give way; otherwise missing rows are added, existing ones kept); the whole settings table is replaced except this computer's state, which keeps its own value (interpreter hash, `export_dir`, export status, audit mark, models install time; OD-368); `install.generation` becomes one more than the larger of the two, `export.seq` the larger (OD-365); `restore.at` and `restore.awaiting_check` (the restored addresses) are recorded. The signing seed derived from the typed key is stored, and if the bundle's settings name another key the typed one becomes current (OD-364). Re-posted items get fresh grants. `ecf resume` (and Slack's Resume) refuses a restored address until a mail check has finished without failing since the restore, saying what to do; `--all` skips held addresses (OD-366). Audited as `restore.completed`, announced as a Security Notice.
- **As built in V1.5** (step 10b, 2026-10-03; code: `ecf/cli_init.py`, `ecf_server/restore.py`, `keywords.py`; OD-371, OD-372): `ecf init --restore <bundle>` starts the service (installing its unit, as `ecf init` does), runs the `ecf restore` flow, then lists what's left: Slack (`ecf slack status`, `set-tokens`), per address `ecf address set <id> --app-password`, `ecf check <id>` and `ecf resume <id>`, then `ecf doctor`. Restore records each address's cursor (`restore.cursors`) for the 7-day keyword rule (§13.6).
- **`ecf import`** (step-up): decrypt, verify the manifest and size limits, migrate N-1 formats only, preview counts and what won't carry over, re-validate every file in the service; YAML loaded with `YAML(typ="safe")`; rejects `..`, absolute paths, symlinks and hardlinks; caps decompression size. Target must be empty unless `--replace` (typed install name). Security-relevant config is applied as one announced diff; `export_dir` and export keys are dropped. Every address arrives paused, stage capped at assist; open approvals are re-posted and need fresh approval. Afterwards re-enter app passwords and reconnect Slack. Unsigned or foreign bundles always follow these rules.
- Logged as `export.*`, `import.*` (§15.2), posted to the summary channel and emailed when email alerts are on; imported history tagged `origin: <source install>`. A successful scheduled export is not posted: it shows in the daily summary; failures, key rotations and `export_dir` changes are posted and emailed (operator decision 2026-10-03, OD-347).

- **Not in the bundle** (v3.0.0 step 5, OD-507, P17): `slack_calls` (§13.4), so `DATA_FORMAT` stays 4.

### 11.10 Upgrade and rollback

`ecf upgrade`: check the release (product, `api_version`, `data_format`, `schema_version`, minimum client) → stop the service → snapshot the database (backup API) → `uv tool upgrade` → `execv` the new `ecf-server migrate` → update the plugin to the same version → start the service → re-check secret-store access (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-111). It warns when a release changes pinned models (affected addresses drop to assist) and names the eval to re-run (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-107). `--to` accepts only release tags; `--wheel` is refused when `install_role = prod`. Rolls back on failure. **`ecf upgrade --to <previous>`** restores the snapshot except `sent`, `threads`, `senders` and `gate` (kept), rewinds cursors to the snapshot so mail since the upgrade is re-fetched (deduplicated by `stable_id`), and resumes every address paused and capped at assist; it warns and asks first. Logged as `upgrade.*`.

**V1.5 plan** (operator decisions 2026-10-02, OD-310, OD-331): built against wheel files (`--wheel` on test installs; `--to` tested against a local index fixture) until the first release publishes an index (OD-272). If an upgrade fails before the new service has completed one normal timer pass, the whole snapshot is restored; after that, the `--to` rules apply and every open grant is voided, approved, delayed and executing items go to `failed_unknown` for reconciliation, and claims are released, so nothing runs twice.

**As built in V1.5** (step 11a, 2026-10-03; code: `ecf/upgrade_check.py`, `ecf/cli_upgrade.py`, `ecf_server/upgrade_state.py`, `upgrade_snapshot.py`, `data/release.json`; operator decisions 2026-10-03, OD-374 to OD-382): step 11 is split into 11a (the checks and the snapshot), 11b (the upgrade itself: `--wheel`, then `--continue`, automatic rollback, the settled mark) and 11c (`--to`). Measured first with `uv tool` 0.12.15 in a scratch tool directory (2026-10-03): the environment holds `uv-receipt.toml` naming the wheel it was installed from; `uv tool install --force <newer wheel>` replaces the files inside the same environment path (new inodes), so the service unit's `ecf-server` path stays valid but a running CLI must not import ecf after the swap; the environment's Python links to uv's `cpython-3.12-…` folder, so a uv Python update changes the interpreter (and the Keychain re-grant applies). `ecf_server/data/release.json` holds product, version, `api_version`, `data_format`, `schema_version` and `min_client`; a test keeps each equal to the code (OD-375); the model pins are read from the wheel's own `models.lock` and `ollama.lock`. `ecf upgrade` with no arguments refuses while no release index exists (OD-374); `ecf upgrade --wheel <file> --check` runs every check before anything stops and prints the report: ecf runs from a `uv tool` environment for this package whose wheel still exists (OD-380); the wheel's release against `GET /v1/upgrade/state` (newer version, schema not older, data format this one or the next, this CLI at least `min_client`); a `prod` install refuses `--wheel`; nothing executing or undoing, no lease held, no `ecf claude` session, no `ecf watch` (OD-379); and the pins that change, with the addresses using them (the gate's roles per preset, plus the local model for A and B), which will drop to `assist` (OD-381). Version order is ecf's own (`X.Y.Z.devN` < `X.Y.ZrcN` < `X.Y.Z`), so no new dependency. `ecf-server snapshot --label <from>-to-<to>` takes the instance lock (refusing while the service runs), copies the database with the backup API to `<data>/upgrades/<label>/ecf.db` (folder 0700, file 0600) and keeps the newest 2 upgrade folders (OD-376). The plugin needs no upgrade step: `ecf claude` renders it from the installed wheel at each start (OD-283), so §11.10's "update the plugin" is moot.

**Preset D in upgrades** (v3.0.0 step 4, S4-D12, P18; §7.10): the wheel's `jev.lock` is read as the "jev" pin and, when the wheel ships one, `jev_mapping.json`'s canonical digest as the "jev_mapping" pin; `GET /v1/upgrade/state` reports both with their D addresses in `pin_users`, so a change to either names the D addresses that drop to assist. A downgrade drops `jev/...` gate rows; the TypeSafe key stays in the Keychain after a rollback (clear it first with `ecf models api-key clear --provider typesafe`); a D address added after the upgrade is lost.

**As built in V1.5** (step 11b, 2026-10-03; code: `ecf/upgrade_run.py`, `ecf/cli_upgrade.py`, `ecf_server/upgrade_state.py`, `service.py`; OD-376 to OD-381): `ecf upgrade --wheel <file>` runs the 11a checks, asks, then **phase 1** in the old CLI: tells the service the stop is deliberate, stops it, runs the old `ecf-server snapshot`, copies the running version's wheel (the one `uv-receipt.toml` names) into the snapshot folder, writes `<data>/upgrade.json` (0600: from, to, label, folder, both wheels, phase, times, pin changes, affected addresses) and runs `uv tool install --force <new wheel>` (`uv` must be on PATH, checked before anything stops). A failed copy restarts the service with nothing changed; a failed install reinstalls the kept wheel and restarts it (phase `failed`). Then it `execv`s `<env>/bin/ecf --install <name> upgrade --continue`, so no old module is loaded after the swap. **Phase 2** in the new CLI: the new `ecf-server migrate`; on macOS `ecf-server regrant` in the foreground (a refusal only prints how to finish it with `ecf service regrant`; OD-378); start the service and wait up to 60 s for it to answer. A failed migration or start stops it, deletes the database's `-wal` and `-shm`, copies the snapshot back, reinstalls the kept wheel and starts the old service (phase `rolled_back`, with the step that failed; OD-331, OD-378). On success the new service records the upgrade (`POST /v1/upgrade/finish`: settings `upgrade.current`, audit `upgrade.completed`; it refuses a record for another version), and at the end of its first tick whose schedule and timer work all succeed it sets `settled_at` (audit `upgrade.settled`; OD-377). Addresses whose pinned model changed drop from `live` to `assist` at that first tick through the existing §9.3 rule (`stages.tick`), which compares each address's gate with its current pins; the CLI names them and the eval to re-run (OD-381). A rollback isn't audited in the database (the old version has no route for it): `upgrade.json` and the command's output record it. Run end to end in the closing run (2026-10-03, launchd, `uv tool` wheels 0.1.0.dev0 and a 0.1.0.dev1 fixture): forward upgrade, settle and `--to` back all worked (§21.1).

**As built in V1.5** (step 11c, 2026-10-03; code: `ecf/upgrade_run.py`, `ecf/cli_upgrade.py`, `ecf_server/downgrade.py`, `items.py`; OD-107, OD-331, OD-382): `ecf upgrade --to <version>` needs this install's snapshot folder `<version>-to-<current>` with its database copy and kept wheel (otherwise it refuses and points to export and import); it refuses while anything is busy (as an upgrade does), says what will happen and asks. **Before the upgrade settled** (the service's `upgrade.current` names this upgrade and has no `settled_at`) the whole snapshot comes back. **After** (or when unknown) the current `ecf-server downgrade-prepare --label <label>` (under the instance lock) copies the snapshot to `ecf.rollback.db` (0600) and, there only: replaces `sent`, `threads`, `senders` and `gate` with the live rows (the columns both versions have, for addresses the snapshot knows); keeps the snapshot's cursors, so mail since the upgrade is read again and deduplicated; voids issued and approved grants; moves open approvals (`awaiting_approval`, `awaiting_stepup`) to `expired`, from which `ecf approve` offers them again (OD-223; operator decision 2026-10-03, within OD-331), and approved, delayed, executing and undoing items to `failed_unknown` (`items.map_downgraded`); clears claims, leases, in-progress marks, delays and queued actions; pauses every address and turns `live` into `assist`. The CLI then keeps the current database files in `before-downgrade/`, puts the chosen copy in place (without `-wal`/`-shm`), reinstalls the kept wheel with `uv tool install --force`, starts the service and records `downgraded` in `upgrade.json`; if the older wheel won't install, the current files come back and the current service starts.

**As built for v1.0.0** (2026-10-06; code: `ecf/release_source.py`, `ecf/cli_upgrade.py`; OD-458, superseding OD-374's "no arguments refuses"): `ecf upgrade` lists this repository's releases with `gh release list` (the operator's own `gh auth`; ecf holds no token), takes the newest stable release newer than this one (an `-rc` or GitHub prerelease only by `--to`), downloads `release-manifest.json`, `SHA256SUMS` and the wheel with `gh release download`, and refuses unless the manifest names the requested tag and its version, the manifest and `SHA256SUMS` list the same files and hashes, the wheel's SHA-256 matches, and its `release.json` version is the tag's. The verified wheel stays in `<data>/releases/<tag>/` (`uv tool` records it and a rollback reinstalls it; earlier downloads are pruned, but only by an ecf that is a `uv tool` install whose receipt wheel is there: from v3.0.5, after a development checkout's ecf deleted the global install's wheel at the v3.0.4 release, §21.2) and goes through the 11a-11c path; `prod` accepts it and still refuses `--wheel`. `--wheel` takes an optional `--sha256sums <file>` (integrity only). `--to` with an older version goes back to that upgrade's snapshot; a newer `--to` must be a release tag. This catches a damaged or swapped asset, not a forged release: access to the repository is the trust root. Untested until the first release: real `gh` output and `gh` under launchd.

**Schema v2** (operator decision 2026-10-08, OD-475; code: `data/release.json`, `upgrade_state.py`, `ecf/upgrade_check.py`): `release.json` gains `classifier_schema` (the shipped schema's version; `tests/test_release.py` keeps it equal to the code) and `GET /v1/upgrade/state` reports the running one (a `v1.0.0` service doesn't, read as 1). When they differ, the upgrade check lists `schema` among the pin changes and every address as affected, since every gate starts again (§9.3). **As built for `v2.0.0-rc2`** (operator-approved 2026-10-09; code: `ecf/upgrade_check.after_upgrade`, `ecf/upgrade_run._recount`): the old client's pre-check can't see a schema change it doesn't know (a `v1.0.0` client ignores `classifier_schema`, so its phase 1 stores no affected addresses), so the new client names the affected addresses after the upgrade: once the new service answers, phase 2 compares the kept old wheel's pins and `classifier_schema` (absent: 1) with the new service's `GET /v1/upgrade/state` by its own rules, adds what it finds to phase 1's lists in `upgrade.json` and the `upgrade.completed` record, and prints the addresses that drop to `assist`. If the kept wheel can't be read, only the schema is compared (a 1.x release had schema 1); if the service doesn't answer the state request, phase 1's lists stand and the first tick still moves the addresses (§9.3). **`v2.1.0`** (classifier plan item 6, 2026-10-10; code: `upgrade_state.py`, `config.py`): `GET /v1/upgrade/state` also reports `extension_stored` (an extension is stored, whether or not in force; `v2.2.0`'s upgrade check needs it) beside `prompt_digest` (shipped) and `effective_prompt_digest` (with the install's extension) (Q6). One migration, 0035 (`senders.request_pass_count`, §8.5; added 2026-10-10 by the pre-classifier plan's G1 refinement, so this sentence's earlier "no migration" no longer holds); `DATA_FORMAT` stays 3 (a new column needs no bump, §8.5), and the facts `v2.1.0` adds (`credential_request`, `crypto_payment`) are new keys in `items.facts`, absent on older items and read as false, so no signal is sent for them. `v2.1.0` adds no fact or field rules can use, so rules applied on it compile on `v2.0.0` after a rollback; rules that don't compile with the running version (a later release's field or fact, or an ignored extension) give way to the starter rules (§7.1, "While extensions are off").

**Schema v3** (operator decision 2026-10-13, OD-498; code: `data/release.json`, `ecf/schema.py`, `claude_pins.local_key`): `release.json` has `classifier_schema` 3, `schema_version` 36 and `data_format` 4; `prompt_digest` is unchanged (`34d0c4cc…`), since the local model is still asked schema v2 (§7.1). The upgrade check's rule is unchanged: a different `classifier_schema` lists `schema` and names every address as affected. For v3 that overstates: only C addresses' gate keys change (their pins hold the v3 schema digest and Claude's prompt digest); A and B keep theirs (`local_key` is built from the schema the local model is asked), so their gate isn't started again. A `v2.2.3` client's phase 1 names every address, and phase 2 only adds to its lists (§11.10 above), so narrowing the rule in v3's client alone wouldn't change the message for an upgrade from `v2.2.3` (open, §21).

**Applied rules** (S3a, 2026-10-13, merged fb49b30; OD-500, P7): the service converts applied rules copied from the v2 starter rules once at start, after the migrations (§8.6): an upgrade from v2 rewrites them, which before v3.0.0 it never did. A changed copy of a fixed rule is left as it is and shows as a System Error and in `ecf doctor`; the pre-upgrade report can't list it (phase 1 runs the installed version's code); from v3.0.0 step 5 the new CLI names it after the upgrade (OD-508, below). A rollback restores the snapshot's settings, so v2 gets its own rules back.

**Values removed** (S3b, 2026-10-13, merged 21f62c6; OD-500): `release.json` `schema_version` 37 (migration 0037); `classifier_schema` stays 3 and `prompt_digest` (the local model's, schema v2) is unchanged, so the upgrade check still names every address as affected while only C keys move (and 0037 clears every stored gate pass, §9.3).

**Rule 6 renamed** (v3.0.0 step 5, OD-508; §8.6; code: `config.rules_customised`, `cli_upgrade._customised_line`): a rule of your own named `phishing` (allowed before), or a changed copy of a fixed rule, stops the v2 conversion at the new version's first start: the default rules apply, with a System Error naming the rename. `GET /v1/upgrade/state` gains `rules_customised` (`[{id, renamed_to, renamed_from}]`, the audit's `customised`; `api_version` stays 1, and a service that lacks it reads as none); phase 2 (the new CLI) carries it in `upgrade.json` beside `converted` and prints one notice per rule, e.g. "your rules file has a rule named phishing, which has the id of one of ecf's fixed rules (spam_or_phishing was renamed phishing in v3.0.0): give it another id (ecf config apply); until then ecf uses its default rules". A notice, not a refusal: the pre-upgrade check can't do it from v2.2.x, since phase 1 runs the installed version's code (`cli_upgrade.preflight`), and v2.2.x's doesn't know the rename (operator decision 2026-10-14, option b). `default_rules_off` is new in v3.0.0 (S4), so no file from before has one.

**Model copies on rollback** (2026-10-08, operator-approved fix; §7.5; removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031), below): the previous release's Ollama copy (`ecf/gemma4-12b:<previous version>`) is no longer deleted by `ecf models install`, so `ecf upgrade --to <previous>` finds its model in place; `ecf models prune` removes old copies only when asked.

**As built for v2.0.0-rc3 (operator-approved 2026-10-09)** (code: `ecf/upgrade_run.py`, `ecf_server/upgrade_snapshot.py`): **reproduced** in the v2.0.0-rc2 release gate (§1.5a item 1, 2026-10-09): a `v1.0.0` install upgraded with `ecf upgrade --to v2.0.0-rc2` (phase 1 by the `v1.0.0` client kept `email_classify_filter-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl` in `<data>/upgrades/1.0.0-to-2.0.0rc2/`), then `ecf upgrade --to v1.0.0` (the rc2 client reinstalled `v1.0.0` with `uv tool install --force` from that folder, so `uv-receipt.toml` named a wheel inside it), then `ecf upgrade --to v2.0.0-rc2` again: the `v1.0.0` `ecf-server snapshot` deleted and remade the folder, taking the receipt's wheel with it, and the copy of the old wheel beside the snapshot failed (`FileNotFoundError`) with the service stopped; `ecf upgrade` and a rollback then refused (the receipt's wheel is gone, OD-380) until ecf was reinstalled by hand. Root cause: the rollback (`upgrade_run.downgrade`, and phase 2's `_roll_back`) installed from inside `upgrades/<label>/`, which the next upgrade with the same label replaces. Phase 1 of that next upgrade is the older version's code, so the fix is in the rollback: every reinstall of an older version (`ecf upgrade --to`, phase 2's rollback, phase 1's failed install) now installs from a copy in `<data>/releases/<tag>/` (where `--to` downloads go; `ecf upgrade`'s pruning keeps the folder the receipt names), made from the kept wheel and checked against it by SHA-256, before anything stops; the receipt never names a file in `upgrades/`. Also, for phase 1 run by v2.0.0-rc3 or later: it refuses before stopping the service when the receipt's wheel is missing; a receipt wheel inside `upgrades/` (an install rolled back by rc2 or earlier) is copied to `releases/` first; any failure after the stop (the copy, the snapshot, writing `upgrade.json`) starts the old service again before reporting; and `ecf-server snapshot` taken again under an existing label keeps that folder's wheel files. An install already left in the reproduced state still needs ecf reinstalled by hand once (`uv tool install --force <its wheel>`).

**v3.0.0: local models removed** (ADR 0031; R-D9, R-D10, R-D13, P3, P4, P13, P26): `release.json`'s `prompt_digest` and `classifier_schema` are Claude's (`claude_review.prompt_digest`, which covers the schema fields `get_message` sends, the signals' wording and the excerpt preparation, not the plugin's agent prompts until v3.0.2 adds `classifier.md`, below; schema v3), `schema_version` 38 (41 after 0039-0041, below), `data_format` 4. The wheel keeps a stub `ollama.lock` (`{"retired": true}`) through v3.0.x so a v2.2.x client's `read_wheel` can read it (it reads the local digest as "None"); the new `read_wheel` reads it only when present and carrying a digest. The new client's `after_upgrade` treats a pre-3.0 `prompt_digest` as unchanged; a v2.2.x client's pre-check (phase 1) says every address drops to `assist`, which over-reports (C's gate key doesn't move) and can't be patched, so the release notes say so. `GET /v1/upgrade/state` gains `converted` (each converted address and its waiting-item count), which the new CLI prints in phase 2 (§4.3). **Rollback** to v2.2.x restores the A and B addresses from the snapshot; 0038 keeps gate rows, so the merge loses none except `ollama_digest` on pre-V1.4 A rows (the merge copies only columns both versions have), and ecf's Ollama login item is still in place. **Clean-up at settle:** `upgrade_state.settle` (the rollback window closed) runs a trimmed, idempotent `retire()` (`ecf/ollama_unit.py`; each command with a 20 s timeout, since it runs in the service's timer thread, diff review R9) that unloads and removes ecf's Ollama login item (on Linux, disables and deletes the systemd unit) and deletes `<root>/ollama/`, never following a symlink; a failure is logged (`upgrade.retire_failed`) and not retried, and a dev service never runs it; model copies (`ecf/gemma4-12b:*`) are left for the operator (`ollama rm`, release notes). The release takes the checked path with the `ecf1009` wheel, rollback, wheel cycle (OD-492).

**Migration 0039** (v3.0.0 step 5, OD-507; review L8): additive only (the `slack_calls` table and two audit indexes; nothing rewritten or dropped; `tests/test_db.py` checks it), followed by a WAL checkpoint (`db.CHECKPOINT_AFTER`, after the index builds over the audit table). Rollback is unchanged: `ecf upgrade --to` puts back the upgrade's own snapshot, taken before 0039 ran (`downgrade.py:4-6`), keeping only `sent`, `threads`, `senders` and `gate` from the live database (`downgrade.py:31`), so `slack_calls`, the indexes and audit rows written since (`item.classified` among them) go with the rollback, as all other post-upgrade rows do.

**Migrations 0040 and 0041** (v3.0.0 step 4, OD-509; step 6f, OD-520, OD-521): 0040 adds nullable columns to `model_calls` for Jev's calls (`backend`, `model`, `fault`, `ms`, `tries`; §4.3), additive, no rebuild; 0041 removes a stored `sonnet` family override from `claude_model_override` (deleting the setting when nothing else is left), audited as `models.override_changed` by `migration` (§7.5). Neither is followed by a WAL checkpoint (`db.CHECKPOINT_AFTER` ends at 39). `release.json` `schema_version` is 41; `data_format` stays 4. Rollback is as for 0039.

**Actor's instructions** (v3.0.1, OD-523, P3, P5; code: `data/release.json`, `upgrade_state.state`, `ecf/upgrade_check.compare`, `changes`, `after_upgrade`, `cli_upgrade._continue`, `_print`): `release.json` gains `actor_prompt_digest` (`tests/test_release.py` keeps it equal to `plugin_digest.actor_prompt_digest()`) and `GET /v1/upgrade/state` reports the running one. The check compares it like `prompt_digest`: a difference, or either side lacking it, lists `actor_prompt` among the pin changes and every address as affected, except on an upgrade from before 3.0, whose crossing already starts every gate (as for `prompt`; `upgrade_run._recount` strips it too). Phase 2 gives the reason "the actor's instructions changed". A 3.0.0 client's phase 1 ignores the field, so it under-reports; phase 2 (the new client) names every address, and the release notes say so. `api_version` stays 1 (an additive field).

**Classifier's instructions and the conversion notice** (v3.0.2, OD-524, P1, P3, P8, P9, P12; code: `data/release.json`, `ecf/upgrade_check.changes`, `after_upgrade`, `cli_upgrade._continue`, `_print`): `release.json`'s `prompt_digest` now includes `classifier.md` (§9.3), so the shipped digest changes and no new field is needed. A `prompt` difference now affects only the addresses using Claude's classifier (the users of `classifier` or `classifier_high`, so C addresses), not D's; schema and `actor_prompt` differences still affect every address. Phase 2's reason for a prompt change is "the classifier's instructions or prompt changed", and `--check` explains `prompt` as it does `actor_prompt`. A 3.0.1 client's `--check` lists a bare "prompt" (expected). **Conversion notice:** `after_upgrade` copies the service's `converted` only on an upgrade from before 3.0 (the crossing, as `crosses_to_claude_prompt` decides), so the CLI prints the notice once, on the 2.x to 3.x upgrade, not on every later one (before, every upgrade from 3.0.0 repeated it); `converted` in `GET /v1/upgrade/state` is unchanged. A rollback to 2.x and a new upgrade print it again for each address still not consented, by design (P9). The notice, `ecf doctor` and the `ecf resume` question share one phrasing (§4.3).

### 11.11 Teardown

`ecf destroy` (step-up; type the install name; offers `ecf export` first): stops and removes the service unit, deletes the database, data directory and secret-store entries, archives recorded Slack routes, deletes the Slack app if a fresh configuration token is supplied, and prints the residue (Slack app if no token, provider app passwords to revoke, the backups in `export_dir`, Ollama's models and login item (named until v4, ADR 0031), the `uv tool` package). Claude transcripts, the rendered plugin and the `ecf claude` config directory live in the data directory (`claude-config`, `claude-work`) and go with it; corrected 2026-10-03 (OD-393).

**As built in V1.5** (step 12a, 2026-10-03; code: `ecf_server/destroy.py`, `api.py`, `service.py`, `__main__.py`; operator decisions 2026-10-03, OD-383 to OD-393): step 12 is split into 12a (the service's part) and 12b (the CLI: the flow, the unit, the data directory, the residue, resuming; OD-383). `POST /v1/destroy` takes the install name typed again and a step-up bound to the install name and install ID, and refuses, listing why, while items are executing or undoing, a lease is held or an `ecf claude` session is open (OD-388). Then, in order (OD-384): it records `destroy.started` and pauses every address; sends the Security Notice straight to the desktop, a Slack DM, the summary channel and alert email (not through the queues, which won't run again); deletes the dead-man's scheduled message; archives the summary channel and every recorded address channel (`already_archived`, `channel_not_found`, `is_archived` and `not_in_channel` count as done); deletes the Slack app with `apps.manifest.delete` when a configuration token is given (`app_not_found` counts as done), and otherwise, or when that fails, revokes the bot token with `auth.revoke`, which "will not uninstall the bot user or the app" but deactivates the bot and removes its channel memberships (docs.slack.dev, verified 2026-10-03; OD-385); and deletes every secret ecf keeps (each address's app password, the Slack tokens, the models API key, the export signing seed). After each step its outcome is written to `<data root>/destroyed/<install>.json` (folder 0700, file 0600, no secrets: the steps, the addresses and their IMAP hosts, `export_dir`, the Slack app ID), which outlives the data directory and stays until you delete it (OD-386). Slack being unreachable stops the run before any secret is deleted; a Slack refusal (a channel that can't be archived, a refused token) is recorded and the run goes on. A second `ecf destroy` skips the steps already done, except that a configuration token given later still deletes the app (OD-387). The service then stops as a stop you asked for (OD-222) and exits 0, and while the record says the service's part is done (`service_done`) and the CLI's isn't, `ecf-server local` refuses to start and exits 0. When the service can't run, `ecf-server destroy --install <name> --confirm <name> [--config-token]` does the same in the foreground under the instance lock, with step-up through the local check and the Keychain prompts on; with no database left it only marks the service's part done (OD-387). The audit events `destroy.started` and `destroy.completed` go with the database; the record and the Security Notice are what remain.

**As built in V1.5** (step 12b, 2026-10-03; code: `ecf/cli_destroy.py`, `cli_init.py`, `cli_export.py`; OD-386 to OD-391): `ecf destroy [--config-token]` (a terminal is required). With the service answering, it reads `GET /v1/destroy` and `GET /v1/upgrade/state` and refuses, listing why, while the service is busy (OD-388), `ecf watch` runs, `upgrade.json` is mid-upgrade (`installing`, `migrating`) or the last upgrade hasn't settled; shows the install, its folder, each watched address (the mailboxes themselves untouched), the Slack channels and app, and that backups in `export_dir` are kept; with no export in the last 24 hours (the newest `export.completed` in the audit, or the scheduled export's last success) asks "Export now?" and runs `ecf export --to` into `export_dir` or a folder you name (OD-389); asks for the install name; with `--config-token` asks for the token (hidden); then `POST /v1/destroy` with step-up, and waits up to 60 s for the service's socket to go. A service that answers but has no usable secret store is stopped and the service's part runs in the foreground; a service that doesn't answer gets the same after a confirmation, without the export offer (OD-387). The CLI's part: the service unit is removed; when `<data>/claude-config` exists, `claude auth logout` runs with ecf's environment (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set; a failure or no `claude` is residue only, OD-390); the data directory is deleted (a symlink in its place is removed, not followed; anything that isn't `<data root>/<install>` is refused); the record gets phase `done`, the CLI's steps and the other installs found in the data root (folders with an `ecf.db`, not `ollama` or `destroyed`). The residue printed (again on any later `ecf destroy`): the service's lines, the Claude login when sign-out failed, and either that Ollama and its login item are shared with the named installs or, when none is left, `ecf models serve uninstall`, `ollama rm <model>` and `uv tool uninstall email-classify-filter` (OD-391; from v3.0.0, ADR 0031, `ecf models serve` is gone: the residue says either that ecf itself is shared with the named installs or, when none is left, `uv tool uninstall email-classify-filter` and `ollama rm <model>` for any model ecf used before v3.0.0); then where the record is. `ecf init` with a destroyed install's name prints a note (phase `done`) or refuses until `ecf destroy` finishes (OD-386). Run end to end against `ecf-server dev` on 2026-10-03 (no Slack, no addresses): the service stopped itself, the folder went, the record stayed. Run in the closing run (2026-10-03) on a throwaway launchd install with a Keychain item: unit, secret and data folder removed, the other install and Ollama untouched (§21.1); not yet run against real Slack.

**V1.6** (step 8, 2026-10-05; code: `ecf_server/destroy.py`, `internal.GOOGLE_APP_PASSWORDS`): for a Gmail address, the list of steps left to do names Google's app passwords page (myaccount.google.com/apppasswords, signed in to that Google account); other providers keep the general line.

### 11.12 Installs and roles

`--install <name>` scopes the data directory, socket, unit label and secret entries, so a test install can run beside prod (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-105). `install_role: prod | test` (default prod, fixed at init; operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-106).

### 11.13 Security trade-off (stated in README and `init`)

App passwords and state live on one computer (no model runs on it from v3.0.0, ADR 0031), so the server-side trust boundary becomes a process boundary on the same machine. Full-disk encryption and a screen lock are required; `doctor` checks FileVault on macOS and LUKS on Linux where detectable. Policy, grants, rules, fraud checks and DKIM verification are the same code as the future server.

### 11.14 Platform notes

| Topic | macOS | Linux |
|---|---|---|
| service unit | LaunchAgent, runs after login | systemd user unit; `loginctl enable-linger` to run without a session |
| secret store | Keychain via `keyring` | Secret Service (desktops), else `systemd-creds --user` (systemd 256+), else refuse |
| step-up | LocalAuthentication run by the service | PAM (password over the socket); polkit on desktops from M5 (OD-224) |
| notifications | `osascript` (shows as Script Editor; unverified) | `notify-send` on desktops; none headless |
| power state | `pmset` | `/sys/class/power_supply` |
| sleep prevention | IOPM assertion on AC power | none in v1 |
| fanless detection | shipped `hw.model` table | none (60-minute catch-up cap) |
| disk encryption check | FileVault | LUKS where detectable |
| data directory | `~/Library/Application Support/ecf` | `~/.local/share/ecf` |
| status | primary platform | **unsupported until M5** (v1.0.0 is macOS-only, OD-422) |

## 12. Security, privacy and threat model [v1]

This section owns the threat model, stated limits and privacy statement; README, SECURITY.md and CLAUDE.md summarize and point here.

### 12.1 Threat model

| Threat | Main controls |
|---|---|
| External sender: prompt injection | rules and triggers first in the service; enum-constrained or validated model output; subagent tool allow-lists; profile scopes; `get_message` limited to claims; no approval tools in MCP; `reason` and subjects sanitized and capped; untrusted-data wrapper; batch guard (§5.6); `classifier_high_batch` default 1 |
| External sender: BEC and invoice fraud | deterministic fraud triggers; sender history; human-confirmed senders for bank triggers; never hidden; escalation; "ecf never pays anything" |
| Header forgery (Authentication-Results, From, MIME) | ecf's own DKIM/DMARC; required signed headers; multiple From = fail; provider headers ignored |
| MIME tricks, padding, hidden HTML, homoglyphs | scan all decoded parts, visible and full text; NFKC + confusable skeleton; `content_unscanned` never hidden |
| Reused Message-IDs, replayed signed mail | `duplicate_message_id`; `stable_id` includes content; `recipient_mismatch` |
| Forged `sent` replies and `X-ECF-Install` | ecf-own skip needs Message-ID + DMARC pass + content hash; loop suppression only on alert-type entries and never suppresses flags |
| A crafted message crashing the service | per-message crash quarantine; crash-loop breaker; dead-man's switch |
| Compromised Slack account | clicks only from your member ID; risky actions need step-up at the computer; list of what it can do in SECURITY.md |
| Attacker text reaching a model that holds tools (confused deputy) | main `/ecf-review` session has no shell and no message bodies; subagents hold only claim-scoped tools; no approval tools |
| Stolen laptop | full-disk encryption and screen lock required; stolen-laptop runbook (revoke app passwords, Slack tokens, Claude sessions) |
| Malicious import bundle | signature check; path, link and size checks; paused and capped at assist; announced diff |
| Supply chain | `uv.lock`; reproducible, hash-verified artifacts; GitHub Releases verified by `release-manifest.json` and `SHA256SUMS` (OD-458); the plugin ships inside the wheel and `ecf claude` renders it from the installed package at each start, so it changes only when ecf is upgraded (OD-271, OD-283; this replaced the plan's marketplace pinned to commit SHAs); the Jev pin checked on every reply (§7.9); gitleaks; Renovate/Dependabot with a cooldown |
| Two installs on one mailbox | install-scoped keywords; pause on foreign keywords or a verified mismatched `X-ECF-Install` |
| DNS forgery on a hostile network | stated limit; DNS failure never yields `pass`; opt-in DoH |
| Flooding (mail or escalations) | page and time budgets; `escalations_per_hour` with a severity-ordered roll-up; burst merge; alert-email caps; send circuit breaker |
| A lying or compromised watcher (in v1: a process on this computer claiming results) | the service computes facts and policy itself; model results validated; telemetry model checked against `models.lock`; profile tokens; stated limit §12.2 |
| Compromised internal account (a listed colleague's Gmail or an org mailbox; V1.6) | its mail passes DMARC and is internal, which matters only for the staff (`team` from v2.0.0) clauses of rules 1 and 1b; from v2.0.0 rule 1b also flags an unplaced `person` from outside about money (OD-476); the money triggers (bank details with change wording, first-time sender with payment, lookalikes) don't exempt internal senders; sends and hides still need approval; monitored addresses aren't internal unless listed (OD-431) |
| Insiders | single user in v1: audit log of every decision and config change; step-up; Security Notices (two-person rules are M2) |
| Your own schema text steering the classifier (v3.0.0 S4; preset C) | the field and value descriptions you write are classifier instructions (the plugin's classifier agent follows the schema text); a description writing one of ecf's 11 fixed fields as a field name (an underscored name anywhere, a one-word name as an identifier, §7.1) is refused (P10), and one using such a word in plain English, or naming a default or user field, warns; that check stops only literal field names, so the controls are the fixed triggers, the fixed rules' facts-only clauses, I1 and the go-live gate (a passing `/ecf-eval` and reviews under the new key); the text is applied only by `ecf config apply` (step-up, Security Notice) |

### 12.2 Stated limits

- **Any process that runs ecf's Python interpreter binary can read ecf's secrets from the Keychain without a prompt** (V1.0 Keychain test, 2026-09-27; OD-163): for example your own scripts or a coding agent using the same uv-managed Python. Other programs must enter your login password.
- In v1, **anyone who controls your OS account controls ecf**: secrets, state and service share one machine. That includes your own coding agent running as you (any Claude Code session with a shell); this is why the plugin lives only in `ecf claude`'s config and OBSERVE carries no email text.
- Step-up confirms intent inside one OS account; it is not a boundary against malware running as you.
- MCP profiles are hygiene, not a boundary.
- **Removed in v3.0.0** (ADR 0031): the limits on a process answering as the local model on Ollama's port, local web pages calling Ollama, and the local model missing purchase-order fraud on credit terms (OD-460).
- DKIM key lookups use ordinary DNS unless DoH is enabled (opt-in DoH, OD-050, isn't built yet: `dns.doh_url` is refused as "not built yet", read from `ecf_server/settings.py` 2026-10-03).
- **Time Machine or another live copy of the data folder is not a backup:** a live SQLite copy isn't a consistent snapshot; the scheduled export is the backup (operator decision 2026-10-02, OD-311; not measured).
- **Building or reading a backup needs memory a few times its size:** `pyrage` encrypts and decrypts whole buffers and the signature covers the whole file (V1.5 step 8b, OD-345).
- Slack keeps what ecf posts under Slack's own retention.
- **On Gmail, mail an account sends to itself arrives without a DKIM signature** (tested 2026-10-05). ecf never sends to a watched address (§8.4, §13.3), so its own mail isn't affected. From V1.6 a person's notes to themselves are recognised by Gmail's `\Sent` label instead (`self_sent`, OD-446); whether mail sent from Gmail's web or app carries the label is unverified (not covered by the V1.6 step 9 run, 2026-10-06).
- **An address in `org_addresses` at a provider other than Gmail** is only as trustworthy as that provider's check that a user sends only as themselves; unverified (OD-447).
- **One person's iCloud addresses aren't folded together** (OD-455): `icloud.com`, `me.com` and `mac.com` can belong to one account, but only Gmail addresses are folded (OD-432), so impersonation clause 4 can flag a listed person writing from another of their own iCloud addresses.
- **Impersonation detection (V1.6) knows only listed names and addresses:** a sender using neither isn't caught, and an outside person who shares a listed name is flagged (OD-433, OD-448).
- **ecf reads INBOX only** (`ecf_server/fetch.py`): mail the provider files elsewhere, such as Gmail's Spam, is never checked (V1.6 planning, 2026-10-04, OD-425).
- **Gmail's own spam filter can file legitimate mail in `[Gmail]/Spam`**, which ecf never reads: in the V1.6 step 9 run (2026-10-06) all 3 DKIM-signed test messages from another provider (Purelymail) went to Spam, and ecf saw them only after they were marked "Not spam" by hand.
- **Google's IMAP download limit for personal accounts is unverified**; ecf stops fetching a Gmail address at 2,500 MB over 24 hours (§14.3, OD-440), Workspace's documented figure (rv).
- **gmail.com publishes DMARC `p=none`** (DNS, 2026-10-05; §18): forged copies of a listed gmail.com address are delivered, arrive unauthenticated (`none`) and raise trigger 6 (§8.5), by design. The eval card `free-forged-own-address` (your own address forged to you) got `fraud_guard` (preset A run b91f57f7, 2026-10-05); how often genuine mail from a listed gmail.com address arrives unauthenticated and raises it (noise) isn't measured.
- **Where a provider can't keep custom keywords** (no `\*` in `PERMANENTFLAGS`, e.g. Proton Bridge), ecf's labels are skipped (OD-439), and what relies on them doesn't work there: spotting a second install by its keywords, the post-restore keyword check (§13.6, OD-318) and the reply guardrail for mail ecf handled before (§8.4); the `X-ECF-Install` check on ecf's own sent mail still works.
- **ecf can't check that another person agreed** to have their Google account watched; OD-427 makes it the operator's condition, and `docs/gmail-setup.md` says so.
- **A changed attached message can go unnoticed on a re-send** (OD-463): ecf's content hash doesn't cover an attached message's headers (§21.2), so a re-sent email with the same Message-ID, the same outer headers and bodies, and only a different attached message's From or Reply-To is treated as a duplicate and not analysed again.
- **Your own field descriptions are classifier instructions** (v3.0.0 S4, P10; preset C): ecf refuses a description that writes a fixed field's name as a field name (§7.1) and only warns on the same word in plain English ("a high priority customer"), so a description can still be worded to sway how the classifier answers a fixed field; the fixed triggers, the facts-only clauses of the fixed rules and the gate are what stop that, not the check.
- **Real-mail corpus** (§16.7, OD-466; built 2026-10-07 except replay):
  - ecf can't check that a corpus comes from a mailbox you own; that is the operator's condition, as OD-427 is for watching.
  - Building, merging or reading a corpus needs memory a few times its size (whole-buffer `pyrage`); figures are measured in the build.
  - The design relies on encrypted swap and core dumps being off (`doctor` checks both).
  - The passphrase and a one-off app password are Python strings, which can't be wiped.
  - The label screen uses the terminal's alternate screen; a terminal that saves alternate-screen lines to scrollback (an iTerm2 profile option; unverified) or restores windows from saved state keeps excerpts.
  - An `ssh -L` forward can make a loopback port reach another server; replay's TLS check against the `127.0.0.1` certificate is what refuses it.
  - The audit pseudonym for a one-off source can be reversed by guessing the address.
  - Gmail's folder size limit, if set, may also cap what a corpus can read (unverified).

### 12.3 Key controls (summary)

Mailbox credentials only in the service; trust boundary in `ecf_server`; stages, sensitivity, action policy, outbound switch and pause enforced by the service; grants hash- and content-bound, single-use, re-checked at execution; fencing tokens; config written only through the API; step-up bound to single-use nonces; TLS via `ssl.create_default_context()`, TLS ≥ 1.2, no STARTTLS downgrade (the probe fails if verification is off); tracebacks never use `show_locals`; imaplib debug output off; YAML always loaded safely.

### 12.4 Privacy statement

- Email is fetched by the local service on your computer. SQLite stores metadata, computed facts, classifications and truncated text excerpts only. **Full messages are held in memory only while they are processed and never written to disk** (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-108; the correction of the earlier wording: OD-109).
- Bodies are processed by Anthropic during `/ecf-review` and `/ecf-eval` (preset C). **In v3.0.0 TypeSafe receives only the eval's synthetic text** (§7.9), never real mail: preset D is held back (OD-516) and no D address can exist (§4.2). When D is on, TypeSafe is a D address's classifier and receives the sender, subject, date, attachment metadata, the redacted classifier excerpt (about 4,000 characters, OD-561) and the derived signals' fixed wording, shortly after each fetch (§7.10). Destinations for email content: the mail provider, Slack (below) and Anthropic; TypeSafe only for a D address, which v3.0.0 doesn't allow. From v3.0.0 no model processes mail on this computer: Gemma, Ollama and the `OLLAMA_DEBUG_LOG_REQUESTS` check (OD-245) are removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031).
- Subjects, senders, classifications, the actor's reason, answers and, on request (Show excerpt), short excerpts go to Slack; to Anthropic during `/ecf-review` and `/ecf-eval`; and, in the eval only, to TypeSafe (synthetic text). Slack keeps them under Slack's retention (free plan: hidden after 90 days, deleted after 1 year, verified, G1-26).
- Claude Code transcripts on your computer contain email text; `ecf claude` sets a one-day cleanup period and purges its config's transcripts on exit.
- Telemetry stays on the machine; identity fields Claude Code includes (user email, account and organization IDs) are dropped on arrival.
