- No payload logging (a structlog no-content processor; operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-165): fields named `body`, `text`, `html`, `raw`, `content`, `subject`, `from`, `sender`, `to`, `cc`, `reply_to`, `recipients`, `excerpt`, `snippet`, `headers`, `attachment_name`, `filename`, `answer`, `reason`, `question`, `password`, `app_password`, `token`, `secret` and `passphrase` are redacted; any other string over 200 characters is cut; raw bytes are dropped. Log code records IDs and counts, not content. Unresolved records (metadata only) are kept until resolved or closed as `resolved_by_mailbox`, and flagged stale after 30 days.
- Exports include excerpts of up to 4,000 characters, not bodies.
- The weekly model watch (§7.6) sends no email content: the optional API key to api.anthropic.com (`/v1/models`); and, only while a TypeSafe key is stored (OD-561), the key to api.typesafe.ai with `GET /v1/models` and one key-check request to `jev-latest` whose text is fixed (the key check's: "ecf key check" and its one question). The ollama.com page request is removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031).
- With email alerts on, alert email goes through your provider to `alerts.email.destination_address`; it carries only what desktop notifications carry (the address ID, counts, item IDs and commands), never a subject, sender or excerpt (operator decision 2026-10-02, OD-316).
- An internal forward sends the original email, unmodified, only to an address on your forward allow-list, after your approval and step-up (OD-316). An allow-list entry is in your org domains or, from V1.6, exactly in `org_addresses`, which may be a personal account at a public provider (OD-425, OD-437); adding such an entry names it first in the `config apply` step-up dialog ("<address> is a personal account your organization doesn't control", §9.7). OD-437's condition that another person's watched mail goes to a public-provider address only with that person's agreement is the operator's to keep: ecf doesn't check it (no such check in `ecf_server/config.py` or the forward path, read 2026-10-06).
- Export bundles may sit in a sync folder (iCloud Drive, Dropbox); they are encrypted to a key the sync provider never sees (OD-316).
- From V1.6 you may watch another person's Google account only when its owner creates the app password and agrees to ecf processing their mail as this statement describes, including what goes to your Slack and to Anthropic (operator decision 2026-10-04/05, OD-427). This adds no destination. **Converted addresses** (v3.0.0, ADR 0031, P3): an A or B address converted to C at upgrade is paused; resume it (`ecf resume <address>`) only after its owner agrees to its mail and the derived signals going to Anthropic, which is what resuming confirms, or remove it. Before Jev (preset D) sees a third-party account's mail, its owner agrees again (PLANNING §4.8).
- **Exception: a real-mail test corpus** (operator decision 2026-10-07, OD-466; ADR 0022; built 2026-10-07 except replay): a file of full messages may be written to disk only age-encrypted, with a passphrase, from a mailbox the operator owns, on a prod or test install, after step-up and with a Security Notice. You read its excerpts and headers while labelling. Excerpts of replayed corpus mail exist only in a throwaway `ecf-server dev` data folder on a RAM disk. In v1 a corpus never goes to Anthropic. It adds a place content is stored and read, not a destination (§16.7).
- **Your own fields** (v3.0.0 S4, OD-502, which supersedes OD-478/OD-481's wording here; behind the switch, off in v3.0.0 since M2 failed, §1.5a item 2b; preset C only, D8): the field and value names and descriptions you write go to Anthropic in every Claude classification request (`schema_text`), and the values chosen for them in every Claude actor request (`classification`); the names go to Slack (the Fix form and review lines). They are operator-written, not email content, and add no destination. `ecf config apply` says so before you apply them (D10, P29): "privacy: your field and value names and descriptions go to Anthropic with each Claude classification request, and the chosen values with each actor request (preset C); never put email content or secrets in them". In v3.0.0 none of it goes to TypeSafe: the user layer is off and is preset C only (D8). There is no free-text field type (R9).
- **Derived signals** (OD-483, ADR 0026; the first, OD-484, from `v2.1.0`): on preset C a classification request to Anthropic may carry a few true/false signals ecf computed, in fixed wording (for example, that an outside sender asks for employees' tax forms). They carry no email text, addresses, keywords or reasons, and add no destination; and, in the eval only, they go to TypeSafe with the synthetic cards (OD-504). (On preset A, until v3.0.0, they stayed on this computer.)
- **Built for the eval only (v3.0.0 step 2, OD-503/504): TypeSafe Jev** (operator decision 2026-10-12, OD-493; ADR 0028): TypeSafe AI, Inc. (api.typesafe.ai, US-hosted per its privacy policy, (rv)) may receive email content as the classifier. In steps 2 and 3 only invented text (the key check, the live check) and the frozen synthetic set reach it; real mail would reach it only through a preset D address, which v3.0.0 doesn't allow (OD-516), and the service refuses an eval naming a corpus session. What the eval sends, over TLS to `api.typesafe.ai:443` (`POST /v1/systemone`, headers `Authorization: Bearer`, `Content-Type`, `Accept`, `User-Agent: ecf`): the pinned `model`; the questions (every schema field's description and its value or level names and descriptions); and the state: ecf's fixed untrusted-data preamble, the true derived signals in fixed wording (OD-483), the sender's display name and address, subject and date (normalised), each attachment's name, type and size, each on one line (with redaction on, a subject or display name that trips fraud trigger 10 is replaced by ecf's marker), and the prepared body excerpt, up to 4,000 characters (1,500 until OD-561; redaction removes only what fraud trigger 10 matched, OD-254; with `--no-redact`, synthetic `--fraud-only` runs only, nothing is removed). The key check and the probe send the minimal POST (state `ecf key check`, one yes/no question). TypeSafe also sees the IP address, times, the account behind the key and the call pacing. Nothing else. What TypeSafe publishes (read 2026-10-13, PLANNING §4.8): hosting in the US and no training or fine-tuning on input (privacy policy, updated 2025-11-19); retention "as long as necessary", with no fixed period (DPA, updated 2026-04-24); zero data retention for enterprise customers only (/legal). Its sub-processor list (trust.typesafe.ai, Subprocessors tab, 14 listed; read from the operator's screenshots 2026-10-13) says AWS stores and processes request data and Modal, Nebius and CoreWeave process prompts without storing them, all in the US; it gives no data description for Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, Cloudflare or ClickHouse, so whether request content reaches them isn't stated. Which agreement governs API use isn't stated in what ecf has read (ADR 0028). In v3.0.0 this covers the eval's synthetic text only; turning preset D on needs this statement reviewed again, with README, SECURITY.md and DISCLAIMER.md.
- The mail provider includes, for an address on the Gmail API (M6, OD-529), Google's API and OAuth endpoints; ecf polls and uses no push service (no Pub/Sub).
- Email content goes nowhere else; adding a destination is a design change [proposed wording].

### 12.5 Repo hygiene

`.gitignore` covers `eval/private/`, the eval build cache `tests/eval/synthetic/.build/`, and stray `*.eml` outside `tests/eval/synthetic/` (committed 2026-09-27).

### 12.6 README security recommendations

Slack (2FA, private channels, restricted app installs, membership reviews); mail (per-address app passwords with 2FA; your own SPF/DKIM/DMARC at `reject`/`quarantine`; rotate app passwords); computers (full-disk encryption, screen lock, patches); Claude (Team or Enterprise preferred for business mail; on Pro/Max turn model-improvement sharing off and keep extra usage off or capped); process (verify payment or bank changes out of band, review the audit log, keep the backup key in a password manager).

## 13. Operations [v1]

### 13.1 `ecf init --mode local`

1. **"Have ready" checklist:** Slack configuration token and a workspace where you can click "Install to Workspace"; your Slack member ID; the app password for each mailbox, and its IMAP server unless it's Gmail (V1.6); your org domains (none needed when every mailbox is at a public provider, OD-441) and the sensitivity for each address; Claude Code and a separate Claude login for `ecf claude`; a TypeSafe API key only if you run Jev evaluations (preset D is held back in v3.0.0, OD-516); Python ≥ 3.12 and uv; whether this install is `prod` or `test`; a password manager for the backup key; an email address if you want email alerts.
2. The service: started first (the unit installed, or started if installed), since it stores every later step; an unconfigured service idles (§11.1).
3. Full-disk-encryption check and secret-store check.
4. The install role, `prod` or `test`, set once.
5. Slack install (§10.1), including the member-ID confirmation click.
6. First address: app password by hidden prompt, sent over the socket to the service; `org_domains` when none are set (default: the address's domain; validated as `config apply`); probe (folders, keywords, sent-mail saving, maximum size; a plain-words note that sender authentication relies on ecf's own DKIM check); sensitivity; preset (C; D, built in step 4, is held back, OD-516) and pair (warning about plan usage for C); stage = shadow; outbound = off.
7. The email-alerts question (off by default; V1.5).
8. Scheduled export (on, daily, by default; `export_dir`; shows the backup key once; V1.5).
9. (The `ecf models install` offer, V1.3, is removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031).)
10. The unit confirmed installed and running.

Steps are idempotent (`--resume`, `init status`). V1.2 delivers the Slack, org-domain and address steps; V1.3 adds the model step; V1.5 the export step.

**As built in V1.2** (step 11c, 2026-09-30; code: `ecf/cli_init.py`, `ecf_server/initsetup.py`): `ecf init [--mode local] [--resume]` prints the checklist and asks "Ready?" (`--resume` skips both), then runs each step the service doesn't already report done, so running it again resumes: (1) the service: every setup step is stored by the service, so if nothing answers on the socket `init` starts it first (installs the unit, or `service start`s an installed one, which clears a tripped breaker); an unconfigured service idles (§11.1); (2) disk encryption (FileVault or LUKS, as `doctor`; a failure asks before going on) and the secret-store backend (unavailable stops `init`); (3) the install role, `prod` or `test`, set once (`init.role_set`) and refused afterwards; (4) Slack, the `ecf slack install` steps, which you may skip; (5) the first address, the `ecf address add` prompts, which also ask the org domains when none are set (the V1.1 path, validated like `config apply`; changing them later is `config apply` with step-up); presets B and C print the fallback reminder, C also the plan-usage note; (6) the unit: confirmed installed and running, or installed now; when the service answers from outside its unit (`ecf watch`), `init` says so instead of installing a second copy. So the unit is in place before configuration rather than last (the order above; V1.2 review, 2026-09-30, rewrote the list to match). `ecf init status` lists the steps as done or to do (models V1.3, export V1.5). The email-alerts question is skipped until V1.5 (OD-206).

**As built in V1.3** (step 11, 2026-10-01; code: `ecf/cli_init.py`, `ecf_server/initsetup.py`; removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031), with the fallback reminder and `GET /v1/init`'s `models` and `fallback_off`): the model step runs after the first address. `GET /v1/init` reports whether a local model is needed (any address on preset A or B; C's local fallback arrives in V1.4) and whether `ecf models install` has completed on this install. When it's needed and the model isn't ready, `init` asks "Install the local model now? (about 8 GB to download)" and runs the same code as `ecf models install`: ecf's Ollama login item first when nothing serves Ollama, then the pull, digest check and copy, with progress. If Ollama itself isn't installed, `init` prints the error's install hint (macOS: `brew install ollama && brew pin ollama mlx-c`) and goes on to the last step; skipping is fine too. `ecf init status` shows the models row as done when installed or not needed. The checklist names Ollama for presets A and B. **Step 12b fixes** (2026-10-01; code: `ecf/cli_models.py`): when Ollama doesn't start within 30 s, `init` says so and goes on to the last step instead of stopping; after an install `init` and `ecf models install` check the model is ready and print why when it isn't (e.g. a listener beyond loopback), instead of "installed"; if the service restarts during an install, `ecf models install` says to run it again (exit 3) instead of waiting forever.

**As built in V1.4** (step 11, 2026-10-02; code: `ecf/cli_init.py`, `ecf/claude_setup.py`, `ecf_server/initsetup.py`): after the model step and the fallback reminder, `GET /v1/init` reports whether any address uses B or C (`claude_needed`); if so, `init` checks Claude Code (installed, v2.1.242+; otherwise it says so and goes on) and ecf's own Claude login, and when there is none asks "Log in to Claude for `ecf claude` now?" and runs `ecf claude --login`; skipping prints the command. **The login** (operator decision 2026-10-02, OD-304): `ecf claude --login` runs `claude auth login` with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set to ecf's config folder and the same allow-listed environment as a session (so `ANTHROPIC_*` never reaches it), then reads `claude auth status --json`; a login already there is left alone; it takes no other arguments. Claude Code keeps the login (macOS: in the Keychain, §10.3); `auth status` also names the account's email and organization, which ecf drops, keeping only `loggedIn`, `authMethod` and `subscriptionType` (shape read from Claude Code 2.1.287, 2026-10-02: exit 1 and `loggedIn: false` when logged out). `ecf init status` gains a `claude` row: not needed, `ecf claude --login`, or the login method and plan.

**As built in V1.5** (step 13b, 2026-10-03; code: `ecf/cli_init.py`, `ecf/cli_export.py`, `ecf_server/initsetup.py`; operator decisions 2026-10-03, OD-400 to OD-403): after the first address come the alert-email step and the backup step, then the model, fallback, Claude and unit steps (OD-403). **Alert email** (OD-400): on already, it says so; with no address that has an SMTP server it says that's needed first and goes on; otherwise it asks "Also send alerts by email?" (default no); yes asks for the sending address (only when several have an SMTP server) and a destination, then runs `ecf alerts email set` (step-up, a test email, routes `slack,email`); a refusal (e.g. a watched destination) is printed and `init` goes on. **Backups** (OD-401): set up already, or `export_schedule: off`, it says so; otherwise it asks "Set up daily backups now? (recommended)" (the schedule's word; default yes): without a key, the `ecf export keys rotate` flow (the key shown once, `saved`, the fingerprint typed, step-up); then a folder: it lists `ecf-backups` under iCloud Drive, each folder in `~/Library/CloudStorage` and each mounted volume but the startup disk (Linux: `/media/<user>/*`, `/run/media/<user>/*`), takes a number or a full path, offers to create a missing folder (0700), and runs `ecf export dir set` with its own step-up (the fingerprint just typed is reused; an existing key's is asked); then "Make the first backup now?" runs `ecf export now`. `init` doesn't turn backups off. **Markers** (OD-402): a no to either question is recorded by the service (`init.skipped.email` or `.export`, the time; audited `init.step_skipped`); `init --resume` doesn't ask it again, plain `init` does. `init status` rows: `alert email` (done when on or skipped, since it's optional) and `export` (done when key and folder are set, with the schedule, folder and last backup, or when `export_schedule` is off; a skipped one stays "to do" and says no backups are made). The checklist adds a password manager for the backup key and an optional alert address.

**As built in V1.6** (step 2, 2026-10-05; code: `ecf/cli_init.py`, `ecf/cli.py`, `ecf_server/initsetup.py`, `api.py`; OD-441): the first-address step asks for the IMAP server only when the domain isn't in `imap_defaults` from `GET /v1/addresses` (gmail.com and googlemail.com: `imap.gmail.com`). The org-domains question (the `address add` prompt) is asked only when none are set and the address isn't at a public provider (`public_domains`). `GET /v1/init` adds `org_addresses` (a count) and `public_only` (every watched address is at a public provider). `init status`'s `org domains` row is done when org domains are set or `public_only` holds ("none needed: every address is at a public provider"), and adds the org-addresses count when there are any. The "Have ready" checklist is unchanged: it still lists each mailbox's IMAP server and your organization's domains (`ecf/cli_init.py` `CHECKLIST`).

### 13.2 `ecf doctor`

Service running and last timer tick; secret-store backend and access (including after interpreter changes) and any wait state; full-disk encryption; Slack bot and app-level tokens, Socket Mode connection, channel membership, DM delivery; IMAP probe results and last broker error per address; DNS/DKIM reachability; pinned Claude IDs and minimum `claude --version` (2.1.295, for the spawn guard's `onFailure: block`, OD-497; `claude_wrapper.MIN_CLAUDE`); the `ecf-mcp` path resolves and the installed wheel's RECORD hash matches the plugin; package/plugin version match; addresses converted to C and paused at the v3.0.0 upgrade, with their waiting-item counts and "resume only after the owner agrees (OD-427), or remove it" (P3; from v3.0.2 in the shared phrasing of §4.3, the row kept until consent or removal, OD-524); ecf's Ollama login item left from before v3.0.0 (its plist, or on Linux its systemd unit, still there, e.g. after an upgrade that didn't go through `ecf upgrade`'s settle), WARN with the commands that remove it; doctor reads the file only and runs nothing (diff review R8); org domains or org addresses set (V1.6; below); per Gmail address, All Mail shown over IMAP and no folder size limit (V1.6; below); outbound state; scheduled-export age, writability and volume; last successful and next scheduled check per address; held count and days in stage; crash-loop breaker state; SQLite `quick_check`, minimum version and free disk; socket path length; on Linux, "Linux isn't supported yet (milestone M5)"; a warning when neither email nor desktop notifications can reach you.

**As built in V1.2** (step 12a, 2026-09-30; code: `ecf_server/slack_doctor.py`, `ecf/doctor.py`): the Slack and step-up checks run in the service, which holds the tokens (`GET /v1/doctor/slack`), and `doctor` prints them with the rest: step-up available here (the checker's name; `ecf stepup test` tries it; none is a failure); Slack installed; your member ID confirmed; the bot token accepted by `auth.test` and still in the recorded workspace; the Socket Mode connection (with the last connected time when down); your membership in every channel ecf recorded (summary and per address); that a DM to you can be opened (nothing is sent; `ecf alerts test` sends one); and an open Slack Delivery Failed alert. Each failure names its fix (`ecf slack set-tokens` then `reauthorize`, Confirm in the DM, `set-member`). The app-level token is judged by the live connection, not by opening a second one.

**Review fixes** (V1.2 review, 2026-09-30; code: `service.py`, `slack_runtime.py`, `slack_admin.py`, `doctor.py`): an error in the service's minute timer is counted; after 5 failed ticks in a row it opens System Error ("timer work failing") and doctor shows "timer work" as FAIL with the error; a good tick resets the count and resolves it. Each step of the Slack thread's periodic work (member check, re-invite, "Needs you", dead-man's switch, digests, summaries) runs on its own, so one failing step no longer stops the rest. `doctor` reports an error from the service's Slack checks as a FAIL row instead of stopping, and an unusable secret-store backend as FAIL. `ecf slack set-tokens` releases Slack posts held for a bad token and resolves Slack Delivery Failed; `reauthorize` is suggested only for `missing_scope`. `ecf slack install` refuses only once an app identity is recorded, so an install stopped partway can be run again. `ecf slack reauthorize` re-posts only "Needs you" and open items' cards, not old digests; since OD-557 it does what `ecf slack repost` does (below). Every step-up purpose validates its target values before they reach the dialog text, so a made-up value is refused, not shown.

**As built in V1.3** (steps 1b, 1c, 12b; code: `ecf/doctor.py`, `ecf_server/models.py`; removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031)): the local-model rows: Ollama's readiness for the pinned model (reachable, listener on 127.0.0.1 only, the server's environment, the digest; FAIL with the fix, WARN before the first install), the server settings that differ from ecf's login item (`OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL`, the cloud feature, flash attention, the q8 cache, debug logging, `OLLAMA_ORIGINS` with `*`), and, when ecf's login item for Ollama exists, FAIL if the program it starts is gone (an Ollama upgrade or removal; fix: `ecf models serve install`). `ecf models serve status` prints the same.

**As built in V1.4** (step 11, 2026-10-02; code: `ecf/doctor.py`, `ecf/claude_setup.py`): the Claude rows. **Level** (operator decision 2026-10-02, OD-305): each fails `doctor` once an address uses preset B or C (`claude.used` in `/v1/status`) and only warns otherwise or when the service doesn't answer. `claude code`: installed and v2.1.242+. `claude login` (only while B or C is used): ecf's own login, from `claude auth status` in ecf's config folder (OD-304); FAIL with `ecf claude --login`. `claude pins`: the pinned IDs in force (overrides applied) and their roles, while B or C is used. `ecf-mcp`: the `ecf-mcp` next to the running Python exists, is executable and has the SHA-256 the installed package's RECORD gives it. `claude plugin`: since the plugin is rendered from the wheel's templates at each start (OD-283), "RECORD matches the plugin" means each template `render_plugin` reads has its RECORD hash, and "package/plugin version" means the installed distribution's version equals `ecf.__version__`, which the plugin carries. An editable install (a development checkout, `uv sync`) lists no template in RECORD, so templates are not checked there and the row says so; `ecf-mcp` is listed and checked either way. Checked 2026-10-02 on a built wheel installed in a scratch venv: both match, and one appended line in `agents/actor.md` or in `ecf-mcp` is reported as changed since install. The fix for every install row is reinstalling ecf.

**As built in V1.5** (step 13a, 2026-10-03; code: `ecf_server/ops_doctor.py`, `ecf/doctor.py`; operator decisions 2026-10-03, OD-394 to OD-399): the service answers `GET /v1/doctor/ops` with rows shaped like the Slack checks; `doctor` prints them after Slack, and skips them when the service doesn't answer (OD-395). `smtp <address>`: from what is stored, without a live login: no SMTP server set, or the last probe's SMTP check failed or never ran, fails when the address has outbound on or sends alert email and warns otherwise; a send accepted after the probe counts as working (OD-396). `alert email`: off, or the sender and destination with the last delivery (sent rows are kept 7 days) and the queue; a warning once the oldest queued email has waited 10 minutes (a failure is already the `alert_email` System Error). `alert reach`: a warning when alert email is off and desktop notifications are off or no notifier exists here, since a Slack failure would then reach nobody (OD-397). `backups`: not set up (no key or no folder) or `export_schedule: off` warn; `backup folder` fails when missing or not writable (the same test file as `export dir set`) and warns on the data directory's disk; the last backup is fine up to one period plus 2 hours, a warning up to two periods, then a failure; with none yet, the first is "due" for one period plus 2 hours after the key or folder was last set; a failed attempt since the last backup makes a fine row a warning naming the error (OD-398). The re-grant fix stays the secret-store row (step 8c; OD-399).

**As built in V1.6** (steps 2 and 3, 2026-10-05; code: `ecf/doctor.py`, `ecf_server/ops_doctor.py`, `probe.py`; OD-438, OD-440, OD-441): the `org domains` row warns when there are neither org domains nor org addresses ("no org domains or org addresses: mail pretending to be people you work with isn't detected"; fix: list their addresses and names in `org_addresses`, or your domains in `org_domains`, with `ecf config apply`) and is OK otherwise, showing the org domains (or "none") and the org-addresses count; the old "not set" warning is gone. `gmail <address id>`, one row per address in Gmail mode at its last probe (from `GET /v1/doctor/ops`): a warning when All Mail isn't shown over IMAP ("All Mail isn't shown over IMAP: archive fails and the email stays in the inbox"; fix: Gmail settings, Labels, Show in IMAP for All Mail, then `ecf address set <id> --app-password`, which probes again); otherwise a warning when the probe's inbox counts show Gmail's IMAP folder size limit is on ("IMAP shows N of M inbox messages", more than 10 apart; fix: Gmail settings, Forwarding and POP/IMAP, Folder size limits, Do not limit); otherwise OK ("Gmail mode; All Mail shown; probed <time>Z"). Without All Mail an archive is refused (`mailbox_actions.py`): the item fails, is listed in `ecf inbox` and "Needs you", and the email stays in the inbox; the probe warnings say the same for a missing Archive or Junk folder and for a server without MOVE or UIDPLUS (wording fixed in V1.6 step 10, 2026-10-06; it said "held for a person").

**Model copies** (2026-10-08, operator-approved fix; code: `ecf/doctor.py`; §7.5; removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031)): with the local-model rows, an OK `model copies` row lists ecf's Ollama copies for other releases, kept for another install or a rollback, and names `ecf models prune`.

**As built in v2.0.0, rewritten for v3.0.0 S4** (OD-478; OD-502, P16, P27; code: `ecf_server/ops_doctor.py`): a `schema` row from `GET /v1/doctor/ops`: OK with "v3, built in (no fields of your own); 7,663 bytes of schema per classify read", or "v3 with an extension;" and the budget line with the bytes per read (§9.7); a warning at 80% of any cap, with the fix "shorten descriptions or remove a field before adding more". While the switch is off (OD-481, kept by OD-502): a stored extension is a warning, "v3, built in; an extension is stored but extensions are off in this version", with the fix "`ecf config apply` with `schema: default` removes it". A stored extension that no longer compiles is a FAIL ("the built-in schema is used"); applied rules whose composed set doesn't compile against the schema in use (§8.6) are a FAIL, "the starter rules are used", with the fix "apply rules that don't use the schema extension or ecf's fixed rules, with ecf config apply". A stored extension beside any preset A or B address (pre-S4 state; D8 now refuses both ways) is a warning, switch on or off, as is one beside a C address with the local fallback on (review R5; fix: turn the fallback off, or remove the fields), naming the addresses, with the fix "remove the fields (`schema: default` with ecf config apply), or the preset A and B addresses (ecf address remove; add them again with --preset C)" (operator decision 2026-10-14). From S4 a `rules` row warns (never fails: mail is decided) for an off id ecf skips (`default_rules_off`) and for a pre-S4 file without a catch-all whose rules now run before the default rules (P3), with the fix "ecf config apply with your rules file (ecf rules test shows what changes)".

### 13.3 Alerting

- **Routes** (`alerts.routes`: `slack`, `email`, or both; default `slack` in local mode, `slack,email` once `ecf init` enables email; at least one required). Per-class overrides `alerts.<class>.routes`. Changed with `ecf alerts set [<class>] --to …` (step-up, Security Notice). `ecf alerts test` sends a test.
- **Email alerts:** `alerts.email.monitored_address` (a watched mailbox whose SMTP login sends them) and `alerts.email.destination_address` (where they go; may not be a monitored address). Exempt from the outbound switch; counted separately from the send circuit breaker; capped per alert type at 10 an hour, then one hourly roll-up (reviewer recommendation confirmed by the operator 2026-09-26, OD-100), and at 30 an hour across all types; none is tried while the sending address has a mail alert open (operator decision 2026-10-02, OD-328); recorded in `sent`. Their text is the desktop notification's, never a subject, sender or excerpt (OD-316). If the provider is unreachable, alerts fall back to Slack and a desktop notification.
- **Slack-health alerts** can't be delivered through Slack: they go to email when on and always to a desktop notification.
- **Security notices** go to every enabled route regardless of class settings.
- **Subjects** (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-112; titles operator-reviewed 2026-09-26): every alert email's Subject starts with `[ecf-alert]` followed by a fixed title; details go in the body. `Operator Input Needed` adds `: <condition> (<address>)`, truncated to 99 characters. `Resolved:` repeats the original subject.

| Alert | Subject |
|---|---|
| Items waiting on a person (stale items, queued step-ups, outbound reminders, send breaker tripped, Claude review queue older than `claude_review_reminder_hours` (24; operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-115), a send scheduled in 10 minutes, a possible second install, Gmail's download limit reached (V1.6)) | `[ecf-alert] Operator Input Needed: <condition> (<address>)` |
| Mail provider unreachable for 15 minutes while the network is up (confirmed by the operator 2026-09-27, OD-113) | `[ecf-alert] Mail Provider Unreachable` |
| App password rejected 3 times (then retried hourly; `ecf address retry` forces a retry; names `ecf address set --app-password`; for a Gmail address it adds that Google revokes app passwords when the account password changes and that they need 2-Step Verification, and names myaccount.google.com/apppasswords: support.google.com/accounts/answer/185833, verified 2026-10-05) | `[ecf-alert] Mailbox Login Rejected` |
| Service crash, dead-lettered jobs, TypeSafe Jev down for preset D (`jev_down`, install-wide, its text kept current; emails Jev couldn't classify in 3 tries, one alert per drain; v3.0.0 step 4, OD-510), Models API failure or a pinned model it doesn't list (V1.4 step 10), sender authentication unavailable, 2 consecutive export failures, Claude work refused for an unpinned model | `[ecf-alert] System Error` |
| Slack posts failing or token revoked (names `slack set-tokens`; `slack reauthorize` only for `missing_scope`; takes precedence over System Error for Slack jobs); a post that gave up, once, as `Slack Delivery Failed: a post wasn't sent` (OD-557) | `[ecf-alert] Slack Delivery Failed` |
| Pinned model gets a retirement date (repeated 30 and 7 days before; from `models.lock`, §7.6) | `[ecf-alert] Model Retirement Scheduled` |
| Fraud guard hit; one email per item, up to 10 an hour; weak first-time + payment goes to the digest instead (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-114) | `[ecf-alert] Possible Fraud Attempt` |
| Regulator trigger or `regulatory` category; up to 10 an hour | `[ecf-alert] Regulatory Mail Notice` |
| Unverified payment sender on a `high` address; at most one batched email an hour | `[ecf-alert] Unverified Payment Sender` |
| Export/import/restore, destroy, sensitivity downgrade, security-relevant config, alert routing, step-up settings, model override, Slack tokens/member ID | `[ecf-alert] Security Notice` |
| Recovery | `[ecf-alert] Resolved: <original subject>` |

Newer models and releases are daily-summary lines only, no email.

**V1.1 (built 2026-09-29):** the two mail-health alerts only, delivered as desktop notifications and shown by `ecf status` and `ecf doctor` (OD-190). An alert is notified once when it opens and once when a later check succeeds (`Resolved:`); opening and resolving are audited (`alert.opened`, `alert.resolved`). "Network up" means the provider's host name resolves through the system resolver, so an offline computer never raises Mail Provider Unreachable and no third party is contacted (operator decision 2026-09-29, OD-198). After 3 rejected logins, checks of that address run hourly; `ecf address retry` makes it due now, and a new app password clears the count. macOS notifications run `/usr/bin/osascript` with the text passed through `on run argv`; Linux desktops use `notify-send`; the `notifications` setting `off` disables them. Notifications carry the address ID and host name only. `ecf doctor` adds, per address, the last check and its error, open alerts, whether `org_domains` is set, and a DNS check (a known `_dmarc` record resolves; 1.5 s timeout).

**In V1.2** (step 9, 2026-09-30; code: `ecf_server/alerts.py`): every alert reads `[ecf-alert] <Title>` on the desktop and in Slack, and `[ecf-alert] Resolved: <Title>` when it clears; Operator Input Needed adds `: <condition> (<address>)`. Routes: `alerts.routes` (default `slack`) and per class `alerts.<class>.routes` for `mail`, `system` and `operator`, changed with `ecf alerts set [<class>] --to slack` (step-up bound to the class, the new routes and the current value; a Security Notice follows). Email routes are refused with "email alerts arrive in V1.5, when ecf can send email" (OD-206). `ecf alerts show` lists them; `ecf alerts test` sends a test alert on every route. Desktop notifications always go too, unless `notifications: off`. In Slack plus the desktop: Mail Provider Unreachable and Mailbox Login Rejected (posted to the summary channel by the Slack thread when they open and when they resolve; migration 0017 marks what was posted, and reopening posts again), System Error, Operator Input Needed and Security Notice. Desktop only: Slack Delivery Failed. System Error sources in V1.2: a start that follows a crash; background jobs that gave up (the `actions` and `slack_in` queues, reported once each; dead Slack posts are Slack Delivery Failed's); and a crash-loop breaker trip, which the service reports on the desktop and posts straight to the summary channel before it exits (best effort: the queue would never send it). Operator Input Needed covers approvals and answers queued for step-up and a Slack channel ecf couldn't create. Email alerts arrive in V1.5 (OD-206) and Model Retirement Scheduled in V1.4.

**In V1.4** (step 9, 2026-10-02; code: `ecf_server/claude_review.py`, `claude_queue.py`, `daily.py`; operator decision 2026-10-02, OD-298): **the Claude review reminder.** Each tick, for each C address that isn't paused (a paused address isn't offered to `/ecf-review`), while any item has waited for `/ecf-review` longer than `claude_review_reminder_hours` (install-wide, 24, 1-168, `ecf settings set claude_review_reminder_hours <hours>`), one `[ecf-alert] Operator Input Needed: Claude review waiting (<address>)` is open, saying how many and since when, and that `ecf claude` then `/ecf-review` clears it; `Resolved:` follows when none has. The wait counts from when the item entered the queue (`items.claude_since`, §4.3); items a session has claimed still count. A mail check doesn't resolve it. The daily summary's per-address line counts "N waiting for /ecf-review" apart from "waiting for the classifier", and a line "Waiting for /ecf-review more than N h: M (per address; the oldest since <time> UTC)" appears while any has.

**The escalation** (v3.0.0, ADR 0031, R-D4, P10): with no local fallback, the alert kind `claude_review_overdue` ("Operator Input Needed: Claude review overdue") opens while any item of an address has waited longer than twice `claude_review_reminder_hours` (48 h by default). It is in `LOUD_KINDS` (it mentions you in Slack), carries counts and dates only (no subject, sender or excerpt) skips paused addresses, and resolves once no item has waited that long (a mail check doesn't resolve it). Alert rows of the removed kinds (`local_model`, `local_model_unsafe`, `model_failures`, `local_model_server`) are deleted by migration 0038; `models_missing` is the model watch's Claude-pin alert and stays. Slack and alert email skip a kind they don't know, and the desktop and lists show it as a System Error (`health.title`; P11).

**As built in V1.5** (step 7a, 2026-10-02; code: `ecf_server/alert_mail.py`, `alerts.py`, `outbound_msg.py`, `service.py`; migration 0029; operator decisions 2026-10-02, OD-333 to OD-336): **alert email.** `ecf alerts email set --from <address> --to <destination>` turns it on (OD-333): `--from` is a watched address whose SMTP login sends, `--to` a plain address that isn't a watched one. It needs step-up bound to both and the current setting, sends a Security Notice (by email too, and to the old destination when it changes), then a test email, and makes the install-wide routes `slack,email` when they were the default. `ecf alerts email off` (step-up) sends a last Security Notice to the old destination, then takes `email` out of every route (a route left empty returns to the default). `ecf alerts set` accepts `email` only while alert email is on; Slack Delivery Failed may go to `email`, never `slack`. `ecf alerts show` names the sender and destination; `ecf alerts test` also queues a test email. `ecf address remove` refuses the sending address. **What is emailed** when its class is routed to email: open and resolved alerts (queued each tick and marked whether or not routed, as the Slack sweep does, so turning email on sends no backlog); one-off alerts; Security Notices (whenever alert email is on); Operator Input Needed raised outside the alert table (an approval queued for step-up, a Slack channel problem, the five full outbound reminders); and the crash-loop System Error, sent synchronously as the service exits, best effort. Possible Fraud Attempt, Regulatory Mail Notice, Unverified Payment Sender, the 10-minute send email and loop suppression (OD-330) are step 7b; the first three go by email whenever the install-wide `alerts.routes` include `email` (OD-334). **The message** (`outbound_msg.build_alert`): From the sending address, To the destination, Subject the alert's title cut to 99 characters, body the desktop notification's text and a fixed footer, `Auto-Submitted: auto-generated`, `X-ECF-Install`, a random Message-ID on the sender's domain chosen before the first try and the Date of queueing, so every try sends the same bytes. It is recorded in `sent` (kind `alert`; no Sent-folder copy), so its copy coming back is skipped as ecf's own mail. **Delivery:** an outbox (`alert_outbox`) drained every 10 s by the service's alert-mail thread, so the timer never waits on SMTP; each row keeps the sender and destination of when it was queued. **Caps:** past 10 an hour for a type (its title without the condition) or 30 an hour in all, an alert is held for its type's roll-up and posted to Slack at once if Slack wasn't a route for it; once the oldest held one is an hour old, one email lists them (`[ecf-alert] <Title>: N more in the last hour`). Roll-ups count toward neither cap, so at most 30 plus one per type go out in an hour (OD-336). **Fallback** (OD-335): a send the server doesn't accept is tried again after 30 s and 2 min; after the third try, or at once when the server refuses it for good, the login is rejected, the app password is missing or the outcome is unknown, the alert is posted to the summary channel if Slack didn't have it (it already reached the desktop where it was raised), audited `alert.email_fallback`, and `[ecf-alert] System Error` (`alert_email`) stays open until an alert email goes through. While the sending address has Mail Provider Unreachable or Mailbox Login Rejected open, nothing is tried: alerts fall back at once, without that System Error (OD-328). Outbox rows settled more than 7 days ago are deleted. Audit: `alerts.email_set`, `alerts.email_off`, `alert.email_fallback`; `security.notice` gains `email`. `ecf doctor`'s warning that a Slack failure reaches nobody with notifications off is dropped when Slack Delivery Failed is emailed. **Fixed:** the Slack thread's alert posts failed on "possible second install" and "send limit reached" (step 3c and 5 alerts missing from its title table); every alert kind now has one title and one class, checked by a test.

**As built in V1.5** (step 7b, 2026-10-03; code: `ecf_server/alert_items.py`, `own_mail.py`, `policy.py`, `triggers.py`, `approvals.py`; migration 0030; operator decisions 2026-10-02, OD-337, OD-338): **mail-content alert email**, sent whenever the install-wide `alerts.routes` include `email` (OD-334); Slack already has the escalation card or digest line. **Possible Fraud Attempt:** one per escalated item with a fraud signal (a fraud trigger, quarantine, the `fraud_guard` rule, a classifier fraud risk of medium or high, or `vendor_change_request`), naming the address, the item's short ID, which of those held, and `ecf item show <id>`. **Regulatory Mail Notice:** one per escalated item with the regulator trigger, the `regulatory` category or rule and no fraud signal. Other escalations (an urgent bug report) aren't emailed. Both are capped like every alert email: 10 an hour per type, then the hourly roll-up (OD-114). Each escalation is handled once (`escalations.emailed_at`), whether or not email is a route, so routing email later sends no backlog; escalations from before migration 0030 count as handled. **Unverified Payment Sender:** on `high` addresses only, at most one email an hour listing, per address, the rule 1a items since the last one (count, short IDs, `ecf inbox --address`); items also escalated as fraud are left to their own email; a human-verified sender doesn't fire rule 1a (OD-065). **Send scheduled:** when a send on a `high` address starts its 10-minute delay, `[ecf-alert] Operator Input Needed: send scheduled in 10 minutes (<address>)` with the item and `ecf cancel <id>`, once (not again after a wake). **Loop suppression** (OD-330; `own_mail.alert_echo`, fact `alert_echo`): a delivery report (`multipart/report; report-type=delivery-status`) whose `In-Reply-To`, `References` or returned headers (any `Message-ID:` line in it) cite a recorded alert email is `bounce`; an automatic reply (`Auto-Submitted` other than `no`, or `X-Autoreply`) citing one in `In-Reply-To` or `References` is `auto_reply`; an alert email itself (its Message-ID recorded as an alert, any `X-ECF-Install` value this install's) arriving in a watched mailbox without passing DMARC (so not skipped as own mail) is `copy`, and fraud trigger 9 doesn't fire on it (OD-338). Such mail is classified as usual; then, unless the plan escalates or a fraud or regulatory signal holds, the plan becomes label `alert_echo` + leave with no actor (rule `alert_echo`; OD-337), and it never raises an alert email itself. A person's own reply to an alert (no `Auto-Submitted`) is an ordinary item. **Old mail** (v3.0.0 step 5, OD-507; operator decision 2026-10-14, review M5): an item a scan or reprocess marked (§5.4) raises none of these three emails; its escalation is marked handled, and its run's Slack summary lists it and mentions you.

### 13.4 Token and speed metrics (operator decision 2026-09-26, OD-116)

- **Gemma, exact** (removed in v3.0.0, ADR 0031): from each Ollama response (`prompt_eval_count`, `prompt_eval_cached_count`, `eval_count`, `prompt_eval_duration`, `eval_duration`, `load_duration`, `total_duration` in ns): input, cached and output tokens; prompt speed `(prompt_eval_count − prompt_eval_cached_count) ÷ prompt_eval_duration` (the duration covers uncached tokens only, verified 2026-09-27, docs.ollama.com; `prompt_eval_count` includes cached tokens, measured 2026-09-30, V1.3 step 0, Ollama 0.35.0 (Homebrew) on the Mac17,3 Air, 24 GB, on AC); generation speed; load time. Tagged with address, preset, stage and role.
- **Claude, via Claude Code telemetry:** `ecf claude` sets `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1`, OTLP exporters to the local receiver with `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/json`. Signals: `claude_code.token.usage` (by `type`, `model`, `query_source`), `claude_code.api_request` (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `duration_ms`, `model`; the duration likely includes prompt processing and network, an inference), `claude_code.cost.usage` shown only as an "API-equivalent" figure.
- **Plan allowance:** the status-line JSON's `rate_limits.five_hour.used_percentage` and `seven_day.used_percentage` with `resets_at` (Pro and Max only; absent on Team and Enterprise, verified 2026-09-27, code.claude.com statusline docs; also available behind a Claude apps gateway). `ecf claude` installs a status-line script in its config that forwards only those numbers and the session ID; the service records them at the start and end of each `/ecf-review`. On Team/Enterprise `ecf stats` reports tokens and API-equivalent cost only.
- **Privacy settings:** `ecf claude` sets `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=0`, `OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES=0`, `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=0`, `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT=0`, `OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES=0`, `OTEL_LOG_MANAGED_SETTINGS=0`, `OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_ACCOUNT_UUID=false`. The receiver keeps only model, token counts, durations, `query_source` and session ID.
- **Reporting:** `ecf stats [--since] [--address] [--preset]`: tokens by model and role, tokens per email, speeds (median, p95), load times; one daily-summary line; the same figures in `ecf eval compare`. Claude figures are exact per review and per model, approximate per email. Metrics follow `log_retention_days`.
- **As built in V1.3** (step 9, 2026-10-01; code: `ecf_server/stats.py`, `ecf/cli_stats.py`; Gemma only, Claude figures arrive with V1.4): `ecf stats [--since 24h|7d|…] [--address] [--preset]` (default 7 days; `GET /v1/stats`) reports, by model (manifest digest) and role and for all roles together: calls and failures; input (with cached) and output tokens; tokens per email (every role's tokens over the emails classified, i.e. successful classifier calls); reading and writing speed in tokens/s as the median and the **slowest 5%** (the 5th percentile: a high percentile of a speed would show the fastest calls; as built 2026-10-01); seconds per call and model load time as median and p95, with loads over 1 s counted as cold starts. The daily summary adds one line for the last 24 hours when the model ran. Each eval run's result summary keeps the same figures for its own calls (they aren't added to `model_calls`, so eval traffic doesn't mix with mail), and `ecf eval compare` prints them for both runs.
- **As built in V1.4** (step 6, 2026-10-02; code: `ecf_server/claude_usage.py`, `ecf/cli_stats.py`): each API request in an `ecf claude` session's telemetry becomes a `claude_calls` row (time, session, model, source: `main` for the main session, `agent` for ecf's plugin agents, else the raw `query_source`; tokens in, out, cache read and written; duration; `cost_usd` when sent), and each session a `claude_sessions` row (start and end; plan usage at the first and last status-line reading; items it submitted work for; refusals by the model check). Plan usage is recorded per `ecf claude` session, not per `/ecf-review` run. `ecf stats` adds a Claude part when no `--address` is given and the preset is B, C or not given (Claude's figures aren't split by address): sessions, emails, tokens per email (a session's tokens over the items it submitted work for, approximate), refusals, and by model and source: requests, tokens, seconds per request (median and p95) and the API-equivalent cost ("not a charge on a plan"); then the plan usage after the last review. The daily summary adds a Claude line when Claude was used in the last 24 hours. Both tables follow `log_retention_days`. `ecf eval compare` shows a Claude eval's figures from these tables (V1.4 step 7, §16.2).

- **Stages and Slack** (v3.0.0 step 5, OD-507; plan §5, P17-P19; code: `timings.py`, `slack_out.py`, `checks.py`, `mail/`): `ecf stats` adds a Slack block from `slack_calls` (one row per post job when it completes: queued to done, tries, seconds in Slack calls, rate-limit holds and pacing; the key's kind only; median, p95, retries, holds). `ecf stats --stages` gives each stage's median, p95 and n: a stage is one `item.transitioned` row's `(from, to)`, timed from the item's previous row; the wait for `/ecf-review` runs from an item's first `awaiting_claude` to its next `classified`; old mail (§5.4) is reported apart and imported items are left out. Each `check.completed` row carries `timings`: the mailbox's own IMAP seconds by phase (connect and login, select, search with its NOOP, fetch of new mail, fetch of backfilled mail, store) and the isolation children's (their wall time, DKIM/DMARC seconds, DNS answers without the network and network queries, approximate under parallel prefetch). Measured costs (CPU, median of 5, this Mac, 2026-10-14; main `1daf644` → this branch): `classifier.store` with its audit row 1.10 → 1.18 ms per item; a 30-message `fetch_page` 23.7 → 23.6 ms; a backfill page over 1,000 old messages 23.1 → 23.7 ms; a 5-message check through the isolate 13.6 → 13.7 ms (this process); `ecf stats --stages` over 400k transitions 1.8 s.

### 13.5 Recovery

`ecf inbox` and "Needs you" list everything waiting on a person. `ecf item show`, `item resolve --reason` and `item requeue` (audited) handle `failed`, `failed_unknown` and stuck `executing`; `needs_human` goes back through `proposed` or `item resolve`. After a revoked token: `ecf slack set-tokens`, then `ecf slack reauthorize`. After `Mailbox Login Rejected`: `ecf address set <address> --app-password` stores the new password, checks resume, and `Resolved:` is sent (operator decision 2026-09-27, OD-119). The admin guide covers these plus a stolen-laptop runbook, a lost backup key, a locked secret store, crash-loop recovery, mailbox reset, and tuning size and scan limits.

### 13.6 Two installs on one mailbox

Messages carrying another install's `$ecf_<install>_*` keywords, or a mismatched `X-ECF-Install` on DMARC-passing, ecf-shaped mail from this install's own address, pause the address and send `Operator Input Needed`. This install's own keywords without a local record are adopted silently.

**As built in V1.5** (step 10b, 2026-10-03; code: `ecf_server/keywords.py`, `fetch.py`, `checks.py`, `health.py`, `policy.py`; OD-318, OD-372): until 10b nothing read keywords on incoming mail; only the `X-ECF-Install` check (step 3c) existed. Each check now reads the flags of the page it fetches in one request (deferred large mail: one request each), and sorts ecf's keywords case-insensitively by the install *name* in `$ecf_<install>_<label>`. Another install's keyword pauses the address (audit `address.paused`, why `second_install`) and raises `Operator Input Needed: possible second install`. This install's keyword on mail newer than the address's restored cursor (same UIDVALIDITY) within 7 days of a restore pauses it (why `restored_keywords`) and raises `[ecf-alert] Operator Input Needed: ecf's labels on new mail after a restore`, resolved at the first check after `ecf resume` (OD-318, OD-372; `restore.cursors` is written by restore). Otherwise this install's keywords are adopted: the email gets an item as usual, its labels go in `facts.ecf_keywords`, and no reply, draft or forward is made for it (policy's send guardrail, at proposal and at execution); labels already there stay, and a message still in INBOX wasn't moved (operator decision 2026-10-03). Two installs with the same name can't be told apart by keywords; the `X-ECF-Install` header still tells them apart on ecf's sent mail.

### 13.7 After a gap

On the first check after a gap the digest opens with "Caught up: N messages since <time>" and links `ecf inbox`; "Needs you" and the daily summary show what's waiting. The README states what a week away costs. A computer left on keeps processing around the clock (the `resident` setting was removed in v3.0.0, ADR 0031).

| `sensitivity_downgrade_delay_minutes` | 0 (local) | 0 in local mode | OD 2026-09-26 |

| Key | Default | Range / values | Origin |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sensitivity` | none; must be chosen | `standard`, `high` | RV |
| `stage` | `shadow` | `shadow`, `assist`, `live` | RV |
| `outbound` | off | on, off | OD 2026-09-25 (Review 4) |
| `preset`, pair | chosen at add | C (D, built in step 4, is held back, OD-516; A and B removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031)) | OD 2026-09-26, OD-506 |

| `max_message_bytes` | 64 MB `high`, 16 MB `standard`; capped at the provider's limit when the probe found a smaller one (OD-196) | 1-64 MB (OD-220) | OD 2026-09-26 |

| `max_sends_per_hour` / `_per_day` | 25 / 250; Gmail addresses `_per_day` 100 (V1.6, §18) | 1-500 / 1-5,000 (`send_limits.BOUNDS`) | OD 2026-09-26 |
| `approval_ttl_days_send` / `approval_ttl_days` | 4 / 14 | 1-60 (P) | OD 2026-09-26 |

| intervals, business hours | install defaults | as above | OD 2026-09-26 |

**`ecf settings show|set` in V1.2** (step 10a, 2026-09-30; code: `ecf_server/settings.py`): `set` changes only keys something reads today. For the install, or one address with `--address`: `business_hours` (written `mon-fri 08:00-17:00 America/New_York`), `mail_fetch_interval_workday` and `_offhours`, and the `catch_up*` keys. Install only: `notifications` (read when the service starts), `deadman_offhours` (OD-219) and `stale_item_days`. Per address: `max_message_bytes` and `max_scan_bytes_per_part` (1 to 64 MB: 64 MB is the largest size whose memory use was measured, OD-195, and raising it needs a new measurement; operator decision 2026-09-30, OD-220), `approval_ttl_days` and `approval_ttl_days_send`. Address values are stored in the address's overrides and win over install values. Each change is audited (`settings.changed`). None of these needs step-up (§9.6). Every other key in the tables above is refused with where it lives, when it arrives, or that it is fixed (V1.2 review, 2026-09-30: the registry now names each one). `slack_member_id` goes through `ecf slack set-member`, which `ecf settings set slack_member_id` also calls; `alerts.*` through `ecf alerts set`; `org_domains` and other security-relevant config through `ecf config apply`; `log_retention_days` through `ecf retention set` (step 11). `resident`, `review_sample_rate`, `label_folder`, `escalations_per_hour` and `max_per_check` (OD-228) are settable since V1.3, `ollama_log_max_mb` and `ollama_log_rotate_days` (install only, OD-266) since V1.3.1; `claude_queue_timeout` (OD-227; its own step-up path, §4.3), `classifier_high_batch` (preset C only; step-up to raise it, §7.5, OD-297) and the install's `claude_review_reminder_hours` (§13.3, OD-298) since V1.4; the export and send-limit keys in V1.5. `resident`, `ollama_log_max_mb`, `ollama_log_rotate_days` and `claude_queue_timeout` were removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031; `settings set` refuses them).

## 15. Contracts [proposed; accepted 2026-09-27, OD-162]

### 15.1 Socket HTTP routes

Callers: **CLI** (token file), **MCP-W** (WORK profile token), **MCP-O** (OBSERVE), **Svc** (internal only). Decision and settings routes refuse MCP profile tokens. All bodies are JSON; errors are problem+json.

| Verb | Path | Callers | Request → response |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/v1/status` | CLI, MCP-O, MCP-W | none → per-address stage, pause, backlog, ETA, breaker state, last tick |
| GET | `/v1/counts` | CLI, MCP-O, MCP-W | `address_id?` → counts by status |
| GET | `/v1/inbox` | CLI | `address_id?`, `stale?` → open items needing a person (id, address, status, age, summary) |
| GET | `/v1/items/{id}` | CLI | → item detail: facts, classification, proposal, grant, history, excerpt |
| POST | `/v1/items/{id}/approve` · `/reject` · `/cancel` | CLI | `{grant_id, nonce_id?}` → new status or `stepup_required` |
| POST | `/v1/items/{id}/answer` | CLI | `{text, nonce_id?}` → new status |
| POST | `/v1/items/{id}/resolve` · `/requeue` | CLI | `{reason}` / `{nonce_id?}` → new status |
| POST | `/v1/items/resolve` | CLI | `{older_than_days?, ids?, reason, nonce_id?}` → count resolved |
| POST | `/v1/approvals/pending` | CLI | `{confirm_ids?, nonce_id?}` → list to confirm, then results |
| POST | `/v1/stepup/nonces` | CLI | `{purpose, target}` → `{nonce_id, code, prompt_text, expires_at, needs_password}` (the service computes the bound hash and the text from the target; V1.2 step 2) |
| POST | `/v1/stepup/{nonce}/verify` | CLI | `{password?}` (Linux PAM only) → `{verified}` |
| POST | `/v1/checks` | CLI | `{address_id?}` → progress stream (JSON lines), final summary (`until_empty` and the model round removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031)) |
| POST | `/v1/backfill` | CLI | `{address_id, since, act?}` → `{address_id, since, act}`; queues a check (V1.2 step 11b). From v3.0.0 step 5 (OD-507): `since` and `until?` UTC times from the range parser (a bare date is still accepted, UTC midnight, for v2.2.x clients), `typed?`, `nonce_id?`; → adds `until`, `run_id`. `act` needs the done count of that range; over 500, step-up `backfill_act` |
| POST | `/v1/backfill/count` | CLI | `{address_id, since, until?}` → the count asked; the next check answers (OD-507, P11) |
| GET | `/v1/backfill/count` | CLI | `address_id` → `{state, since, until, in_range, held, to_classify, estimate}` |
| POST | `/v1/reprocess` | CLI | `{address_id, since, until?, rules_only?, force?, dry_run?, typed?, nonce_id?}` → the dry run's counts, or the run started (OD-507; plan §4) |
| GET | `/v1/reprocess` | CLI | → each address's reprocess: running, or the last one's outcome |
| POST | `/v1/reprocess/stop` | CLI | `{address_id}` → counts so far |
| POST | `/v1/approvals/scan/{run}` | CLI | `{confirm_ids?, nonce_id?}` → a run's waiting approvals, then results (step-up `approve_scan`) |
| POST | `/v1/items/{ref}/undo` | CLI | → `{id, undo}`: the digest's Undo, at the next check (OD-507; plan §4.3) |
| GET | `/v1/backfill` | CLI | → each address's backfill: running, or the last one's outcome; items read and how many fired a fraud trigger (V1.2 step 11b; review 2026-09-30) |
| POST | `/v1/backfill/stop` | CLI | `{address_id}` → `{address_id, items}`: ends the backfill; what was read stays (V1.2 review, 2026-09-30) |
| POST | `/v1/service/stopping` | CLI | → `{ok}`: the next stop is on purpose, so it disarms the dead-man's switch (`ecf service stop`, `uninstall`; OD-222) |
| GET/POST/DELETE | `/v1/addresses`, `/v1/addresses/{id}` | CLI | add/set fields, `nonce_id?` → address record; list (with `org_domains`; from V1.6 also `org_addresses` (a count), `public_domains` and `imap_defaults` (domain → IMAP server), and each record's `max_sends_per_day`, null for the default); remove → residue list |
| GET | `/v1/stages` | CLI | → each address's stage, label, days in stage, sensitivity, paused, held count (V1.2 step 10a) |
| POST | `/v1/addresses/{id}/stage` · `/sensitivity` · `/outbound` · `/pause` · `/resume` · `/retry` | CLI | `{value, reason?, nonce_id?}` → new state, gate or review status; `/resume` of an address converted at v3.0.0 and not yet consented is refused (409) unless the body has `owner_agreed: true` (§4.3) |
| GET | `/v1/addresses/{id}/outbound` | CLI | → `ecf outbound report`: track record, `high` gate, latest suppressed proposals and sends, send limits, reminder schedule; `POST` also takes `value` `resume`, `snooze` (`days`) and `dismiss` (V1.5 steps 5-6) |
| POST | `/v1/pause-all` · `/v1/resume-all` | CLI | → the addresses that changed (V1.2 step 8a) |
| GET | `/v1/senders?sender=&address_id=` | CLI | → sender record (category, expected Reply-To, verified, DMARC pass count, shared platform) (V1.2 step 10c) |
| POST | `/v1/senders/confirm` · `/reply-to` · `/verified` | CLI | `{sender, address_id?}` plus `{category}` / `{domain}` (null clears) / `{on}`, and `nonce_id?` → sender record (V1.2 step 10c) |
| GET/POST | `/v1/settings` | CLI | `{key, value, address_id?, nonce_id?}` → setting; GET → all settings |
| POST | `/v1/config/apply` | CLI | `{document, dry_run?, nonce_id?}` → `{changed, applied, changes: [{section, change}], sha256}`; step-up (V1.2 step 10b) |
| POST | `/v1/rules/test` | CLI | `{rules, cases_dir}` (absolute) → per-case outcomes under current and proposed rules, `changed`, `skipped`, `expected_matched` (V1.2 step 10b) |
| POST | `/v1/eval/mistral` | CLI | `{root, case, model}` (an absolute generated PROD set, one of its case ids, a listed Mistral grader) → the set checked (`gen.verify`), the email read and the fixed grading prompt built by the service, one Mistral chat-completions call with the key from the secret store (strict `json_schema`, no tools, 120 s) → `{status, answer?, usage, detail, retry_after?}`; status `ok`, `rate_limit`, `auth`, `provider`, `failed` or `too large`, never Mistral's text; nothing logged (`ecf eval grade --grader mistral:<model>`, OD-540) |
| POST | `/v1/eval/expect` | CLI | `{root, variants?}` (root absolute, a generated set; `variants`: per case id an object of `sender_type`, `priority`, `category` and/or `deadline_mentioned` (`labels.VARIED`, OD-563) to a list of schema values, true or false for a yes/no field, no other field; the service builds every combination, at most 54 (`labels.max_variants()`: three judges); the body may be up to 2 MiB on this route alone, other routes 64 KiB) → `rules_digest` and per case `id`, `rule`, `safety` (`must_escalate`, `must_not_hide`) and `error` under the starter rules with the shipped schema (as `ecf eval run`), the card's labels standing in for the classifier, plus per variant its `labels`, `rule`, `safety` and `error` with the variant merged into the card's labels before they stand in; writes nothing (`ecf eval expect`, OD-534; eval plan draft 21, OD-549) |
| POST | `/v1/secrets/{name}` | CLI | `{value, nonce_id?}` → `{stored}` (write-only; never returned) |
| GET | `/v1/slack` | CLI | → app, workspace, member, pending member, connection (V1.2 step 4) |
| POST | `/v1/slack/app` | CLI | configuration token → app ID (`apps.manifest.create`; token and returned credentials not kept) |
| POST | `/v1/slack/install` | CLI | bot token, app-level token, member ID → install status (a DM asks the member to confirm) |
| POST | `/v1/slack/tokens` · `/member` | CLI | new tokens or member ID, `stepup_nonce` → install status (step-up, Security Notice) |
| POST | `/v1/slack/reauthorize` · `/refresh` | CLI | configuration token → `permissions_updated`; `/refresh` (`ecf slack repost`, and the CLI after reauthorize) refuses when Slack isn't installed, moves waiting approval cards out of a forgotten channel, draws waiting approval cards again with their current grant, sends the rest again, clears approval cards' dead posts, and returns `queued`, `reposting`, `not_recovered`, `backlog_held` (OD-557; additive, `api_version` stays 1) |
| POST | `/v1/slack/remove` | CLI | `{install, config_token?, nonce_id?}` → what was done and what is left by hand, for `ecf slack remove` (step-up) |
| GET · POST | `/v1/alerts` · POST `/v1/alerts/test` · POST `/v1/alerts/email` · POST `/v1/alerts/email/off` | CLI | GET → routes per class and the alert email sender and destination; POST `{class?, to, nonce_id?}` → routes (step-up); test → where it was sent; email `{from, to, nonce_id?}` → `ecf alerts email set`, email/off `{nonce_id?}` → `ecf alerts email off` (both step-up; V1.5 step 7a) |
| GET · POST | `/v1/destroy` | CLI | GET → `{install, install_id, role, addresses, slack: {app_id, channels}, export_dir, last_export_at, busy, record}`; POST `{install, config_token?, nonce_id?}` → the record with `residue` (step-up; the service stops afterwards; V1.5 step 12a) |
| POST | `/v1/upgrade/finish` | CLI | `{from, to, label, started_at, pin_changes, affected}` → the record (V1.5 step 11b) |
| GET | `/v1/upgrade/state` | CLI | → `{version, schema_version, data_format, api_version, classifier_schema, prompt_digest, effective_prompt_digest, extension_stored, extension_pending, pins, pin_users, install_role, busy: {executing, leases, claude_sessions}, upgrade}` (V1.5 step 11a; §11.10; `extension_pending`, v3.0.0 S4: the C addresses a stored, not yet used extension moves at the next start) |
| GET | `/v1/export` | CLI | → `{key: {generation, fingerprint, created_at}?, previous, dir, same_volume}` (V1.5 step 8a) and `{schedule, keep, last_ok, failures, last_error, set_up}` (step 8b) |
| POST | `/v1/export/now` | CLI | → `{ok, error?}` or `{ok, dir, file, seq, bytes, sha256, at, counts, key_generation, pruned}`: a scheduled export at once (V1.5 step 8b) |
| POST | `/v1/export/keys/new` · `/v1/export/keys` · `/v1/export/dir` | CLI | keys/new → `{pending_id, key_text, fingerprint, replaces, expires_at}` (the key text only here, once); keys `{pending_id, fingerprint, nonce_id?}` and dir `{path, fingerprint, nonce_id?}` → as GET (both step-up; V1.5 step 8a) |
| GET · POST | `/v1/export/passphrase` · `/v1/export` | CLI | GET → `{passphrase}` (six fresh words, not kept); POST `{path, passphrase, nonce_id?}` → `{path, seq, bytes, sha256, signed}` (step-up bound to the path; V1.5 step 9a) |
| POST | `/v1/import/inspect` · `/v1/import` | CLI | inspect `{path}` → what the header says (kind, signed, own, install, time, seq, schema) without secrets; import `{path, secret, dry_run: true}` → the preview (V1.5 step 9b); `{path, secret, replace?, install?, nonce_id?}` → `{source_install, counts, config_changes, replace}` (step-up; step 9c) |
| POST | `/v1/restore` | CLI | `{path, secret, backup_key?, dry_run: true}` → the preview; `{path, secret, backup_key?, stopped, older_ok, nonce_id?}` → `{counts, generation, safety_copy, addresses, config_changes}` (step-up; V1.5 step 10a) |
| GET | `/v1/doctor/slack` | CLI | → `{checks: [{name, level, detail, fix}]}`: Slack and step-up, run by the service (V1.2 step 12a) |
| GET | `/v1/doctor/ops` | CLI | → `{checks: [{name, level, detail, fix}]}`: SMTP, alert email and its reach, backups, run by the service (V1.5 step 13a); the `schema` row (v2.0.0) |
| GET | `/v1/schema` | CLI, MCP-O, MCP-W | → `{version, extension, digest}`: the effective schema (the install's extension or null; v2.0.0, OD-478) |
| POST | `/v1/digests` | CLI | `{address_id}` → `{address_id, posted, since}`: the digest now (operator decision 2026-09-30) |
| GET | `/v1/init` | CLI | → `{install_role, slack_installed, slack_member, slack_pending_app, org_domains, addresses}` (V1.2 step 11c); `claude_needed` (V1.4; `models` and `fallback_off` removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031)); `smtp_addresses`, `alert_email`, `export {key, dir, schedule, last_ok}`, `skipped {step: time}` (V1.5 step 13b); `org_addresses` (a count), `public_only` (V1.6 step 2) |
| POST | `/v1/init/role` | CLI | `{install_role}` → set once, then refused (V1.2 step 11c) |
| POST | `/v1/init/skip` | CLI | `{step: email\|export}` → records the declined step (`init.skipped.<step>`), audited (V1.5 step 13b) |
| GET | `/v1/retention` | CLI | → `{days, last_run}` (V1.2 step 11a) |
| POST | `/v1/retention` | CLI | `{days, nonce_id}` → `{days, was, changed}` (V1.2 step 11a) |
| GET | `/v1/stats` · `/v1/logs` | CLI | filters → metrics; audit events |
| POST · DELETE | `/v1/sessions`, `/v1/sessions/{id}` | CLI (`ecf claude`) | `{client: {version, plugin_digest}}` (v2.2.0; §10.3) → `{session_id, profile_token, telemetry_port, telemetry_bearer, models, waiting, last_plan}`; revoke (held submissions settled first) |
| POST | `/v1/review-queue` | MCP-W | `{address_id?, limit?}` → claimed items (id, need, agent, claim token), `more`; results of the session's ended claims (POST: it claims; V1.4 step 3) |
| POST | `/v1/claims/{id}/message` | MCP-W | `{claim_token}` → untrusted-email wrapper (POST keeps the token out of the URL; V1.4 step 3) |
| POST | `/v1/claims/{id}/classification` · `/proposal` | MCP-W | claim token + payload → `{accepted, errors}` |
| POST/GET | `/v1/eval/runs`, `/v1/eval/runs/{id}/…` | CLI (V1.3); MCP-W added with `/ecf-eval` (V1.4) | start run; next case; submit prediction → metrics only (proposed; as built, the V1.3 service runs the cases itself and `/ecf-eval` uses the routes below, OD-287) |
| POST/GET | `/v1/eval/runs` (V1.3) | CLI | start a run in the service `{root, classifier, fraud_only, backend, redact, for_gate, signals, copy_to, jev_concurrency}` (backend `null` or `jev`, §7.9; `jev` needs the TypeSafe key) → progress; GET → the current run and the 5 latest results. `actor`, `battery_floor`, the Gemma and `systemone:` backends and model-driven corpus runs are removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031), and `jev_state` and `jev_preamble` in step 3 (OD-512); a request naming a `corpus_session` is refused (real mail would reach Jev only through a preset D address, held back, OD-516; P5) |
| POST | `/v1/eval/rescore` (§16.7) | CLI | `{result, corpus_session}` → a corpus result scored again against the current labels; `{result, synthetic_root, through_policy}` → a synthetic result mapped to v2, or planned again through today's facts and policy (§16.2); written beside the original; no model runs |
| POST | `/v1/eval/routes` (§16.2) | CLI | `{sets, results, corpus_session?}` → the route report: each set's routes three ways, each result's changed cases attributed (on the first set), an open corpus's routes; no model runs |
| POST | `/v1/eval/runs/stop` (V1.3) | CLI | → progress; the run ends after its current case; from V1.4 step 7 `{local, claude}`: a Claude eval ends at once and saves what was scored |
| POST | `/v1/eval/claude` (V1.4 step 7) | CLI | register a Claude eval `{root, preset, sensitivity, fraud_only, classifier_model?, actor_model?, batch}` → its state; GET `/v1/eval/runs` adds it as `claude` (OD-288) |
| POST | `/v1/eval/next`, `/v1/eval/results` (V1.4 step 7) | MCP-W | `eval_next {limit}` claims cases; `eval_results` → progress and metrics only; `/v1/claims/{id}/…` serve an eval case's reference too (OD-287) |
| GET · POST | `/v1/models` · `/v1/models/install` · `/v1/models/prune` (V1.3) | CLI | removed in v3.0.0 (ADR 0031); `GET /v1/models` answers 404 |
| GET | `/v1/models/claude` (v3.0.0) | CLI | → `{claude, watch}`: the pinned Claude models and the model watch, for `ecf models status` |
| POST | `/v1/models/watch` | CLI | → the model watch's status after running it now, for `ecf models watch` |
| POST | `/v1/models/claude-override` (V1.4) | CLI | `{value, nonce_id?}` → the override, for `ecf settings set claude_model_override` (step-up, §7.5) |
| POST | `/v1/models/keys/anthropic` · `/v1/models/keys/typesafe` (v3.0.0 step 2a, OD-503) · `/v1/models/keys/mistral` (OD-540) | CLI | `{key}` or `{clear: true}` → the key checked (prefix, characters), validated by one call within 5 s, stored, audited and a Security Notice posted (§7.6); never on MCP |
| GET | `/v1/stats` (V1.3) | CLI | `since, address_id?, preset?` → model-call figures (§13.4; Gemma's until v3.0.0, Jev's for a D address, held back, OD-516). From v3.0.0 step 5: `since` a UTC time (`hours` from older clients), a `slack` block without `address_id`; `stages=1` → stage times instead |
| GET | `/v1/addresses/{id}/gate` (V1.3) | CLI | → the go-live gate's checks for the pinned digest (§9.3) |
| POST | `/v1/statusline` | status-line script (WORK token) | `{five_hour, seven_day, five_hour_resets_at, seven_day_resets_at}` (the session is the token's) → `{recorded, eval?}`; `eval` is an open Claude eval run's progress, counts only (V1.4 step 6; `eval` v2.2.0) |
| GET | `/v1/health` | any | → `{ok}` (no data) |
| POST | `/v1/corpus/preflight` | CLI | the fetch request (`address` or `email`, `host`, `app_password`; `owner_email`; `out` and limits) → resolved folder, size, estimates; refused on `ecf-server dev` (§16.7) |
| POST | `/v1/corpus/fetch` | CLI | the same plus `expect_folder`, `nonce_id`, `passphrase?` → step-up first (`corpus_fetch`), then the run starts; the generated passphrase is in this answer only |
| GET | `/v1/corpus` | CLI | none → the run's state and counts (never the passphrase) |
| POST | `/v1/corpus/stop` | CLI | none → stops the run; what was fetched is written, marked incomplete |
| POST | `/v1/corpus/info` | CLI | `path` → the file's clear header (unverified) and the labels count |
| POST | `/v1/corpus/session` | CLI | `path`, `passphrase` → opens one decrypted corpus (one at a time; the passphrase isn't kept) → `session_id`, `corpus_id`, count, header |
| GET | `/v1/corpus/session/{id}/keys` | CLI | → each message's index and label key |
| GET | `/v1/corpus/session/{id}/items/{index}` | CLI | → one message for the label screen: display headers, attachment names, a few facts, keyword hits, the stored excerpt redacted and not; never model output |
| DELETE | `/v1/corpus/session/{id}` | CLI | `stop?` → releases the session; refused while an eval run uses it unless `stop=1`, which stops the run after its case. A session idle for 15 minutes is dropped at the next tick |
| POST | `/v1/corpus/merge` | CLI | `sources` [{path, passphrase}], `out`, `allow_mixed`, `passphrase?`, `nonce_id?` → step-up (`corpus_merge`, bound to the files' sha256s and `out`) before any decrypt, then a new corpus; refused on `ecf-server dev` |

**As built through V1.2** (review 2026-09-30; code: `ecf_server/api.py` and the route modules): the service accepts two callers, the CLI token and a WORK session token (`/v1/sessions`, V1.0); OBSERVE arrives with the MCP server in V1.4, so `/v1/status` and `/v1/counts` answer CLI and MCP-W only for now, and no CLI command calls `/v1/counts` yet (it is for MCP). Not yet built: `/v1/addresses/{id}/outbound` (V1.5), `/v1/secrets/{name}` (app passwords go through `/v1/addresses`), `/v1/export`, `/v1/import`, `/v1/restore` (V1.5), `/v1/eval/runs/{id}/…` and `/v1/statusline` (V1.4). **Added in V1.4** (step 3): OBSERVE (no token: `/v1/status`, `/v1/counts`; OD-280), `/v1/review-queue` and `/v1/claims/…` (WORK only); (step 6) `/v1/statusline` (WORK only), the telemetry fields of `/v1/sessions`, `claude` in `/v1/status` (the last review, for `doctor`) and in `/v1/stats`. **Added in V1.3:** `/v1/models`, `/v1/models/install`, `/v1/stats`, `/v1/eval/runs` (start, status) and `/v1/eval/runs/stop`, `/v1/addresses/{id}/gate`, all CLI only. `ecf-server dev` alone also serves `/v1/dev/clock` (GET, POST: read or move the fake clock) and `/v1/dev/chat/posts` (GET, DELETE: the fake Slack's recorded posts); a production service answers `not_found`. **v3.0.0 step 2a** (OD-503, P19): `/v1/models/api-key` is removed in v3.0.0; a v2.2.x client's `ecf models api-key` is refused, and the v3 CLI refuses an older service. No `api_version` bump.

The API carries an integer `api_version`; the server accepts clients at N and N-1.

### 15.2 Audit log events

JSON lines, one object per event: `ts`, `event`, `install`, `address_id?`, `stable_id?`, `actor` (`service`, `os_user`, `slack:<member>`, `mcp:<session>`), `outcome` (`ok`, `denied`, `error`), `data` (event-specific, no email content). Event families: `check.*` (started, completed, deferred, lease_skipped), `item.*` (created, classified, proposed, transitioned, stale), `action.*` (granted, executed, failed, undone), `approval.*`, `stepup.*` (requested, verified, refused), `answer.*`, `config.*` (applied, rejected), `stage.*`, `sensitivity.*`, `outbound.*`, `send.*`, `slack.*` (posted, click_refused), `alert.*`, `model.*` (refused, retired), `export.*` (requested, completed, failed), `import.*` (requested, validated, completed, failed), `restore.*`, `upgrade.*`, `service.*` (started, stopped, crash, breaker), `secret.*` (written, locked_wait), `address.*` (added, removed, retry; OD-191), `mailbox.reset`, `item.duplicate_delivery`, `precheck.decided`, `action.failed`. **Added in V1.2** (V1.2 review, 2026-09-30; names as written by the code): `action.outcome_unknown`, `action.undo_requested`; `item.resolved`, `item.requeued`, `item.stale`, `item.excerpt_shown`; `approval.*` (requested, queued, approved, rejected, expired, reoffered); `answer.*` (queued, recorded, expired); `stepup.*` (requested, verified, consumed, refused); `send.cancelled`; `address.paused`, `address.resumed`; `stage.changed`, `sensitivity.changed`, `settings.changed`, `sender.*` (confirmed, reply_to_set, verified_set), `retention.*` (changed, run), `backfill.*` (started, finished), `alerts.set`, `alert.*` (opened, resolved), `security.notice`, `init.role_set`; `slack.*` (app_created, installed, tokens_replaced, member_confirm_sent, member_confirmed, reauthorized, channel_recorded, channel_gone, channel_archived, click_refused, click_unknown, click_failed, disconnected, reconnected). **Added in V1.3** (names as written by the code): `policy.decided` (rule, source, actions, dropped), `model.item_failed`, `model.item_retried`, `models.installed`, `review.recorded`, `approval.batch`, `eval.completed`, `ollama_log.rotated` (V1.3.1); `stage.changed` gains the gate's result, any override and the held choice. **Added in V1.5** (steps 8 and 9, names as written by the code): `export.key_rotated`, `export.dir_set` (without the path), `export.completed` (kind `scheduled` or `manual`), `export.failed`, `secret.regranted`, `import.completed`, `restore.completed`, `upgrade.completed`, `upgrade.settled`, `destroy.started`, `destroy.completed` (step 12a; lost with the database, OD-386); imported audit rows carry `origin`, the source install's ID. Service start, stop, watchdog and breaker events go to the service log, not the audit table. `export.*` and `import.*` events also carry: person (the OS user), client version, time, scope, counts, bundle SHA-256, data-format version and duration; imports add source install, account and export time (plan §13). **In V1.1** (V1.1 build, 2026-09-29; code: `ecf_server/audit.py`): events are written to the `audit` table in the transaction that makes the change; on every tick, and at shutdown, new rows are copied in id order to `<data>/audit/<address_id or _install>/YYYY/MM/DD.jsonl` (folders 0700, files 0600, each line with its row `id`), and a high-water mark in `settings` advances after each batch, so a crash can only repeat the last batch's lines, which carry the same `id`. `ecf logs [--address] [--event <prefix>] [--since <time or 30m, 2h, 3d>] [--until …] [--limit N] [--follow]` reads the table through `GET /v1/logs` (`--since` and `--until` through the range parser from v3.0.0 step 5, §10.2). A test checks that a processed fraud email's subject, body text and sender address never reach the files. Mapping from the early design's activity log (`docs/history/LOCAL-EMAIL-PROCESSING.md` §5a): `dry_run` → stage `shadow` / status `observed`; `classification_source` → `decision_source`; `action_executed` + `error` → `executed` / `failed` / `failed_unknown`.

**Added in v3.0.0 step 2a** (OD-503; never the key): `models.api_key_set` gains `replaced`; `models.jev_key_set` (`replaced`) and `models.jev_key_cleared` (`had`); each set, replace or removal also writes `security.notice`.

Corpus (OD-466; built 2026-10-07): `corpus.fetched` with counts, bytes, order, whether complete and why it stopped, `corpus_id`, the file's sha256 and the source as an `address_id` or, for a one-off source, `sha256` of the folded email (12 hex) plus its domain; never the email or the path.
